author: By Clint Combs, Contributor
title: ICE Agent Falsely Accused Federal Defender of Helping Client Evade Arrest and Deportation
content:
Minneapolis, MN — It was supposed to be another routine court appearance.


Assistant Federal Defender Michael Deates and his Salvadoran client settled inside the Minneapolis courtroom on April 28. ICE Deportation Officer Michael O’Neal sat inside the gallery when he heard a familiar name: Ezequiel Portillo-Rodriguez.


He pulled out his government phone and then searched for the name. A Certificate of Nonexistence (CTNE) that he filed in April 2025 popped up. To O’Neal, this meant that there were no official records of Portillo-Rodriguez ever holding a visa, green card or U.S. citizenship. He texted agent Blake Willwerscheid, asking if he knew about the case. Willwersheid told him that Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) Special Agent Brubaker was in charge of the case. A prosecutor later testified that this HSI Agent thought he was talking to an agent Witt in St. Paul.


Had O’Neal looked through court records he would have found something more relevant than a CTNE. On Sept. 2, 2025, Portillo-Rodriguez started his six-month stint inside the notorious Golden State Annex in McFarland, Ca. He filed an asylum claim while inside the private immigration jail run by GEO Group. Attorneys wrote that Portillo-Rodriguez had a “fear of persecution and torture” if he were deported back to El Salvador. Two weeks later an asylum officer denied this claim.


An immigration judge overturned that denial on November 7, 2025, finding his fears credible.


Portillo-Rodriguez filed a habeas corpus petition on Jan. 26, 2026. His attorney Deborah Czuba filed an emergency motion for a temporary restraining order on March 12. Four days later the government decided not to contest the review.


In California, U.S. District Judge Dale Drozd declared that the government had violated Portillo-Rodriguez’s Fifth Amendment Due Process rights by subjecting him to indefinite detention without a proper hearing.


On March 18, Judge Drozd issued an injunction releasing Portillo-Rodriguez and barring ICE from re-arresting him on immigration charges.


A month later, O’Neal was texting his boss, Supervisory Detention and Deportation Officer Nicholas Carey, looking for a green light to arrest Portillo-Rodriguez. He got no response while court was in session. Once the hearing adjourned, O’Neal cornered the prosecuting attorneys, asking if this was a case where Enforcement and Removal Operations (ERO) was barred from placing a detainer. The prosecutors told him they didn’t know.


O’Neal then approached U.S. Deputy Marshal Cassandra Stone, telling her he planned to take Portillo-Rodriguez into custody. Stone told him an arrest could be made at the U.S. Probation and Pretrial Services office. O’Neal claimed that Deates was standing close enough to eavesdrop.


“Deates was listening to the conversation I was having with Deputy Marshal Stone, made eye contact with me, then told his client Portillo-Rodriguez they needed to leave and follow him downstairs,” O’Neal wrote.


Deates denied this in his sworn declaration.


“I did not overhear, and had no knowledge at the time of, any conversation,” he wrote.


Deates and Portillo-Rodriguez walked downstairs to eat lunch at the Federal Defender’s Office. O’Neal rushed to the courthouse cellblock. He called Carey, demanding an immediate administrative warrant. Minutes later, Carey emailed a signed Form I-200 straight to O’Neal’s inbox.


The plainclothes task force scrambled to spring a familiar trap. O’Neal left the courtroom with Deputy Marshals Cassandra Stone and Gnika. Stone went to the Marshals Office to scan the live security video feeds, spotting Deates and his client in the public lobby.


By the time O’Neal and the marshals rushed down to the ground floor, the lobby was empty. The marshals searched the interior corridors while O’Neal glanced out a window. He caught sight of the pair walking along the sidewalk next to Minneapolis City Hall toward the light rail platform.


The three rushed outside before a red light stopped them at the intersection of 3rd Avenue and 4th Street. The light turned green. Trains departed in both directions. O’Neal saw Deates standing alone on the light rail platform. Portillo-Rodriguez was on his way back home to California.


After the failed trap, O’Neal contacted Special Agent Brubaker for an update. Brubaker informed him that Portillo-Rodriguez had been released in California on a habeas corpus petition.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: La derrota del trumpismo: ¿un canto de cisne o un cisne negro?
content:
LA DERROTA DEL TRUMPISMO: ¿UN

CANTO DE CISNE

 O UN

CISNE NEGRO

?


Por Rafael Bautista S.


Mientras el futuro más temible llegue,


lo único que nos devuelva la luz será


esta velita prendida que supimos


cuidar en plena oscuridad.


Ya con la cabeza fría, conviene profundizar analítica y prospectivamente lo que se ha de jugar en estos casi dos meses de transición hacia las más temibles opciones que se pondrán en movimiento, una vez que el Estado profundo ha decidido prescindir del episodio Trump. Por cuestiones de sobrevivencia discordante –como ya señalamos– entre dos opciones supremacistas de restauración del liderazgo imperial

[1]

, la derrota de Trump no limpia el panorama sino lo enrarece aún más.


Todos saben que los demócratas son rusóbos, para empezar, y eso no augura un cese de la amenaza nuclear sino la radicaliza, como ya se está observando en los últimos movimientos beligerantes de la OTAN, Inglaterra y Alemania

[2]

 contra Rusia. El AIPAC, por cuestiones ya de sobrevivencia del Estado sionista, más aún cuando perdió Netanyahu, hará uso de su fuerte influencia entre los demócratas

[3]

 para continuar la política nuclear contra Irán y el exterminio de los gazatíes y los palestinos en general (Líbano, Siria y Cisjordania). Lo cual, además de la prolongación del genocidio palestino, no hace sino continuar, por otros medios, la política expansiva (aunque cada vez menos posible, como la inutilidad de los bombardeos recientes de parte de USA e Israel a Irán) del Estado sionista.


Tampoco los inmigrantes verán otro panorama más alentador con los demócratas, cuando fue la administración “demócrata” de Obama, por ejemplo, la que más cantidad de deportados produjo. De boca para afuera, los demócratas harán de Trump el chivo expiatorio que necesita la restauración imperial para justificar su continuidad. Creyendo que la limpieza de la imagen imperial podrá ofrecerle demagógicamente al mundo, otra cosa que no sea una nueva versión de la continuidad de “un mundo basado en reglas” para los demás y excepciones para el Imperio.


En ese contexto, pondremos a consideración el panorama que sugiere Alexander Dugin y nuestro comentario a lo que creemos, una de las descripciones más cercanas a lo que se viene. En sus propias palabras

[4]

, si Trump pierde irremediablemente el control del Congreso: “la venganza de los demócratas contra Trump y sus seguidores

no se parecerá a nada de lo que hemos visto antes

”. Los demócratas no pasarán por alto, lo que significó el desmantelamiento de los brazos administrativos y operativos de su poder de influencia nacional y global, cuando se creó la Oficina de Eficiencia Gubernamental, el DOGE, y se inició la desarticulación de la Agencia de los Estados Unidos para el Desarrollo Internacional, la USAID (desde donde se operó la restauración derechista –una vez desarticulada por la “primavera democrática”– en Latinoamérica, en favor de la tutela demócrata gringa). Esa era una de las vías que permitió la injerencia de los intereses que representa, por ejemplo, George Soros. Por eso, no es casual la sincronía de la ola de protestas en Europa

[5]

 y el triunfo demócrata en USA. Hasta el triunfo de Lula se explicaría, en parte, por esa caída de las piezas de dominó que sostenía al trumpismo, a nivel global (rival en la jefatura de un nuevo orden mundial que destaca otro tipo de intereses, sobre todo financieros, que tienen en Soros un actor reconocible).


Dugin, en tono de socarrón señala: “realmente creyeron que Trump cumpliría sus promesas y que el Estado profundo estaba a punto de ser erradicado de raíz”. Pero Trump, que nunca generó el contexto para la realización del golpe definitivo, ahora tiene, en el Congreso (tanto en diputados como en senadores, además de gobernadores), la mayoría necesaria para que el globalismo, que intentó atacar, reorganice filas con sus portavoces y comiencen el contraataque.


Ya algunos analistas en geopolítica preguntan si quien ganó en las “midterm” fue, en realidad, Soros. Pero éste es sólo el actor expuesto y si algo manifiesta el

poder duro

 es la no exposición. Éste

poder duro

 (o Estado profundo) actúa creando la objetividad que se constituye en escenario, una vez que ya ha mudado a otro tipo de realidad, teniendo a todos ocupados en el escenario conveniente que el poder produce para desplegar mediáticamente conspiraciones para el disfrute masoquista del morbo político. Con esos fines se viene activando la alerta, en 33 países …

author: Unknown
title: Saki: Turkish citizens top the list of deportations from Europe
content:
Deportations across Europe have accelerated following the implementation of the new Pact on Migration and Asylum. These measures have begun to affect not only undocumented migrants but also asylum seekers and political refugees who have been granted asylum.


The adoption of the pact has been followed by an increase in deportation orders targeting Kurdish refugees in particular. Numerous Kurdish political refugees have begun to be returned to Turkey from the European countries where they reside. Refugees, including politicians, poets and writers, face trials carrying potential prison sentences of several decades under cases brought against them after their return to Turkey.


Peoples' Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party) MP Özgül Saki spoke to ANF about recent developments affecting migrants in Europe and the growing number of deportation orders.


'The price of the crisis is poverty, massacres and displacement'


Özgül Saki said that pressure on refugees had intensified following the implementation of the new Pact on Migration and Asylum on 12 June 2026. She added said: "Following its entry into force on 12 June, the Council of the European Union (EU) formally adopted a new regulation known as the Return Regulation on 1 October 2026, aimed at accelerating the deportation and return of irregular migrants who have no legal right to remain.


We must first recognize that since 2013, we have been witnessing mass migration on a scale unprecedented in previous periods. The period of conflict that began with ISIS attacks in Syria and Iraq, Israel's genocidal policies against Palestine, the escalation of tensions between Ukraine and Russia into a prolonged war, the Taliban's return to power in Afghanistan and US attacks on Iran have displaced millions of people. In my view, the underlying cause is the imperialist capitalist system's continued reliance on war as a regional strategy to resolve its own crises. The price of this crisis continues to be paid by the peoples of the region through poverty, massacres and displacement.


We are witnessing the re-emergence of colonial reflexes. Efforts to remain protected within Europe's own borders are proceeding alongside expansionist ambitions beyond them. Concepts described as 'European values,' such as human rights, democracy and equality, have lost their meaning. We are confronted with a Europe dominated by governments that regard everything as permissible in the name of 'security' and 'defense,' are turning toward fascism and envision a white Europe.


There is a widespread expectation that migration statistics will increasingly be used as a political tool, particularly amid the rise of the far right in Germany, the Netherlands and France. The prominence of 'returns,' 'border security' and 'irregular migration' in election campaigns indicates that this right-wing and fascistic trajectory will continue. As a result, a deliberate anti-migrant political agenda is being implemented through new, multilayered mechanisms of pressure on refugees."


'Restrictions begin at the border'


Özgül Saki said that, according to the Council of the European Union, the regulation adopted on 1 October expands member states' powers to carry out deportations.


Saki continued: "We have already begun to see the serious consequences of the new legislation in recent months. The coming period will bring highly unfavorable conditions both for migrants already living in European countries and for those seeking to apply for asylum.


The Council of the European Union stated that the new rules adopted on 1 October will complement the Pact on Migration and Asylum and contribute to its implementation. The regulation gives member states greater scope to carry out returns and allows for the establishment of 'return hubs' in countries outside the EU. This means that people who have been issued return decisions and are deemed to have no right to remain in the EU may be transferred to these centers under agreements or arrangements concluded with the relevant non-EU countries


Eurostat figures and recent EU data show that asylum applications across the EU have declined by approximately 24 percent. However, this decline has been achieved by deliberately making the application requirements more complicated from the outset. author: Sicilia Libertaria
title: La politica tra piazze e maranza
content:
Mobilitazioni e decreti.


La classe politica italiana (ma si potrebbe benissimo estendere in generale alla classe politica europea, per tacere ad esempio di Trump) mostra tutta la sua incapacità a comprendere le gravi falle che il sistema capitalistico ha provocato nella società oppure, che forse è più vicino al vero, la sua pervicace volontà a mantenere a tutti i costi il sistema esistente.


Lo scatenamento dei più tremendi spiriti animali del capitalismo e del sistema politico mondiale degli ultimi anni si traduce in guerre, instabilità economica, crisi sociali, peggioramento progressivo delle condizioni di vita delle classi sfruttate. La risposta da parte delle classi dirigenti è ovunque la repressione, la criminalizzazione delle mobilitazioni che la società esprime, il fomentare l’odio sociale e l’anestetizzare l’opinione pubblica con opportuni diversivi.


Quanto sta accadendo in queste settimane in Italia è la perfetta fotografia di questo stato delle cose. Le piazze piene di una protesta spontanea e incontenibile, animata principalmente da giovanissimi e studenti, i blocchi e le manifestazioni promossi da agricoltori ed autotrasportatori contro il caro carburanti e il carovita, in particolare al Sud, hanno provocato nel governo una reazione che qualcuno ha definito infantile-adolescenziale, definizione corretta se vivessimo in un mondo giusto ma così non è, e che si è tradotta nell’ennesimo decreto sicurezza e nell’introduzione nel codice penale dell’ennesimo reato, con cui si tenta di imbrigliare le proteste degli ultimi anni. Questo per quanto riguarda in prima istanza i cosiddetti maranza, termine comodo per liquidare la profonda insoddisfazione che investe il mondo giovanile, mentre nei confronti di autotrasportatori e agricoltori i fascisti al governo hanno fatto ricorso al più classico dei metodi: il bastone e la carota. Dapprima sono state mandate le forze dell’ordine per identificare camionisti e agricoltori che bloccavano le strade, il giorno successivo è stato varato un decreto che distribuisce briciole per sedare momentaneamente la protesta.


Dall’altra parte, l’opposizione parlamentare rappresentata dal centro sinistra non ha saputo neppure cavalcare la protesta, anche solo per mettere in difficoltà un governo in palese affanno che pur vuole battere alle prossime elezioni politiche. Senza considerare l’incredibile presidio milanese convocato dalla Cgil e dal Pd per dire no alla violenza, in generale leader ed esponenti del “campo largo” si sono limitati a criticare il governo per i provvedimenti presi, precisando che alla repressione dei comportamenti violenti vanno affiancate politiche sociali che affrontino il malessere giovanile e diano una risposta al carovita e alla crisi di salari e retribuzioni. Senza peraltro entrare nel merito delle questioni, tutto chiuso in un linguaggio ormai logoro e stereotipato, rappresentazione di un teatrino veramente distante dalle questioni sociali e dalla gravità della crisi che ci attanaglia. A cosa servono dichiarazioni di principio, prese di posizioni, manifestazioni di solidarietà, quando va bene, se tutto ciò rimane un flatus vocis, buono per i media e per animare uno sterile dibattito?


Il governo della destra fascista, o delle destre destre, come preferiscono definirlo i benpensanti convinti così di poter continuare ad alimentare il mito della destra liberale e ragionevole, che tanto ragionevole nella sua storia non è stata quando si è trattato di difendere l’ordine costituito, esprime al meglio la sua idea di società gerarchizzata, ordinata, controllata e prona al volere dei potenti. Naturalmente la maschera democratica viene adattata al caso. Quindi se la destra fa quello che ha sempre fatto, qualche interrogativo potrebbe suscitarlo quella parte politica che continua a definirsi sinistra (tolto l’alibi del centro). Pierluigi Bersani, uno degli esponenti più in vista di quella “sinistra” che si è fatta investire dalla furia neoliberista, ha sostenuto in un noto programma televisivo che di fronte alla gravità della crisi mondiale in atto occorrono risposte radicali. Non ha poi chiarito in cosa consistano e soprattutto come dovrebbero attuarsi queste decisioni radicali, tuttavia ha ragione. Eppure le menti più illuminate della sinistra italiana, come Bersani, continuano a pensare che correttivi al capitalismo cosiddetto selvaggio e un nuovo protagonismo statale siano sufficienti a ridare vita ad un rinnovato patto sociale di stampo socialdemocratico …

author: Marina Amaral
title: Por que a sustentabilidade é o “mito do capitalismo”?
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a Newsletter da Pública, enviada sempre às sextas-feiras, 8h. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


“Eu digo que sustentabilidade é um mito corporativo, quer dizer, é um mito que foi criado pelas corporações, pelo capitalismo, para iludir as pessoas com a ideia de que a natureza é infinita, de que a gente pode continuar furando petróleo, sujando oceanos”, disse Ailton Krenak em uma entrevista para vestibulandos, em 2025, quando a Unicamp incorporou o livro “A vida não é útil” na lista de leituras obrigatórias.


Lembrei da frase ao pensar na COP31, que acontece nesta semana na Turquia, e recebeu o presidente Lula em clima de festa. Não apenas por sua reeleição, que mantém o Brasil entre as lideranças do debate climático, mas também por manter a principal proposição de Belém com a apresentação do mapa do caminho para o fim do uso dos combustíveis fósseis bem como de resultados positivos de seu governo, destacando-se a queda do desmatamento (sobre a expectativas para a COP leia a

coluna

 de ontem de Gustavo Faleiros e ouça o

episódio

 desta semana no Bom Dia, Fim do Mundo).


Ainda assim, como todos sabemos, Lula não vai abrir mão de explorar petróleo na Margem Equatorial, onde o poço Morphus, na bacia da Foz do Amazonas, já obteve três amostras positivas anunciadas pela Petrobras. E não apenas ele: dez anos depois do Acordo de Paris nem os países que são grandes produtores nem os que são grandes consumidores de gás, petróleo e carvão agiram de forma decisiva nessa direção – o consumo só ficou um pouco abaixo este ano por causa da guerra no Irã.


Mas como sociedade continuamos distantes do debate climático, apesar de cientistas, ambientalistas e lideranças indígenas brasileiras engajadas na questão.  Como diz o pensador Krenak, “estamos jogados em um abismo cognitivo”, que nos impede de perceber o colapso não apenas climático (o que já é muito), mas ecológico, com velocidade e dimensões ainda subestimadas pelos países e pelas populações.


E a disparidade de consumo tem um papel determinante nessa escalada para o caos, embora passe ao largo da maioria das discussões. Mais do que isso: empresas, governos e corporações fazem de tudo para ninguém pensar no assunto e continuar trocando de smartphone todo ano sem culpa – um único aparelho chega a consumir 200 kg de matéria-prima obtida com mineração de acordo com a plataforma

Mine my phone

.


Há outra razão ainda mais delicada para se esquivar dessa discussão. O estímulo ao consumo que é a mola propulsora desse modelo só funciona por causa da desigualdade social crescente. Imagine se todos tivessem a mesma possibilidade de compra: o mundo já teria acabado. Em vez disso, os preços sobem, excluindo os 90% mais pobres, enquanto se venera o luxo e a opulência nas redes sociais.


Como disse a filósofa Deborah Danowski em uma inesquecível entrevista ainda durante a pandemia: “Não há mais mundo para todo mundo.


O segredo mais guardado é que vivemos tempos de escassez que acompanham a guerra, o colapso climático, social e ecológico (típico cenário dos futuros distópicos). A redução na oferta, que afeta especialmente os alimentos, sensíveis às mudanças climáticas, e de energia (que afeta todos os preços e é a razão principal para o aquecimento do planeta), faz subir os preços, o que se agrava com a maior frequência de eventos extremos, ou mesmo pela alteração persistente de condições climáticas nas regiões de lavoura, como é o caso o café. E isso só tende a piorar.


Esse é um dos motivos que impediu o cumprimento da promessa simbólica de picanha e cerveja nesse governo Lula, que teve como flanco mais frágil o aumento de custo de vida. O presidente até tentou explicar que o preço dos alimentos — o mais essencial — vinha subindo desde os governos anteriores, mas o fato é que uma quantidade cada vez maior de pessoas sente a defasagem entre o que ganham, precisam e desejam. Veja as centenas de milhares de manifestantes na França, em um movimento que começou com estudantes pedindo investimento no ensino e se expandiu para uma multidão multifacetada reivindicando melhores condições de vida.


A desigualdade é a pedra fundamental para o mundo seguir nesse “abismo cognitivo” na definição de Ailton e se manter indiferente à emergência que vivemos. Basta lembrar que a crise energética mundial ocorre pelo aumento da demanda em um mundo em que 700 milhões de pessoas vivem sem luz. O justo …

author: Unknown
title: Karşıyaka Emek ve Demokrasi Platformu: İşçilerin canı sermayeye kurban edilemez
content:
Karşıya Emek Demokrasi Platformu, Aliağa’daki HABAŞ Demir Çelik fabrikasında meydana gelen ve 19 işçinin yaşamına neden olan patlamaya karşı basın açıklaması gerçekleştirdi. Açıklamaya, Emek Partisi (EMEP), Türkiye İşçi Partisi (TİP), Halkların Eşitlik ve Demokrasi Partisi (DEM Parti) ve Toplumsal Özgürlük Partisi(TÖP) katıldı. İzban önünde toplanan kitle, çarşı içinde yürüyüş gerçekleşti. Yürüyüşte, “Kaza değil katliam”, “İşyerinde ölmek istemiyoruz”, “Katil patron hesap verecek” sloganları atıldı.

İş cinayetlerinin bugüne kadar “kaza”, “fıtrat” ya da “kader” diye normalleştirilmeye çalışıldığı vurgulanan açıklamada “Madenlerde, inşaatlarda, fabrikalarda yaşanan ölümler, işçilerin yaşamının sermayenin kâr hırsı karşısında nasıl hiçe sayıldığını göstermektedir. Patlamanın meydana geldiği fabrikada daha önce de ölümlü ve ağır yaralanmalı iş kazaları yaşanmıştır. Son iki ay içinde biri 20, diğeri 55 yaşında iki işçinin yaşamını yitirmesi, çalışma koşullarının ne kadar tehlikeli olduğunu ortaya koymuştur. Buna rağmen tesis, eskiyen altyapısı, yıpranmış üretim teknolojisi ve yetersiz güvenlik önlemleriyle adeta patlamaya hazır bir bomba gibi çalıştırılmaya devam edilmiştir” denildi.

Her ölümün ardından hiçbir şey olmamış gibi üretime devam edildiği hatırlatılan açıklamada, “Bu kitlesel iş cinayetinin sorumluları yalnızca işçi sağlığını ve iş güvenliğini hiçe sayan fabrika sahipleri ve yöneticileri değildir. Denetimleri kâğıt üzerinde bırakan, eksiklikleri görmezden gelen, işçilerin yaşamını tehdit eden çalışma koşullarına göz yuman kamu kurumları ve yetkilileri de sorumluluk taşımaktadır. Yıllardır işçilerin insanca çalışma ve yaşama taleplerine kulak tıkayan, ağır ve güvencesiz çalışma koşullarını görmezden gelen, emekçilerin hakları yerine sermayenin çıkarlarını önceleyen siyasi iktidar da iş cinayetlerinin siyasi sorumluluğunu taşımaktadır. İşçi sağlığı ve iş güvenliğini güvence altına almak yerine sermayenin kârını korumayı esas alan, etkili denetim mekanizmalarını işletmeyen ve cezasızlığın önüne geçmeyen politikalar, benzer acıların tekrar tekrar yaşanmasına zemin hazırlamaktadır” ifadelerine yer verildi.

Açıklamada son olarak şu ifadeler kullanıldı:

“Bu katliam, emeği değersizleştiren, işçi sağlığını maliyet unsuru olarak gören ve kârı insan yaşamının önüne koyan sömürü düzeninin sonucudur. İş cinayetleri ne kaderdir ne de kaçınılmazdır! İş cinayetleri politiktir. Bu nedenle olayın bütün yönleriyle açığa çıkarılması, ihmali ve sorumluluğu bulunan fabrika sahiplerinden yöneticilere, denetim görevini yerine getirmeyen kamu yetkililerine kadar herkesin yargı önünde hesap vermesi sağlanmalıdır. Karşıyaka Emek ve Demokrasi Platformu olarak işçilerin ve tüm emekçilerin yaşam hakkını, sağlıklı, güvenli ve güvenceli koşullarda çalışma hakkını savunmaya; iş cinayetlerine, sömürüye, güvencesizliğe ve denetimsizliğe karşı ortak mücadeleyi büyütmeye devam edeceğiz.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Unknown
title: Çiğdem Doğu: Young people no longer accept the life imposed by capitalism
content:
Kurdistan Women's Communities (KJK) Executive Council member Çiğdem Doğu appeared on a special program broadcast by Medya Haber television, where she discussed the Peace and Democratic Society Process initiated by Leader Apo (Abdullah Öcalan) and violence against women.


The first part of this in-depth interview can be read

here

.


Looking beyond the Middle East region to world politics, Trump has not fallen, but he has become increasingly surrounded. Democrats and Republicans have clashed, and electoral balances have shifted. Meanwhile, youth-led resistance and uprisings are taking place in Spain, France and Italy. How should we interpret these developments? What direction are these changing balances giving to the broader process?


There was also an election in Brazil, where Lula won. He represents a more democratic and somewhat more left-leaning position. There was also an election in Serbia. This was a very important experience. A candidate list was formed under the leadership of the student youth movement. The students themselves were not on the list, but they supported democratic and honest politicians whom they believed in. That list won. This provides a very important indication for evaluating certain developments.


There was also a recent election in the United States. We cannot simply conclude that the peoples won or that the Democrats won in a broader democratic sense. But certain signals emerged, and it is important to evaluate them. We all know Trump. The peoples of the world know him. He emerged as a model of imperial leadership. He was perhaps the clearest example of the type described by the Kurdish People's Leader in the manifesto as a "murderous, hierarchical" personality. He disregarded everyone and paid no attention whatsoever to the peoples.


This tendency already exists within the capitalist system. At least when nation-states first emerged, there was a legal system, even if it was never fully implemented. Trump and leaders like him, however, adopted an approach that recognized no legal, moral or ethical boundaries. They put this approach into practice. People speak of a Third World War as though it has yet to begin, but it has already begun. Trump was one of those leading it. He waged war against Iran. There are other wars taking place around the world. He claims to have resolved numerous conflicts, but in reality, he played a role in provoking and escalating wars. Naturally, this has produced social, economic and humanitarian consequences. The American people have also paid a price for these policies. In this sense, the American public delivered a response, saying that such leadership could not continue and that one person could not govern in this manner.


I want my words to be understood correctly. We are people who hold a socialist ideology. Our standards and expectations are therefore much higher. Nevertheless, peoples send messages through elections. It is very important to understand the sociological dynamics behind these developments and interpret what elections reveal. This does not mean that powerful socialist movements have emerged or that the Democrats are necessarily better simply because they won. Such a comparison would not be accurate or objective. What matters is understanding what the people are saying. From this perspective, the American public has delivered a response. The message was that the escalation of wars, the refusal to recognize the will of peoples and the unilateral decisions affecting the Palestinian people and the peoples of the Middle East were not accepted. It is important to recognize this as a positive message.


'

Young people no longer accept the life imposed by capitalism'


Why is this important? Because perceptions are also being manufactured. We frequently hear claims that "the right is advancing" or "the far right is on the rise." This is also a form of psychological warfare. We must evaluate everything sociologically. We need to carefully analyze what social tendencies are telling us and what realities they express. We are leading figures within a socialist movement, and we must therefore approach these developments through sociological analysis.


The example of Brazil is important in this respect. The student movement in Serbia generated significant mobilization, struggle and rebellion. Youth movements have also become increasingly active in Paris and other French cities, as well as in Italy, Germany and various other countries. These …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: Estados Unidos: Apostillas electorales
content:
Zohran Mamdani, alcalde de Nueva York, Estados Unidos


Por Mario Hernandez


El alcalde Mamdani disfrutó del triunfo de los cuatro candidatos a los que les dio su apoyo para el Congreso


Entre ellos estaban las integrantes del DSA (Socialistas Democráticos de América) Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier, el ex contralor Brad Lander y la gobernadora Kathy Hochul.


La victoria más contundente de la noche fue la de Chevalier, que se quedó con su distrito en el norte de Manhattan y el Bronx con el 87,5 % de los votos. Su rival, el republicano Jomo Williams, apenas arañó un 12 %. Semejante paliza electoral deja bien en claro que las propuestas de Chevalier, que incluyen impuestos a los ricos, salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE, entre otras demandas progresistas, calan profundo en gran parte de sus nuevos votantes. Su triunfo demuestra además que se puede hacer campaña definiéndose abiertamente como socialista, e incluso enfrentar a la policía en las calles, sin miedo a “espantar a los propios”. De hecho, el tono combativo de Darializa y su ya famoso cruce con la policía el día del tiroteo del ICE en el Bronx sin duda le sumaron un buen caudal de votos.


Chevalier cruzó duro al ICE y remarcó la importancia de la vivienda accesible, vistiendo una kufiyya como símbolo de apoyo a Palestina. De todos modos, sorprendió que su discurso hablara muy poco de política internacional: la única mención a Palestina se dio cuando la tribuna empezó a cantar de forma espontánea “Palestina libre”.


Además de Chevalier, el DSA conquistó una segunda banca por el Distrito 7, donde Valdez, que también contaba con el respaldo de Mamdani, logró un triunfo cómodo con más del 83 % de los votos frente a su rival republicano. Valdez, referente del DSA, va a reemplazar a la congresista del establishment demócrata Nydia Velázquez, que se retira en enero. Al igual que Chevalier, Valdez hizo campaña con propuestas de salud universal, vivienda para todos y la abolición del ICE. Un dato clave: a diferencia de Mamdani, ni Valdez ni Chevalier le dieron su apoyo a la gobernadora Hochul ni dijeron que la iban a votar.


Con esto, el DSA pasa a tener tres bancas en el Congreso por Nueva York: Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Claire Valdez y Darializa Avila Chevalier. Si a eso se le suma el flamante congresista y ex miembro del DSA Brad Lander, a quien Mamdani también apoyó, el alcalde pasa a contar con una bancada importante que representa sus intereses y muchas de sus ideas en el Congreso.


Pero el festejo de Chevalier no fue la única parada de Mamdani esa noche. Antes de subir hacia el Bronx, apenas cerraron las urnas, el alcalde pasó la primera parte de la noche con la gobernadora Kathy Hochul y sus seguidores. En el discurso que dio ahí, Mamdani definió la elección como un “punto de quiebre” para el Partido Demócrata y afirmó que “empezamos el trabajo de transformar a nuestro partido para que vuelva a ser de los trabajadores”.


Su respaldo fue determinante para darle un vuelco a la campaña de Hochul. Hace menos de dos años, parecía que su carrera se había terminado. Todavía golpeada por la ajustada elección de 2022, donde los demócratas de Nueva York perdieron cinco bancas en el Congreso en parte por su incapacidad para movilizar al electorado propio, sus chances de ganar la interna y la reelección parecían bajísimas. Su imagen positiva rozaba apenas el 40 % (al nivel o por debajo de la del presidente Trump), y las encuestas mostraban que un mano a mano en 2026 contra un candidato republicano fuerte podía ser muy parejo.


Pero entonces entró en escena el alcalde Zohran Mamdani. Su meteórico ascenso al poder fue una ola que, al igual que la “ola azul” demócrata, empujó a cuanto candidato llevara la “D” de demócrata en la boleta, y su apoyo temprano y explícito a Hochul le devolvió el aire a la campaña de la gobernadora. Los resultados del martes demostraron la fuerza que tuvo ese espaldarazo. Hochul no solo logró la reelección, sino que aplastó por completo a su rival republicano Bruce Blakeman por más de 20 puntos.


Gran parte de este triunfo se explica por los mismos factores que impulsaron las victorias demócratas en el resto del país: el rechazo a Trump y al Partido Republicano, la bronca con las atrocidades del ICE y la guerra contra Irán, y la frustración por la inflación y el costo de vida. En realidad, el éxito de los demócratas a nivel nacional tuvo más que ver con el odio a Trump que con las propuestas reales de …

author: Unknown
title: Socialist Strategy within the Architecture of Power
content:
The artwork in this dossier, produced by Tricontinental: Institute for Social Research, depicts three forms of power: social power in magenta, governmental power in yellow, and systemic power in cyan. Where these forms overlap, new colours emerge, representing their different configurations and interconnections within a broader architecture of power. This composition invites us to consider how power is organised, contested, and transformed through processes of emancipation.


When a radical government takes office with a mandate for transformation, the next morning it will have to confront banks that remain in private hands, mines under corporate control, private mainstream media, and public administration governed by inherited procedures. Capital can postpone investment, transfer money abroad, close factories, hoard essential goods, dismiss workers, and speculate against the currency. The havoc wrought on the economy and population can then be presented as proof that transformation is impossible, all while the government is held responsible for a crisis produced or intensified by forces beyond its control.


This reality reveals a central problem for socialist strategy. Taking governmental office can be an important step toward systemic transformation, but misunderstanding these two forms of power as one and the same can have dangerous consequences. A clear analysis of where power resides and how its different forms interact is necessary to avoid patterns that have plagued revolutionary processes across the world.


An electoral victory may be mistaken for a revolutionary event when a left-wing party has taken office even though the wider state apparatus, the economy, and the institutions that shape common sense remain largely beyond its control. Conversely, a socialist movement may possess considerable social strength without being able to translate that strength into governmental authority or changes to the structures of the state and economy.  The ruling class exercises power through its control over production and the structures that reinforce it, while the working class exercises collective power through strikes, demonstrations, and the organisations it builds through struggle. To use a single word – power – for all these different capacities can confuse political strategy. In this dossier, we therefore distinguish three related forms of power as an analytical framework for debate and discussion:


Social power

 is the organised capacity of a class or political bloc to act collectively, reproduce material life, and contest the ruling class’s command over society. It is built through institutions of struggle and cooperation such as trade unions, peasant and women’s organisations, cooperatives, community structures, cultural and media projects, political education, and political parties. Through these institutions, a class or political bloc can struggle to reshape common sense and establish moral and intellectual leadership.


Governmental power

 is the capacity to assume governmental authority, whether through elections, insurrection, or another political rupture, and to use executive, legislative, and administrative institutions to pursue a programme. It provides access to important instruments of administration and policy but does not, by itself, amount to control of the state or the wider system.


Systemic power

 is the capacity to transform the class character and institutional form of the state, bring the major means of production and the social surplus under democratic authority, and reorganise the relations through which society reproduces itself. It includes state power but cannot be reduced to it because capitalist social relations are reproduced beyond the formal institutions of the state – through property, finance, the world market, colonial relations, culture, and social reproduction – and many of these relations exceed the reach of any single government or national state.


These forms are analytical distinctions, not sealed compartments, and do not constitute a fixed sequence. They overlap, develop unevenly, and can pull in opposite directions. Governmental power may become a bridge between organised social power and systemic transformation. It may also weaken popular organisation and reconcile it to the existing system. The central strategic question is therefore not which form of power matters but how the three can be connected in a process of emancipation.

On 25 October, the “Student List” won a projected 140 of 250 seats in the Serbian parliament, defeating the ruling party that has been in power for 14 years. The electoral victory comes on the back of a student movement that began on 1 of November 2024, when a newly renovated canopy fell at the railway station in Novi Sad and killed sixteen people. Since then, people in Serbia have organised mass protests and assemblies.

We reached out to Klasna Solidarnost (Class Solirarity), founded in Belgrade in 2016, which grew out of an anarcho-syndicalist movement. Its members continue to participate in student occupations while critiquing electoral strategies. They are also active in antifascism, solidarity with Palestine, antimilitarism, support for workers, and the “Solidarna kuhinja” free kitchen, as well as political analysis and publications.

The mainstream media has presented the student movement as “decentralised” and highlighted the appointing of non-politicians to parliament; is this an accurate reflection of the movement now?

The appointment of non-politicians to parliament is one of the main talking points of the Student List. There were over 160 candidates with PhDs on the list, which was highlighted as a key reason why the new government should be “better” than the old one in which it turned out that even some ministers had fake PhD diplomas. The Student List basically has a technocratic structure and by what we’ve seen so far, it aims to create a “government of experts” which is perfectly in line with the dominant neoliberal ideology that convinces us that the society will be better as a whole if we have experts leading the government.

For us as anarchists, this of course is a fairy tale because we know how technocratic governments ended in countries like Italy and Greece in the last 10-15 years, where they simply ushered in the most brutal neoliberal reforms, bringing down the life standard of the working class even more than their predecessors. And this is actually one of the key elements that show us there probably won’t be much improvement in the working class’s life standard.

During the Student List’s electoral campaign, the focus was on defeating the political mafia regime of the SNS (Serbian Progressive Party), which had been in power for 14 years. The movement focused on the regime’s criminal acts and massive corruption scandals, but it barely mentioned any economic measures to improve the everyday lives of the working class.

Now that the SNS regime is finally gone, it remains to be seen what the economic policy of the new government will be, but from what we’ve heard so far, there isn’t any mention of substantial changes in the economic position of Serbia as a client-state of the European Union, and a partial economic partner of the US, China, and Russia.

How does it compare to former “decentralised” parliamentary movements such as Podemos in Spain?

UN MOUVEMENT QUI A SON HISTOIRE

LES NOUVELLES CLASSES OUVRIERES

V. GRIFFUELHES LE SYNDICALISME REVOLUTIONNAIRE

L’histoire des classes ouvrières, de leur mode de vie, de leur statut, de leur fonction ; celle des poussées ou des explosions de ces mêmes classes ; celle enfin des organisations et des idéologies qui s’efforcent ou affirment en exprimer les volontés, le rôle ou le destin, sont évidemment imbriquées, interdépendantes, mais elles ne sont pas identiques. Cette constatation banale est souvent oubliée dans les polémiques ou les affrontements entre les diverses écoles socialistes.

Chaque fraction a tendance à substituer à la société ouvrière complexe, intégrée dans une société globale en mouvement, une image, ou une formule, dont elle se sert pour construire ses hypothèses, justifier sa politique, tracer ses perspectives. Si bien que les débats se nourrissent de mots ou de schémas, parfois vrais à l’origine, parce que correspondant à un moment ou à un lieu déterminés de la mêlée sociale, mais qui finissent avec le temps, par ne plus être que des pièces de musée. Ce qui fait des discussions une bataille vaine, détachée des réalités, à peine humanisée par la nostalgie des anciens ou le besoin d’exaltation des nouveaux. Et l’extrême érudition finit par brouiller la connaissance des banalités du présent visible.

Même le syndicalisme révolutionnaire - ou syndicalisme libertaire, ou anarcho-syndicalisme - n’échappe pas à cette regrettable pratique. Et pourtant il n’est pas né bien net, défini et définitif. Il n’acquiert ses caractéristiques qu’après avoir passé par une série d’expériences, il est produit de ces expériences, et il ne cessera pas de prendre forme, d’acquérir son langage, de s’enrichir d’idées-forces et de méthodes d’action, d’être partiellement ou totalement absorbé par la société totale.

Dans son travail sur les Bourses du Travail et la C.G.T., publié aux environs de 1910, Paul Delesalle constate et prévoit ces naturelles transformations : « ce qui caractérise le mouvement syndicaliste français, c’est son évolution constante ». Dans une classe ouvrière produite par une société déterminée, les formes d’organisation sont multiples, de même que les idéologies qui habillent ou utilisent ces organisations sont diverses. Le syndicalisme révolutionnaire ne sort pas du cerveau d’un théoricien. Il est pratique qui cherche une doctrine pour se propager et se multiplier.

La variété des situations, des cas, des tentatives, se montre infiniment plus riche que les formulations les plus subtiles. Et tel qui avait raison en une conjoncture précise, se trouve dépassé, éliminé quand il s’accroche à ses vérités d’hier pour justifier ses errements d’aujourd’hui. Il nous apparaît donc bien inutile d’établir un modèle unique, et vénérable, d’un syndicalisme révolutionnaire qui, de 1890 à 1976, en Suède comme en Espagne, aux Etats-Unis comme au Japon, en Argentine comme en Italie, se serait manifesté suivant des canons identiques. Non plus que d’en figer les traits ou les objectifs présents. Ni même de l’opposer à des formes ou des conceptions d’organisation révolutionnaire présentées comme mieux enracinées dans les classes productrices et reflétant plus naturellement leurs intérêts ou leurs espoirs.

Ce serait oublier l’essentiel, à savoir la nature propre, conditionnée, multiple, normalement contradictoire, du syndicalisme révolutionnaire, pour la vaine commodité d’une querelle de mots. Alors qu’hier comme aujourd’hui nous fournissent un matériel humain et des situations sociales en abondance. La vie quotidienne des classes ouvrières, la vie …

Από τη Βιολάντα μέχρι τη Ράνα Πλάζα στο Μπαγκλαντές, τα αφεντικά πλουτίζουν πάνω στο αίμα των δολοφονημένων εργατ(ρι)ών. Δεν διστάζουν να αιματοκυλήσουν τον πλανήτη που έχει φτάσει στα όριά του, για να κερδίσουν ακόμα περισσότερα. Διαγκωνίζονται για καλύτερη θέση στο τραπέζι που στήνεται πάνω στην καταστροφή της φύσης και της ζωής, στη λεηλασία της κοινωνίας. Με κυβερνήσεις, στρατούς, δικαστές, αστυνομίες, τράπεζες και fund, επιβάλλουν τη στυγνή εκμετάλλευση, τη φτώχεια, την αρπαγή των κοινών αγαθών, της στέγης, τις πιο αντικοινωνικές νεοφιλελεύθερες πολιτικές στην υγεία, στην παιδεία, στην εργασία κ.α. Σε όποιον διεκδικεί μια ζωή με αξιοπρέπεια, όνειρα και δικαιώματα, επιφυλάσσουν ακραία καταστολή, βόμβες ή έναν υγρό τάφο στη Μεσόγειο.


Στον κόσμο των αφεντικών που κερδίζει με το θάνατό μας, φυσικό και κοινωνικό, οι εργάτ(ρι)ες αρνούνται να υποκύψουν στο δόγμα του σοκ και απαντάνε “Δεν μπορείτε εσείς, μπορούμε εμείς, να δημιουργήσουμε έναν κόσμο αλληλεγγύης, ισότητας και δικαιοσύνης”. Με το κύμα των καταλήψεων και της ανάκτησης επιχειρήσεων στη Λατινική Αμερική και στην Ευρώπη, συνέβαλαν στη νοηματοδότηση της εργασίας έξω από λογικές εκμετάλλευσης, ανταγωνισμού και ιεραρχίας, συνέχισαν την παραγωγή όχι ως νέα αφεντικά αλλά ως από κοινού συνεργαζόμενοι – σύντροφοι, έκαναν τους χώρους δουλειάς εστίες αντίστασης και δημιουργίας, μέσα από τον εργατικό έλεγχο και την αυτοδιαχείριση, τη συμμετοχή και τη στήριξη των δικτύων αλληλεγγύης και των κοινωνικών κινημάτων, την αδιαμεσολάβητη σύνδεση μεταξύ τους και με την κοινωνία, χωρίς την ανάγκη πολιτικών εκπροσώπων. Οι δράσεις τους συνθέτουν την Οικονομία των Εργαζόμενων. Δικτυώνονται τοπικά, περιφερειακά και παγκόσμια για να μοιραστούν τις εμπειρίες τους, να αντιμετωπίσουν από κοινού την καταστολή της αστυνομίας, των τραπεζών και των fund, να διαμορφώσουν, μαζί με την κοινωνία, τον αγώνα ενάντια στον καπιταλισμό.

content:
Anfang 2026 haben Anarchist:innen in Großbritannien zu die folgende Kampagne öffentlich gemacht. Bis zur Wahl 2029 treffen sie sich zu vier Kongressen, nehmen jeweils an den 1.-Mai-Demos in eigenen Blöcken teil und werden am Wahltag ihren Widerstand gegen die Herrschaftsordnung erklären. Dabei verfolgen sie den Ansatz, verschiedene anarchistische Strömungen zusammen zu bringen. Sie gründen keine neue Föderation, sondern streben an, bestehende anarchistische Strukturen und Gruppen zu stärken und zu verbinden. Unter anderem stellen sie dazu diese Zines zur Verfügung: https://wearetheeclipse.com/flyers-and-zines/ Hier findet sich der „Über“ und das „Manifest“.


ÜBER (die Eclipse-Kampagne) von: https://wearetheeclipse.com/about/


Eclipse 2029 ist ein Projekt zur Wiederbelebung der anarchistischen Bewegung im Vereinigten Königreich, um dem Narrativ des Wahlkampfs entgegenzuwirken und unsere Fähigkeiten zu stärken, Widerstand gegen eine voraussichtlich an die Macht kommende rechtsextreme Regierung zu leisten.


Wir streben den Aufbau einer widerstandsfähigen Gemeinschaft durch eine Reihe jährlicher Zusammenkünfte an (die jeweils mit einer Sonnenfinsternis zusammenfallen und bis zur Wahl im Jahr 2029 stattfinden).


Wir wollen eine gemeinsame Plattform für gegenseitige Verteidigung und Zusammenarbeit zwischen anarchistischen Gruppen schaffen und zudem autonome direkte Aktionen von Affinitätsgruppen unter dem Namen „Eclipse-Komitees“ fördern. Die Plattform wird in Form einer Website und von Publikationen einen sichtbaren Raum bieten, um diese Aktionen zu teilen und die Bewegung miteinander zu vernetzen.


Jedes Treffen wird einem bestimmten Zweck dienen, um zum Aufbau der Bewegung beizutragen.


Das erste Treffen im Februar 2026 zielt darauf ab, bestehende anarchistische Gruppen zusammenzubringen, um gemeinsame Grundsätze für strategische und taktische Einheit zu entwickeln, nach denen wir arbeiten können. Damit soll ein Raum für die Kommunikation zwischen verschiedenen Projekten und Gruppen geschaffen und der Austausch von Fähigkeiten und Ressourcen gefördert werden, um unsere gemeinsamen Ziele zu erreichen.


Das zweite Treffen wird sich auf den Austausch von Kompetenzen und die Bildung neuer Affinitätsgruppen – „Eclipse-Komitees“ – konzentrieren, die in ihrem lokalen Umfeld aktiv werden sollen.


Das dritte Treffen wird ein breiterer Aufruf an Nicht-Anarchist*innen sein, den Wahlkampf abzulehnen und sich unserem Widerstand anzuschließen.


Wir werden jedes Jahr Blöcke bei den Maikundgebungen organisieren, um diese für die anarchistische Bewegung zurückzugewinnen, und wir werden am Tag der Parlamentswahl eine Demonstration organisieren, bei der wir die Gründung unserer Widerstandsbewegung offiziell verkünden werden.


DAS MANIFEST DES ECLIPSE-KOMITEES


Brennt in euch nicht die Wut unter der beunruhigenden Sonne dieses Imperiums?


Etwas läuft grundlegend schief. Trotz all der Arbeit, die wir in den Aufbau einer neuen Welt gesteckt haben, sind die Probleme der gegenwärtigen Welt nach wie vor allgegenwärtig. So können wir nicht weitermachen: wirkungslos, zersplittert und ängstlich. Wir können es uns nicht leisten, das Feuer in unseren Herzen zu verraten, indem wir weiterhin so tun, als wären wir machtlos.


Wie lange können wir das noch ertragen?


Wir können Widerstand leisten und neue Visionen entwickeln. In unseren Gemeinschaften. In unserem Alltag.


Dies ist ein Aufruf, uns zu versammeln.


Wir werden nichts von dem korrupten Staat verlangen, der uns in diese Lage gebracht hat. Stattdessen fragen wir uns: Wie können wir die Macht nutzen, die wir haben? Wie werden wir eine Welt schaffen, die dem Ansturm eines sich rasch entfaltenden Krieges gegen uns, eines Krieges gegen das Volk, Widerstand leistet?


Draußen zeichnet sich eine komplexe Landschaft ab, und wir können sie untergraben. Gemeinsam. Wir können uns der Unausweichlichkeit widersetzen und sie verhindern, dass die extreme Rechte bei den bevorstehenden Parlamentswahlen 2029 neue Schrecken für unsere Gemeinschaften hervorbringt.


Könnt ihr euch eine Sonnenfinsternis vorstellen und spüren, wie sich ihre Freiheit nähert?


Die Kräfte des imperialen Kapitalismus, des Patriarchats und der Zerstörung werden zunehmend instabil. Der Neoliberalismus verfault zum Faschismus. Das globale Imperium bricht zusammen, während unser Planet zerstört wird und Millionen unter Kriegen und ökologischer Zerstörung leiden.

title: Anarchist Parenting
content:
Author:

An Anarchist FAQ


PDF File Size:

 381 KB


Download PDF


The Anarchist FAQ presents a compelling vision of parenting based on freedom, mutual respect and trust in children’s natural capacity for self-regulation, challenging the authoritarian assumptions embedded in conventional family structures. Its strongest contribution is connecting the personal and political, arguing that raising children without coercion, punishment or imposed moralism is itself a form of anarchist practice. It places freedom, mutual respect and autonomy at the heart of parenting. It challenges us to reject the authoritarian structures of the traditional family and recognise that raising free, confident and independent children is an essential part of building a free society.

 An Anarchist FAQ found at

https://ananarchistfaq.anarcho-copy.org/

Anarchist Parenting


 An Anarchist FAQ


 


Introduction:

 What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Part 1:

 What are the main obstacles to raising free children?


Part 2:

What are some examples of libertarian child-rearing methods?


Part 3:

 If children have nothing to fear, how can they be good?


Part 4:

 But how will a free child ever learn unselfishness?


Part 5:

 Isn’t “libertarian child-rearing” just another name for spoiling the child?


Part 6:

What is the anarchist position on teenage sexual liberation?


Part 7:

 But isn’t this concern with sexual liberation just a distraction from revolution?


Introduction:

What methods of child rearing do anarchists advocate?


Anarchists have long been aware of the importance of child rearing and education. We are aware that child rearing should aim to develop

“a well-rounded individuality”

 and not

“a patient work slave, professional automaton, tax-paying citizen, or righteous moralist.”

 In this section of the FAQ [see

here

] we will discuss anarchist approaches to child rearing bearing in mind

“that it is through the channel of the child that the development of the mature man [or woman] must go, and that the present ideas of . . . educating or training . . . are such as to stifle the natural growth of the child.”

 [Emma Goldman,

Red Emma Speaks

, p. 132 and p. 131]


If one accepts the thesis that the authoritarian family is the breeding ground for both individual psychological problems and political reaction, it follows that anarchists should try to develop ways of raising children that will not psychologically cripple them but instead enable them to accept freedom and responsibility while developing natural self-regulation. We will refer to children raised in such a way as

“free children.”


Work in this field is still in its infancy (no pun intended). Wilhelm Reich was the main pioneer in this field (an excellent, short introduction to his ideas can be found in Maurice Brinton’s

The Irrational in Politics

). In

Children of the Future

, Reich made numerous suggestions, based on his research and clinical experience, for parents, psychologists, and educators striving to develop libertarian methods of child rearing (although he did not use the term “libertarian”).


In this and the following sections we will summarise Reich’s main ideas as well as those of other libertarian psychologists and educators who have been influenced by him, such as A.S. Neill and Alexander Lowen. We will examine the theoretical principles involved in raising free children and will illustrate their practical application with concrete examples. Finally, we will examine the anarchist approach to the problems of adolescence.


Such an approach to child rearing is based upon the insight that children

“do not constitute anyone’s property: they are neither the property of the parents nor even of society. They belong only to their own future freedom.”

 [Michael Bakunin,

The Political Philosophy of Bakunin

, p. 327] As such, what happens to a child when they are growing up

shapes

 the person they become and the society they live in. The key question for people interested in freedom is whether

“the child [is] to be considered as an individuality, or as an object to be moulded according to the whims and fancies of those about it?”

 [Emma Goldman,

Op. Cit.

, p. 131] Libertarian child rearing is the means by which the individuality of the child is respected and developed.


This is in stark contrast to standard capitalist claim that children are the

property

 of their parents …

author: winter oak
title: Anarchy at the seaside
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


One of the more memorable periods in my political activism was with Worthing Anarchist Teapot.


I discovered the other day that evidence of this initiative can still be found on the internet, in archived pages published by the friend who was the main force behind it.


Her aim was to replicate in our English seaside town a project that had been quite a hit down the road in Brighton, namely to set up temporary cafés, offering free tea and coffee, in order to spread the word about anarchism.


The first entry in her

diary

 is dated October 1 1998 and she records, defiantly eschewing the use of capital letters:* “some brighton anarchist teapot collective members came over and met with us to discuss creating a worthing teapot. lots of interest and ideas to share and we’re well on the way to having our own anarchist teapot now after it being a vague idea that we might act on at some point in the future, it’s now within sight of becoming a reality”.


You can read the full account for yourself if you like (the timeline starts from the bottom of the page) – basically we did manage to open a café in a couple of locations but only very briefly, as things kept going wrong.


An entry on December 19, still in 1998, describes an evening I remember very well indeed: “a couple of collective members spent an hour or two last night doing the rounds of any worthing pub that would let in anarchists! this was the anarchist teapot desperate attempt to raise funds. we managed to raise just over 30 quid from only four pubs (and one of them only had five people in it). so not bad really. and we had an amusing time arguing with pissed-up people. and were told by a middle-aged man: ‘ah, anarchy, that was popular when i was at school'”.


I tried this a decade later, with a different anarchist friend, and it did not work at all. Society (and pubs) had changed a lot in that time.


The New Year saw us adopt a new tactic. “16th january 1999. well, still no premises and no-one to stay overnight, so no prospect of premises for a while either. instead we’ve been taking the teapot to the streets (we did one today and two over christmas/new year). basically this means a wonky trestle table (but with a nice table-cloth!), a tea urn with a very fetching bright red insulating jacket secured with string, fliers, leaflets and zines, a few collective members, and a couple of donations tins. the ‘street teapots’ have been slow, attracting mainly the people who already knew about us. we have reached a fair number of new people though, so not all bad. it’s the suspicious look people give you when you offer them a free cup of tea that’s so disconcerting”.


We then carried out a special “occupation” of a town landmark that we called the “bandstand”, although it was really just some seating under a roof.


“13th february 1999. today the anarchist teapot squatted the bandstand in worthing town centre, declaring it a ‘free tea zone’. brilliant day! really busy and we gave out loads of tea and info to allsorts of people. overall a great response apart from two old ladies who came over tempted by a free cuppa, saw our literature and said ‘we’re not taking tea from anarchists’ before walking off!


“this was so much better than our usual saturday stalls. we had a big black anarchist flag flying, a huge brightly painted banner saying ‘free tea zone’, and lots of balloons. there’re benches in the bandstand so people could sit down and have their tea. all this made an eye-catching and welcoming area. we also had some vegan flapjack and choccy cake – though this didn’t last long! – and we got through two tea urns in about four hours. so … a great success, we’ll definitely be doing this again”.


I don’t think we did, in fact, but the street stalls kept going for a long time, albeit without the friend I have been quoting and, eventually, without the tea, because it was too much work for little purpose (at this point we became simply Worthing Anarchists). My friend Gil and I were the mainstays of this Saturday tradition for a decade and it only stopped when, sadly, he died at the end of 2009.


I also discovered in the internet archives the

text

 of the little leaflet that we handed out to the good people of Worthing. I know that I basically wrote it, although others in the group may well have made amendments.


Here I have reinserted the capital letters, as I am sure they were there in the printed version!

title: ziq - Unterstützen Anarchist*innen die Demokratie?
content:

Anarchie braucht keine Demokratie

Das Wort "Demokratie" kommt von zwei griechischen Wörtern: Demo- was "Volk" bedeutet.

-kratie: was "Herrschaft", "Regierung", "Leitungsorgan" bedeutet.

Wörtlich bedeutet Demokratie also: "Herrschaft durch das Volk". Oder genauer gesagt, von der Mehrheit des Volkes.

Meiner Meinung nach ist jede Person, die darauf abzielt, dass wir vom "Volk" regiert werden (so abstrakt und bedeutungslos dieses Konzept auch sein mag), nicht für Anarchie. Aber leider wird diese Ansicht nicht immer von den Menschen geteilt, die sich heute Anarchist*innen nennen. Es fällt mir schwer, mir vorzustellen, dass Anarchist*innen, die vermutlich gegen jede Form von Autorität sind und hoffentlich die Vorstellung von Herrschenden ablehnen, damit einverstanden sind, von "dem Volk" regiert zu werden... Ich weiß, dass ich auf keinen Fall von irgendjemandem regiert werden will. Aber viele Anarchist*innen romantisieren weiterhin die Demokratie, vielleicht weil sie nicht in der Lage sind, die jahrelange Propaganda zu durchbrechen, mit der sie vom Staat und seinen Schul- und Medienapparaten gefüttert werden.

Von klein auf wird uns eingehämmert, dass Demokratie gleich Freiheit ist. Jede*r Anarchist*in wird dir sagen, dass die meisten von uns zwar in Gesellschaften leben, die von demokratischen Formen regiert werden, aber niemand von uns so etwas wie Freiheit hat. Trotzdem machen viele uns Ausflüchte, sodass wir die Demokratie weiterhin romantisieren können... Wenn du in einem Raum voller Anarchist*innen sagst, dass du gegen die Demokratie bist, wirst du zweifelsohne die leidenschaftliche Behauptung hören, dass das, was wir jetzt haben, keine "echte" Demokratie ist, aber "wenn wir Anarchismus hätten, hätten wir eine "echte" Demokratie und die Dinge wären anders, weil Anarchismus die einzige echte Demokratie ist!"

Viele Anarchist*innen geben sich viel Mühe, an unterdrückerischen Phantomen wie der Demokratie festzuhalten, und bemühen sich sehr, diese liberalen Konzepte mit der Anarchie zu verschmelzen, obwohl es dafür eigentlich keinen Grund gibt. Anarchist*innen, die darauf bestehen, dass Anarchie und Demokratie ein und dasselbe sind, obwohl die Demokratie für eine endlose Liste von schrecklichen Gräueltaten verantwortlich ist, erweisen der Anarchie keinen Dienst.

Unsere Machthabenden nutzen die Demokratie, um uns in In- und Outgroups zu unterteilen, die Mehrheitsgruppe gegen die Minderheitsgruppen auszuspielen und allen ein falsches Gefühl der Kontrolle zu geben. Uns wird vorgegaukelt, dass wir mitbestimmen können, wie unser Leben verläuft, weil wir an der glorreichen Demokratie teilnehmen dürfen. Natürlich werden wir alle, die nicht zur herrschenden Klasse gehören, weiterhin ausgebeutet und leben in ständiger Knechtschaft. Die einzigen, die wirklich von der Demokratie profitieren, sind die Herrschenden, die sie benutzen, um uns zu entfremden und abzulenken, damit wir uns nicht erheben und sie alle für das lähmende Elend, das sie verursachen, töten. Anarchie lehnt Autorität und die Herrschaft von Mehrheitsgruppen über Minderheitsgruppen ab. In der Anarchie geht es darum, die Autonomie jeder einzelnen Person zu wahren und die Autorität, die uns von Unterdrückenden aufgezwungen wird, abzubauen. Die Demokratie gibt bevorzugten Gruppen das Recht, Minderheitsgruppen zu unterdrücken. Die Demokratie ignoriert die Autonomie des Individuums zugunsten des kollektiven Willens der herrschenden Gruppe. Die Demokratie ermöglicht es den Machthabenden, brutale Machthierarchien aufrechtzuerhalten. Sie ist der Inbegriff von Autorität und dient dazu, den tyrannischen kapitalistisch-staatlichen Status quo überall auf der Welt aufrechtzuerhalten.

Demokratie ist die Tyrannei der Mehrheit, egal wie man sie zu verschleiern versucht. In der Praxis wurden alle Formen der Demokratie von einer Mehrheitsgruppe dazu benutzt, eine Minderheitsgruppe zu kontrollieren oder ihr etwas vorzuschreiben. Alle Formen der Demokratie wurden dazu benutzt, die Autonomie zu unterdrücken, die Selbstbestimmung zu unterdrücken und die Herrschenden von der Verantwortung für ihr Handeln zu entbinden. Wie können Herrschende für ihre Gräueltaten verantwortlich sein, wenn "das Volk" sie gewählt und ermächtigt hat, diese Gräueltaten zu begehen?

author: Malik Chiconela Santana
title: A judicial solution to a political problem
content:
Venâncio Bila Mondlane, the leader of the Mozambican opposition, finds himself awaiting trial (scheduled for November 17) for his alleged role as the progenitor of the seismic protests that followed the 2024 elections and threatened to topple the state. Mondlane is president of the recently formed National Alliance for a Free and Autonomous Mozambique (ANAMOLA) party. He is accused of five crimes by the Public Prosecutor’s Office, namely

public justification of crime, incitement of collective disobedience, public instigation of crime, instigation of terrorism, and incitement of terrorism

. A conviction could mean up to 20 years in prison for the presidential runner-up, the crippling of the opposition, and a transition in the state’s handling of political opponents.

Mondlane’s road to the 2024 ballot was lined with legal and procedural obstacles.

Blocked

 from contesting the leadership of his party at the time, the Mozambican National Resistance (RENAMO), he left it and allied his campaign with the Democratic Alliance Coalition (CAD), whose electoral eligibility was confirmed on May 9, but was excluded by the National Election Commission (CNE) on July 18. The Constitutional Council (CC) upheld the decision on appeal, arguing that the parties who had formed CAD failed to notify the

Ministry of Justice and Constitutional and Religious Matters

 of their intention to form a coalition. The court framed the decision as a purely technical issue; however, its consequences were undeniably political. Mondlane found himself politically isolated only two months before the elections. Forced to reorganize his campaign, Mondlane forged a last-minute partnership with the Optimistic People for the Development of Mozambique (PODEMOS), running as an independent with the party’s political and parliamentary support.

This chronology illustrates how the political agency of Mondlane and his supporters was repeatedly at odds with applications of the electoral law. It may not establish that each application of electoral law was politically motivated, but, at the very least, it raises a broader question of how ostensibly procedural outcomes can reshape the field of political competition, and suggests that legal procedure is not necessarily neutral.

After the October 9, 2024, vote, the CNE declared Daniel Chapo, candidate of the ruling Mozambique Liberation Front (Frelimo), the winner with about 70%, to Mondlane’s 20%. In December, after more than 300 complaints of electoral crimes and irregularities had been lodged with local and district courts, the Constitutional Council revised those figures to roughly 65% and 24% respectively. The revision was, in effect, an admission that the election commission’s results were dubious at best and fictional at worst. The CC altered the results when, as a body of electoral oversight, it could only order the CNE to recount the votes or annul the elections. Unsurprisingly,

the Mozambican Bar Association

 (OAM), opposition parties, and civil society groups expressed concerns over the CC’s vague legal reasoning and the lack of an evidentiary basis for its alteration of the results.

What ensued in the wake of these opaque elections was a six-month period of unprecedented violence. In Mozambique, several elections have been followed by periods of armed conflict. What made this period unprecedented, however, was that the antagonism was not between the state and an organized army, but rather between the state and a mobilized mass of unarmed civilians. According to a

report

 by the Mozambican NGO Plataforma Decide, 411 civilians were killed, some 3,700 were injured, and around 7,200 were illegally detained between October 2024 and January 2025. These figures were disputed by the then commander-general of the police, Bernardino Rafael, who stated that 96 civilians were killed. Even so, charges have only been brought

against two officers

, and, with no updates, it is unclear whether the prosecution is pursuing these cases at all.

The protests began on October 21, when Mondlane called for a peaceful march in tribute to Elvino Dias, his lawyer, who was assassinated by assailants of no particular origin as he prepared an appeal challenging the preliminary election results. This march, like many that followed, was dispersed violently, including through the use of tear gas and live ammunition. Given that we live in a society that promotes ignorance and superficiality, perhaps it shouldn’t be all that surprising that current day anarchist discussions of historic inter-anarchist debates usually miss the point when it comes to colonialism (and imperialism more generally.)

Anarchists do not somehow become immune to colonial society’s influence simply by making abstract and hollow declarations of opinion. Knowledge and comprehension require actual commitment and curiosity, and these are sadly rare qualities among the European, Euro-American and Euro-Canadian anarchists of today.

This article is an attempt at a brief analysis of what’s been missing in recent anarchist discussions of three historic inter-anarchist debates. The term “debates” is used here in the widest sense of a general disagreement rather than some formally-held event or correspondence. Specifically, I refer to the debates between Luigi Galleani and Ricardo Flores Magón over the Mexican Revolution, between Peter Kropotkin and Errico Malatesta on the First World War, and between Emma Goldman and Reginald Reynolds on Palestine.

In the case of Reynolds, we should note that he considered himself a fellow traveler and sympathizer of anarchism, wrote regularly for the anarchist periodicals edited by Vernon Richards, and married the socialist-turned-anarchist Ethel Mannin, but did not self-identify as an anarchist, so my phrase “inter-anarchist debate” must also be understood in the broadest sense.

The anarchist periodical Tinderbox and the anarchist website The Transmetropolitan Review (TTR) have recently invoked the Galleani-Magón debate, though without even being aware of it in the former case.

The individual who writes articles at the TTR website claimed in May of this year that the historic anarchist Partido Liberal Mexicano (PLM) made a “fateful alliance with Pascual Orozco,” the latter being a bourgeois revolutionary who, with the help of Pancho Villa, took control of Ciudad Juárez in 1911. The author makes no distinction between the on-the-ground forces of the PLM and the Junta (leadership board) of that organization, which, from Los Angeles obviously could not directly control the actions of every individual on the frontlines in Mexico, even if they had wanted to.

TTR goes on to sell the lie that at the time, “the PLM was willing to work with anyone against Madero, and they took positions in Orozco’s rebel government alongside oligarchs and hacienda owners, something which further isolated the PLM from anarchists.”

In reality, Magón and the rest of the Junta, in their periodical, Regeneración, called for violent resistance to Orozco once he took control of Juárez, denouncing him as bourgeois and openly accusing him of being on the wrong side of the revolution, specifically because he was trying to disarm other revolutionaries and was friendly with the rich.

To be clear where TTR wasn’t, the anarchists they claim the PLM isolated …

author: Matt Simmons
title: ‘Not at a distance’: listening and participating as decolonized journalism practice
content:
Stella Caruso records a video of drumming and singing led by Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty. Photos by Matt Simmons


This story was produced in collaboration with

The Narwhal

.


I reach out to ​’Cúagilákv Jess Housty around the time of the Haíɫzaqv new year, when the wán̓ái (herring) return and harvesting season begins again after the long, dark winter.


We first connected six years ago, when Xenaksiala Elder Wa’xaid Cecil Paul left this world for the next and I was tasked with writing a

tribute

 to his life and legacy. I called ‘Cúagilákv and they told me stories about their interactions with him. Our paths have intersected a few times since — and before, unknowingly, in the neighbourhood I grew up in where they also spent time during their Youth. ‘Cúagilákv’s

poems

 are part of my love story, too, a thread of words and wild mint, mail and ferries. 


This time, I’ve reached out because I’m thinking about a tugboat called the Nathan E. Stewart, which ran aground near the village of Q’vúqvai in Gale Passage 10 years ago. Eight hours after it hit the rocks, it sank, spilling more than 100,000 litres of diesel and other pollutants. Grief and anger and trauma remain.


Much has been done since to protect Haíɫzaqv lands and waters from another tragedy. ‘Cúagilákv tells me how many others, including their brother, Dúqva̓ísḷa William Housty, are working on the technical and policy side of marine protections and stewardship. But ​’Cúagilákv is following a different path to care for Haíɫzaqv territory. 


“I’m going to deepen my commitment to land-based Youth programming so every kid in the community loves the territory and wants to protect it — and eventually they’ll be the system,” they explain.


Allisa Brown watches the other kids in λáλix̌sístala, the Big House at Kvai. Allisa joined me and Veda on the boat with ‘Cúagilákv

when we headed back to Wágḷísḷa the next morning.


Haíɫzaqv youth and camp staff Aria Reid and Norman Paul warm the drums by the fire before the 20th anniversary

celebration.


And they invite me and my daughter to attend the anniversary of the opening of λáλix̌sístala, a Haíɫzaqv Big House which was raised two decades ago on a beach in the Kvai watershed, around two hours by boat from the Haíɫzaqv capital of Wágḷísḷa (Bella Bella, B.C.) . I accept with gratitude, and following the words of Wa’xaid, I listen. I follow the Wedzin Kwa to where it meets K’sien, and from there follow the river to the ocean. 


In his house overlooking the bay at Wágḷísḷa, Ian Reid, a Haíɫzaqv artist and carver, tells me old stories of the animals and people, and some new ones too. We’re sitting together in his living room while our daughters play in the kitchen. Veda, my kiddo, and Hazel, theirs, met at Kvai and became fast friends. Eli, Hazel’s big brother, is in and out of the house, trying out some newfound freedom on his bike. Ian’s partner, Cayce, offers me a coffee. Cayce and I grew up a few blocks from each other and spent a year at the same elementary school — but we’re only meeting now. Ian’s brother, Garney, is outside the house fixing a water line in the street. I sat with Garney and his wife on the boat down to Kvai. We talked about movies.


I brought a blanket for Ian from the Unist’ot’en feast hall, delivering it for a friend. Ian, whose Haíɫzaqv name is ‘Nusi, meaning “Full Moon,” made a frog crest that was used by Dinï ze (Hereditary Chief) Nedïbïs of the C’ihlts’ehkhyu (Big Frog) Clan of the Wet’suwet’en Nation. Ian puts the blanket on “the way they would put it on me in the feast hall” and poses for a photo.


‘Nusi Ian Reid holds his abalone-adorned talking stick, wearing the blanket from the Unist’ot’en feast hall.


Why am I telling you all this? 


Because, as Opaskwayak Cree scholar Shawn Wilson says in

Research is Ceremony,

 “… it is important for storytellers to impart their own life and experience into the telling. When listeners know where the storyteller is coming from and how the story fits into the storyteller’s life, it makes the absorption of the knowledge that much easier.”


In a word: trust. 


I’ve been leaning into participatory journalism as a means of getting closer to stories that centre and prioritize the Indigenous communities where I’ve been welcomed and trusted, letting respect and reciprocity be my guides. In this practice, I’m not only finding deeper truths and more connection — I’m discovering richer, more nuanced stories.

Standing With and …

Breathing Room


from the apocalyptic, fascistic Right to the insufficient, hypocritical, quietly genocidal Left


In the recent elections in Brasil, one of the largest countries in the Global South, leftwing darling Lula beat Flavio Bolsonaro, the fascistic dynast supported by the country’s plantation owner class. In Israel, the extreme Right lost the elections to the far Right (not a typo). And in the US, a “blue wave” has given the Democrats an ample margin of control in both chambers of Congress as well as a strong majority of governorships (for non-US readers, for whatever weird-ass reason related to our especially amnesiac, isolationist culture, in the US blue is the color of the Left and red is the color of the Right). In once Republican-held or toss-up states like Texas, North Carolina, and New Jersey, Democratic candidates won by double digits while conservatives won in what were, until yesterday, solidly Republican states like Florida or Louisiana by only 1 or 2%.


A high level Republican operative connected to Trump admitted to the press that these elections were just “too big to rig,” casually acknowledging how common it is to redraw electoral maps or send the precise vote-counting machines to the friendly districts and low quality, high-failure-rate machines to the unfriendly districts, in order to win an extra percentage point and tip elections.


Brasil


In Brasil, where former far Right president Jair Bolsonaro serves a sentence of house arrest in his mansion for launching a failed coup attempt after he lost the 2022 elections, his son Flavio Bolsonaro carried the first round of the elections in early October but failed to attain a majority. In the second round, held October 25

In practice that means he promotes oil drilling and mining in the Amazon, he subsidizes the intertwined beef-soy industry causing so much destruction in the south and west of the country, and he also supports manufacture and higher tech industry.
