author: daniel
title: Ableistisches journalistisches Versagen
content: Dieser wurde aber weitgehend totgeschwiegen. Es gab kaum Presseberichte. Selbst über die Besetzung eines Bundesministeriums berichtete einzig die Frankfurter Rundschau. Journalist*innen schreiben lieber über Einzelschicksale. Mitleid-erweckende Berichte generieren online Klicks und gefallen Leser*innen. Die Berichte bleiben oberflächlich und die systemischen und politischen Hintergründe werden nicht beleuchtet. Betroffene als Objekte einer bequemen Berichtserstattung. Sobald Betroffene als Akteur*innen auftreten und das System, das sie behindert, anprangern, werden sie unsichtbar gemacht. Die Redaktionen stehen offenbar zu dieser ableistischen Linie. Der Lüneburger Behindertenbeirat kritisierte die Nicht-Berichtserstattung der Landeszeitung (LZ) über eine Kundgebung am europäischen Protesttag für die Gleichstellung von Menschen mit Behinderung. Die Redaktion antwortete am 22. Mai 2026 wie folgt: „Anm. d. Red.: Am Protesttag selbst hat die LZ tatsächlich nicht berichtet. Wir stellen hingegen regelmäßig Schicksale von Menschen mit Einschränkungen in den Mittelpunkt von Geschichten – unabhängig von Protest- oder Gedenktagen. So haben wir beispielsweise am 9. Mai von der 16-jährigen Lotti berichtet, die trotz Unterstützungsbedarf ihren Traumberuf lernen will.“ Selbst die verwendete Sprache ist hier ableistisch. Das Wort „Behinderung“ wird gemieden, obwohl dies kein Schimpfwort ist, sondern eine neutrale Eigenschaft. Das ist ein journalistisches Versagen. Die Graswurzelrevolution wird dagegen über die Proteste und ihre Hintergründe ausführlich in der GWR 514 berichten. Seid auf den Schwerpunkt der Dezemberausgabe gespannt!

author: Sarah Hughes
title: Members Alarmed by End-Run around Democracy at Buffalo Health Care Local
content:
Things had been tense for some time inside the leadership of Communications Workers (CWA) Local 1168, a 4,800-member health care union based near Buffalo, New York. Still, it was a high-functioning local with a busy calendar of events, stewards handling grievances, organizers pursuing leads, and leaders organizing at work.


So it was a surprise to members in June when their parent union, CWA, put the local into trusteeship, at the request of the local’s president and seven of the nineteen executive board members.


Trusteeship meant the union’s bylaws and elected leaders were suspended, and most of its work temporarily ground to a halt. The appointed Director of Organizing and Mobilizing Mary Nowocien and elected Vice President Patrick Weisansal II found themselves locked out of their group chats, email, and union hall, and facing an internal union prosecution.


A staffer of CWA District 1, Erin Spaulding, was assigned as trustee—tasked with maintaining the functioning of the local, setting up and overseeing judicial processes for the charges against officers, and making a plan to return the union to local control.


Nowocien and Weisansal saw the sudden trusteeship as an escalation of a long-running conflict and a deliberate undermining of the upcoming union elections. Weisansal had just announced his intention to run against incumbent President Cori Gambini.


Now the elections are on hold until the trials are over, whenever that is. And lately, the employer has been taking advantage of the turmoil in the union.


While the allegations are serious, members are concerned that the trusteeship was a nuclear option for an internal financial matter and that it has torn apart relationships at the local, weakened opposition to management’s schemes and denied democratic processes to an active, engaged union membership.


ALLEGED TIMECARD ISSUES


The trusteeship filing lists the cause as “serious allegations of financial misconduct” from officers and “dueling charges” between leaders.


Gambini and Executive Vice President Robert Andruszko had accused Nowocien and Weisansal of defrauding the local of thousands of dollars, by getting paid by both the union and their employer for the same hours worked, and by falsifying records. These issues came to light during a timecard audit in the fall of 2025 by their employer, Kaleida Health.


Nowocien and Weisansal acknowledged there were significant errors on old timecards and paychecks, but said it was the product of the employer’s faulty timekeeping and payroll system, and human error. The majority of other officers also had issues, they pointed out, but only some were being singled out for discipline by the local and the employer.


Spaulding, the trustee, interviewed all the suspended officers and allowed the majority to return to their paid positions—with the exception of Nowocien, Weisansal, and three others not facing any charges: the Communications and Political Directors and one of the Area Vice Presidents. Also fired were two longtime staff organizers, on the grounds that there was no work for them to do, according to one, Ann Converso, who had recently helped organize a new unit of substance use disorder counselors and was gearing up for their first contract fight.


Many current leaders on both sides of this schism were part of a reform caucus in Local 1168, the Caucus of Rank-and-File Healthcare Employees (CORHE), which dissolved when they won their positions in 2020.


Since winning, Gambini and a few others have butted heads with Weisansal, Nowocien, and others over how to tackle problems. The latter camp frequently organized their facility—Buffalo General Hospital, the union’s largest unit—to push back against management’s changes and violations. Gambini and leaders aligned with her argued that that wasn’t the right approach—that they had to pick their fights and not overextend the membership, according to Weisansal.


One Buffalo General steward, who asked to not be named, said members were appalled that the trustee had removed elected officers. “If our employer treated one of our members in a similar fashion,” the steward said, “union leadership would rally around them and fight to return them to their position!”


Spaulding wrote in a public FAQ posted on the local’s social media that the temporary administration “is not intended to be punitive or find guilt against any individual in the Local. It is intended to stabilize the Local while issues are …

author: Tam Saavedra
title: WEI and UN Women Co-Launches Guide for Disability-Inclusive
content:
Across Asia and the Pacific, 350 million women and girls with disabilities navigate conflict, crisis, and climate instability. While they are frontline peacebuilders, community leaders, and human rights defenders, they remain systematically excluded from formal peace and security decision-making.

To break down these barriers, Women Enabled International (WEI) and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific have officially launched a landmark publication today: the Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive National Action Plans on Women, Peace and Security in Asia and the Pacific. Released ahead of the annual UN Security Council high-level debate in New York, this first-of-its-kind guide provides a practical, policy-oriented blueprint for governments, policymakers, and civil society.

Read the full Guidance Note on Disability-Inclusive NAPs on WPS in Asia and the Pacific

Historically, women with disabilities in peace policies have been viewed narrowly as victims or passive recipients of protection. Co-drafted through consultations with 26 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities, in collaboration with Women Enabled International and the UN Women Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, this guide directly challenges that narrative. It grounds its framework in a human rights model of disability and the core movement principle: “Nothing about us without us”.

As WEI Executive Director Maryangel García-Ramos Guadiana stated during the launch:

“The true value of this Guidance Note is that it exists, not as a siloed document, but as a means to ensure we, as feminist disabled change-makers, are not left out of the agenda, but we are the ones who get to set the agenda.”

UN Women Regional Director for Asia and the Pacific, Christine Arab, added:

“National Action Plans on WPS that include everyone lead to peace that lasts.”

The publication was shaped by participatory research, drawing on focus groups and surveys with 26 grassroots leaders with diverse disabilities across the region. It addresses critical ground-level hurdles—including digital exclusion, inaccessible evacuation infrastructure, and ableism in mainstream spaces—ensuring that the voices of women, girls and gender-diverse people with disabilities form the foundation of the guidance.

The publication urges stakeholders to align National Action Plans (NAPs) with international standards—including the CRPD, CEDAW, and UN Security Council Resolution 2475—across all four WPS pillars:

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Participation: Reserve seats for organizations of persons with disabilities (OPDs)—especially women-led OPDs—on NAP steering committees with full accessibility support.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Prevention: Recognize women and gender-diverse people with disabilities as active peacebuilders and integrate intersectional early-warning indicators.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Protection: Address unique forms of violence (such as caregiver abuse or institutionalization) and guarantee accessible shelters and evacuation procedures.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

Relief & Recovery: Ensure transitional justice mechanisms, reparations, and post-conflict upskilling actively include women with disabilities.

The guide also features a practical Disability-Inclusive WPS NAP Checklist to help stakeholders evaluate progress at every stage of policy implementation.

This Guidance Note was made possible with the generous support of the Government of the Republic of Korea (through the Ministry of Gender Equality and Family) as part of the project “Promoting Leadership of Future Generation Peacebuilders and Change-makers in Asia and the Pacific”, and of the Australian Government under the Regional Framework Towards Peaceful, Inclusive Societies (2023–2027).

author: James Moore
title: Be More Human: Why Mental Health Care is Broken and What We Can Do to Fix It: An Interview with Sir Norman Lamb
content:
Hello, this is James and welcome to the Mad in America podcast. This week, we are asking why people with mental health conditions die 15-20 years earlier than people without. Why does the UK spend £100 million every year placing patients far from home? How did the question, ‘What matters to you?’ transform mental health care in Norway? Can mental healthcare be more compassionate?

Sir Norman Lamb asks these questions, and more, in his book Be More Human, published by Jessica Kingsley Publishers. Sir Norman is a former Health Minister, an NHS trust chair, and a dedicated mental health campaigner who was knighted in 2019 for his public and political service. He has seen the cracks in the system up close. In his book, he sets out to answer these questions, and many others, uncovering the reasons why our mental health services are failing. He shares eye-opening stories from patients who have been let down, but also inspiring tales from trailblazers who are shaking things up with creative, community-first solutions.

In this interview, we talk about how his personal and professional experiences led to him wanting to lift the lid on the UK’s mental health system. We also discuss how personal accounts of mistreatment and abuse motivated him to think differently about the human element so often missing from mental healthcare. Finally, we discuss novel, community-based alternatives that offer dignity, compassion and hope.

The transcript below has been edited for length and clarity. Listen to the audio of the interview here.

Norman Lamb: Thank you, James. You can drop the Sir bit. I’m happy just to be Norman, but it’s really good to talk to you; great that we’ve got this opportunity.

Lamb: Yes, it’s been an interesting journey, James, because if you scroll back to the late ’90s, early 2000s, I hadn’t really focused much on mental health. It hadn’t touched me in any particular way. Then I was elected to parliament in 2001, and as a member of parliament in North Norfolk, I wanted to be available to constituents to take up their concerns. I became aware of a lot of people coming to see me with their own stories about the mental health system and how, in their terms, they felt it was failing them in various ways: awful waiting lists, awful use of coercion and institutionalisation. Those stories leave a mark on you.

Then we were hit personally in our own family. Our oldest son, Archie, when he was 15, was diagnosed with obsessive-compulsive disorder. We managed to get a referral to the Mental Health Trust at a moment when we were fairly desperate. He was in quite a bad way, and we were told that we would have to wait up to six months for anything to happen.

When you’re a family in despair and really anxious about a child, being told you’ve got to wait up to six months is sort of hopeless, really. I’m acutely conscious that for many people nowadays, it could be a year waiting. We did what any family would do if they’re able to. We paid for care, and in a way, there’s the injustice because most people can’t do that. They are literally just left waiting.

I sort of concluded that a service that leaves people waiting so long when they’re desperate is not really a service at all in any meaningful sense, and everyone preaches the importance of early intervention in mental health. Yet the system seemed to be delivering intervention at the latest possible moment, often when people were already in crisis.

Then scroll forward to 2012: I became a minister in the Department of Health, and you get a whole lot more stories, people coming to talk to you, wanting to influence you, and it’s a profound privilege for people to be willing to tell you their very personal stories. Sometimes about dreadful loss through suicide, but often just other failings of a system that is under acute strain, but failing too many people.

I left the department in 2015, after the General Election that year, and a couple of months after that, my elder sister, Catherine, who’d been in a state of acute depression after the death of our mother, made one or two attempts on her life and was admitted to a fairly dismal unit up in the north of England. She was in there for about 10 weeks. She was a voluntary patient. But despite being a voluntary patient, she was locked up with everybody else.

After her period in there, she was discharged back home. But some months later, she ended up taking her own life, and so our family had to cope with that tragedy, leaving two …

author: Marion Brown
title: A Decade of the Rise and Rise of “Functional Neurological Disorder” (FND)
content:
“FND occurs when the brain has difficulty sending and receiving signals properly, even though scans like MRI or CT appear normal. It affects movement, sensation, speech, cognition, and other functions. Symptoms are genuine, involuntary, and can be disabling.”


—

NIH website


M

ore and more people are being diagnosed with ‘functional neurological disorder’ (FND). FND is essentially a term for ‘unexplained’ symptoms—including severely disabling symptoms such as movement disorders, blackouts and so-called ‘non-epileptic seizures’—and which doctors say has no clear cause. I began to notice about 10 years ago that these ‘unexplained’ symptoms were the same symptoms as those experienced by some people when taking prescribed drugs for ‘depression’, ‘anxiety’, ‘stress’, etc. and especially when trying to reduce or come off these psychiatric drugs.


I began to meet more and more people with the FND diagnosis who were also experiencing withdrawal effects after stopping antidepressants, benzodiazepines, and other psychiatric drugs—but no doctors seemed to connect the two. I have now come to think that the diagnosis of FND is essentially a way to dismiss adverse effects and withdrawal symptoms—so that doctors can continue to say that psychiatric drugs have no such effects because these effects are diagnosed as something else, even while admitting that they can’t explain what that something else is.


Background


I had trained over some years and became qualified as a

Human Givens Practitioner

 in 2011, and subsequently worked as a private Human Givens practitioner/psychotherapist in Helensburgh, Scotland. This work brought me into contact with many people who, it turned out, were struggling with the effects of having taken medicines prescribed usually by their primary care physician for ‘depression’, ‘anxiety’, ‘insomnia’ etc. This led on to the co-founding of a local ‘motley-crew’ patient self-help group, Recovery and Renewal, in 2013.


Initially we met locally to offer companionship and free non-drug wellness support—and also to ask collectively for formal National Health Service (NHS) support for people who were struggling with adverse and withdrawal effects of these very commonly prescribed drugs. Our efforts were mostly met with fobbing off by local GPs and by official NHS and Scottish Health service bodies.


My lay-person research campaign began as an attempt to formally raise concerns with prescribers about the apparently overlooked adverse and withdrawal effects of antidepressants and benzodiazepines—which were and are (especially antidepressants) commonly prescribed in primary care settings. People who had come together through our Recovery and Renewal group (which later become

a wide-reaching Facebook Group

), were (and are) fellow researchers and campaigners. We are now mainly active on X @recover2renew.


Questioning ‘Unexplained Symptoms’


We began questioning the diagnosis of Medically Unexplained Symptoms (MUS) and Functional Neurological Disorders (FND) in 2016—as it was apparent by then that these mysterious disabling conditions (of ‘unknown aetiology’) were appearing in people’s medical records and that these ‘conditions’ (listed in the DSM) clearly shared many symptoms with antidepressant (and benzodiazepine) side effects and/or withdrawal effects.


I came across a book,

ABC of Medically Unexplained Symptoms

 (2013) and was startled to find chapters written by the (now internationally well-known) FND ‘experts’ Jon Stone and Alan Carson in Scotland—chapters in particular which seemed to refer to the very symptoms that people were experiencing as a consequence of taking (and/or trying to withdraw from) antidepressants & benzodiazepines.


Being also based in Scotland, this was particularly pertinent to the people in our local group, with

Stone

 and

Carson

 having close connections with (and funding from) the Scottish Government and Scotland’s National Health Service. It became apparent that ‘Medically Unexplained Symptoms’ (a DSM diagnosis) seemed to be becoming more often diagnosed as ‘Functional Neurological Symptoms’ (FND).


My own first article was published by Mad in America in December 2016:

“An Outsider’s Observation: Medically Unexplained Somatic Symptoms in General Practice

”

content:

Anarchie ist ein fortlaufender Prozess zur Demontage von Autorität.

Anarchie ist die unerbittliche Verneinung von Herrschaftsstrukturen, das Bestreben, sich kleine Bereiche des Lebens frei von Ausbeutung und Leid zu schaffen.

Anarchie ist der kompromisslose Vorstoß gegen Unterdrückung und die lautstarke Forderung nach Autonomie und Selbstbestimmung, die Ablehnung aller Klassen, Institutionen und Dogmen, die geschaffen wurden, um Menschen zu beherrschen.

Anarchie ist vor allem eine Praxis, nicht eine Theorie. Es geht darum, aktiv daran zu arbeiten, autoritäre Verhältnisse zu beenden, wo immer sie existieren, und nicht-autoritäre Alternativen aufzubauen. Es geht nicht darum, eine Lebensweise für einen imaginären Ort, eine imaginäre Zeit und imaginäre Menschen vorzuschreiben. Es geht um reale Menschen und die Bewältigung realer Probleme.

Anarchie ist eine lebendige und atmende Praxis, die wir in unser tägliches Leben einbauen. Eine persönliche Haltung gegen die Herrschaft, die alle unsere Entscheidungen beeinflusst und so den Verlauf unserer Existenz prägt.

Es gibt kein Endziel für Anarchie. Sie ist ein fortwährender, nicht enden wollender Kampf gegen hierarchische Strukturen und die Autoritätspersonen, die im Luxus an der Spitze dieser Strukturen sitzen.

Anarchie ist der Wunsch nach Freiheit von Tyrannei. Anarchie sind unzählige Generationen verschiedener Menschen mit dem Drang, freier zu sein als sie es unter den Systemen sind, die sie gewaltsam regieren.

Anarchie ist die Ablehnung der Regierung, der Staaten, der Grenzen, des Kapitals, des Patriarchats, des Gender-Essenzialismus, der Sklaverei, der Ideologie, der Rechten, der Linken, des Klerus, der Demokratie, des Privateigentums, der Technokratie, der Kernfamilie, des Humanismus, des Imperialismus, der Gefängnisse, der Fabriken, der Gründerväter, der Bürokratie, der Ethnokratie, der Heteronormativität, der Idole, der Tradition, der Polizeiarbeit, der Neuronormativität, des Ökozids, der Zivilisation und jeder anderen Form von Autorität.

Anarchie ist Gemeinschaftsgärten, Umsonstläden, Graffiti, 3D-gedruckte Waffen, FKK, vegane Potlucks [1], Hausbesetzungen, Lebensmittelwälder, Sabotage von Pipelines, freie Software, die Befreiung von Kühen, Ladendiebstahl, das Sichern von Saatgut alter Kulturpflanzen, die Bildung autonomer Zonen, Attentate auf Tyrannen, Guerilla-Gärtnern, Zines schreiben, Regenwasser auffangen, Wahlurnen verbrennen, Biodiversität, Abschaffung der Whiteness, Hacken, Aquaponik, Musik machen, Upcycling, Polizeistationen abfackeln und Wildblumen in der ganzen Landschaft säen.

Anarchist*innen sind jene Personen, die sich weigern, von irgendjemandem oder irgendetwas regiert, beherrscht oder dominiert zu werden. Anarchist*innen sind wütende, verbitterte, verlorene, ängstliche, desillusionierte, gewalttätige, friedliche, mutige, idealistische, mitreißende, furchtlose Träumende.

Ein*e Anarchist*in steht allein gegen die riesige Flut der Autorität, die in alle Richtungen ansteigt. Anarchist*innen verbinden sich mit jeder geschundenen, geknechteten Seele im gemeinsamen Angriff gegen die rücksichtslosen Systeme, die uns entmachten und entfremden sollen.

Anarchie ist geprägt von endlosen Widersprüchen, existenzieller Angst und unerträglichen inneren Konflikten, und doch ergibt Anarchie für jede Person, die entsetzt oder wütend ist über die groben Ungerechtigkeiten, die diesen kleinen blauen Planeten verschlingen, einen perfekten Sinn. Anarchie ist für jede Person, die ein Leben in Würde anstrebt.

Anarchie ist ein unmögliches, absonderliches, aber für unser Überleben notwendiges Streben.

author: Archipelago Anarchist Archive
title: Archipelago Anarchist Archive, Perpustakaan Anarkis, and Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (A Brief Introduction)
content:
Initiatives in anarchist archiving, librarianship, and journals of archives & libraries in Indonesia

The Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) is an informal, alternative archives and library initiative established in 2024 with the aim of preserving and distributing anti-authoritarian materials. AAA is driven by a number of anarchist archivists and librarians from various cities in Indonesia.

The materials that AAA focuses on are those produced in, and related to, the archipelago (known as Indonesia), whether in Indonesian or in non-Indonesian languages. These materials can take the form of texts, photographs, audio, video, and so on. All of AAA's digital archive collections can be accessed through the Internet Archive.

Link to the Archipelago Anarchist Archive collection: https://archive.org/details/@archipelago-anti-authoritarian-archive

Perpustakaan Anarkis (Anarchist Library) is an preservation and distribution project for anti-authoritarian materials based on plain text. Plain text was chosen because it makes it easier for authors and translators to distribute their work, easier for publishers to reproduce it, and easier for those who wish to archive it[1]. Perpustakaan Anarkis understands anti-authoritarianism in a flexible manner, though not without limits. Therefore, it can be said that Perpustakaan Anarkis accepts and includes both anarchist materials (from all tendencies, except anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism) and materials that can enrich anarchism, such as avant-garde(ism) that challenges not only the boundaries of art but also the state and centralized power, libertarian Marxism, autonomism, democratic confederalism, and so on. In addition, Perpustakaan Anarkis also accepts and includes reportage from the front lines (confrontation) and the home front (care) of flashpoints of popular struggle and resistance, labor strikes, and so on.

Because in anarchism, decentralization and prefiguration are important. And by practicing decentralization and prefiguration, we (and us all) no longer need to wait to act and be overly dependent on a single central point.

Besides anarcho-capitalism and anarcho-nationalism, Perpustakaan Anarkis is also not intended for authoritarian Marxists, misanthropic individuals, extractive technologism (automation that subordinates), avant-garde(ism) that leads to fascism, and other authoritarian tendencies and centralized power.

[1] Authors and translators can distribute their works without the hassle of layout, editing, cover design, and other technical work. Conversely, publishers no longer need to go through the trouble of dealing with writing and translation. And archivists—in addition to finding archiving easier—will receive various versions of the work.

Link to the Perpustakaan Anarkis collection: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/index

Anarsip: Jurnal Arsip & Perpustakaan Anti-otoritarian (Anarsip: Journal of Anti-authoritarian Archives & Libraries) (published periodically, every 6 months) is a space for theorizing–practicing–theorizing–practicing anarchist archives and librarianship. Because we believe that anarchist archives and librarianship should not stop at merely the definition of "managed by, and archiving materials of, anarchist(s) and/or anti-authoritarian [movements and ideas]," but also means using methods, practicing ways of working, and thinking in an anarchist and/or anti-authoritarian manner. If the Situationist International said "to be avant-garde is to move in step with reality" (Internationale Situationiste #8); then we say "to be anarchist archiving and librarianship is to move in step with reality and anarchism."

Link to follow the developments of Anarsip: https://id.anarchistlibraries.net/special/anarsip-jurnal-arsip-perpustakaan-anti-otoritarian

Archipelago Anarchist Archive (AAA) adalah inisiatif pengarsipan dan perpustakaan informal nan alternatif yang didirikan pada tahun 2024 dengan tujuan mempreservasi sekaligus mendistribusi materi-materi anti-otoritarian. AAA digerakkan oleh sejumlah arsiparis dan pustakawan anarkis yang berasal dari berbagai kota di Indonesia.

Adapun materi-materi yang menjadi fokus dari AAA adalah materi-materi yang diproduksi di, dan yang berkaitan dengan, wilayah kepulauan (yang kini disebut sebagai Indonesia) baik itu yang berbahasa Indonesia maupun yang berbahasa non-indonesia. author: Thomas More
title: A Guide to the Study of Marx - Max Beer
content:
A short study-circle syllabus on Marx by the socialist historian Max Beer. It was published in 1924 by the Labour Research Department as part of its workers’ education series. It covers three areas: Marx’s general views (class society, the relativity of economic and ethical concepts, the Hegelian inheritance), historic materialism, and political economy, from surplus value to the falling rate of profit. It also includes a short biographical sketch of Marx and a suggested order for reading Capital. It ends with G. D. H. Cole’s practical hints for students and class leaders, and period adverts from the Plebs League and the Communist Bookshop. It is a good example of how Marxism was taught to British worker-students in the 1920s.

Labour Research Department, LRD

Must We Lie to Please the Critics?

Social Conditions and Character.

Anarchists, Wise and Otherwise.

We find ourselves in a world of conflicting ideas, and every person who has individuality enough developed to be more, in human life, than a domestic animal or lifeless machine, must align himself with others who hold the same opinions, whether he will or not, and then he is in the view of others, and perhaps in his own view, labeled with the name of the idea he holds. So we find that nearly every person is labeled, and some persons have a number of labels.

Finding that we must be something—must hold to certain ideas and work for certain ends—if we work at all, or amount to any more in human life than an ox, or an ax, it very naturally follows that we will adopt and work for the prevalence of such ideas as will bring us the greatest happiness, now or bye and bye. That is why I am an Anarchist. I am convinced that to work for the realization of the Anarchist ideal will bring me more satisfaction than an adherence to, or working for, any other ideal would bring me.

But every one should be able and willing to give a reason for the “faith that is within him,” and I will try and do so.

I find myself in a world of sunshine and shade; of joy and sorrow; of happiness and woe. All around me I see fellow beings; beings that are constituted very much as I am, have similar desires, hopes and aspirations. I find that they are constantly trying to gratify these desires; to realize their hopes and attain to that for which they aspire. I find further that they can do these things only by exploiting inorganic nature, and by assisting each other. I find that as things are now, these beings instead of mutually assisting each other are constantly striving to injure each other, not because they take delight in the suffering of a fellow, but because they see no other way of satisfying their desires and aspirations. They think this state of affairs wrong, and are constantly clamoring for a change, but have not yet learned the great fundamental fact of human solidarity—of our interdependence.

Long have the various members of the human family sought to adjust themselves to environment, and of late have begun to endeavor to adjust the environment to suit themselves. All mankind craves for freedom, but most of the people have sought to gain freedom by subjugating others, or by restricting all alike. They have not learned that they cannot be free while they are holding others, or while they seek to restrict the freedom of others. No one desires to be injured, and yet no one can be secure from injury as long as he injures others. We all wish to be free from injury. I crave for freedom. I see that others want the same condition, and I know that my freedom can be made secure only by the freedom of all others. I know of no other ideal but Anarchy that, if really would secure freedom to me and to all others, therefore I am an Anarchist.

En svensk förf. Fredrik Lindholm, har någon gång år 1909 "gjort" en skrift om anarkismen, vari han åtagit sig att framställa anarkismens uppgifter. Skriftens huvudsakliga innehåll har blivit ett upprepande av de kungamord och tsarmord, som anarkisterna anklagats för, och i vissa fall väl även utfört.

Den omfattar en period då despotismen, liksom nu i många länder, intog högsätet, då folket var helt rättslöst, då anarkisterna och andra motståndare till stats- och utsugningsmonopolen, behandlades som förbrytare och fördrevs ur landet. Ofta fanns det blott en utväg att väcka uppmärksamhet för dessa ohyggliga förhållanden: Bombens detonation.

Bomben var avsedd eller träffade en herre som i sitt dagliga liv, kanske tanklöst, undertecknat hundratals dödsdomar och förvisningar, som framställde sig vara i kompani med gud, innehade kontroll över alla kanaler till det existerande rättsväsendet, befallde över polis och militär, följaktligen utövade ensam härskarmakt eller representerande sådan makt.

Jag anser mig inte i detta sammanhang ha någon befogenhet att diskutera huruvida det var rätt eller inte. Det skulle bli en alltför vidlyftig avhandling, att framställa vad man talar för och emot i ett sammanhang som detta. Våldet har alltid karaktäriserats som ultima ratio, en sista utväg.

I anarkismens politiska och sociala tankevärld har våldet ingen plats. Såväl de politiska som sociala uttrycksformerna skapar en miljö och atmosfär, som avlägsnar ifrån våldet och främjar inbördes hjälp. Dessa förändringar bygger anarkisterna inte på en sinnets förändring som grundlag, men på fakta som att möjligheterna för det sociala välståndets fördelning uppnåtts och herraväldets och förtryckets förverkligande avlägsnats.

Den fulländning som anarkismens samhällsideal företräder bygger på orsakernas upphävande, orsakerna till våldsmentaliteten.

De invändningar som göras, bygga på helt andra förutsättningar. Den ägande som fruktar för att tjuvar och rånare skola tillägna sig hans egendom, vinkar indignerat bort pratet om att våldet skulle bli överflödigt, noggrant förbiseende att människorna under kommunistiskt-anarkistiska samhällsformer inte ha någon anledning att stjäla eller med våld försvara sig mot stöld.

Militären, som tränat in sin yrkesmentalitet och den fanatiske chauvinisten komma med sina argument! Skola vi inte försvara oss mot utländska fiender?

Här är en fråga som redan nuet borde taga klar ställning till. Finns det någon mening i att försvara sig mot utländska fiender? Vad är det man kan och vill försvara? Marken, naturen, sjöarna, kan inte försvaras, kan inte erövras. Under ett krig kan man däremot förstöra dem. Ja, måste förstöra. Fransmän och belgare förstörde stora delar av sina egna områden, direkt, när tyskarna trängde fram under världskriget, förstörde för att inte tyskarna skulle få nytta av det. Franska och belgiska sprängämnen och volymkulor träffade fransk och belgisk natur - och förstörde kanske lika mycket som "fienden", tyskarna, förstörde.

Krigets mekanisering är ett kapitel som vilar tungt på vågen när det gäller att mäta våldets uppgift i nuet. Förr, när en hord människor dreva mot varandra med pikar och muskedunder, var det hela ett farligt äventyr, som begränsades av vapnens räckvidd. Nu finnes det inte längre någon sådan begränsning. Brand-, gift- och spränggaser ha förverkat varje tanke på "försvar" och mobiliserat angreppstanken som enda möjlighet i en våldskonflikt mellan staterna. De långskjutande kanonerna understryka denna utveckling. Ett krig blir blott ett fruktansvärt förgörande av allt levande.

Enda synpunkten som talar för att med krigets våld lösa de mellanfolkliga konflikterna, är den, att vapenfabrikerna och sprängämnestillverkarna behöva experimentera och måste ha stora dividender.

Les deux auteurs veulent, disent-ils, « éclairer ce versant ignoré, souvent délibérément, qui révèle la fraternité de leurs combats ». Cela me paraît une excellente idée[1].

Le présent ouvrage n’est cependant pas à strictement parler une réponse à Affinités révolutionnaires : en effet, le mode d’exposition de leurs idées choisi par Besancenot & Löwy, au moins dans la partie historique, ne permet pas de répondre, parce que leur argumentation est trop allusive et vague, fondée sur un exposé extrêmement approximatif des faits. C’est pourquoi, plutôt que de répondre, j’ai simplement choisi d’aborder les mêmes faits, les mêmes questions, mais à notre manière : le lecteur se fera lui-même une idée.

Это письмо я пишу сегодня, тринадцатого июня тысяча девятьсот восьмого года, дорогие братья Пракседис и Энрике, чтобы сообщить вам дело, которое, на мой взгляд, имеет капитальное значение. Идею, которую я сейчас изложу вам, я уже высказал нашему товарищу Либрадо, и он с ней согласен. Перейдём к сути.

Вы знаете так же хорошо, как и я, что ни одна революция не достигает после победы того, чтобы восторжествовали и стали практическими идеалы, которые её воодушевляли, и это происходит потому, что полагаются на то, что новое правительство сделает то, что должен был сделать народ во время революции.

Так всегда и происходило. Повсюду поднимается знамя с более или менее важными реформами; вокруг него группируются скромные люди; идёт борьба; проливается более или менее обильно кровь, и, если революция побеждает, собирается Конгресс, которому поручено облечь в законы идеалы, заставившие народ взяться за оружие и сражаться. В Конгресс идут люди всевозможных идеалов: одни передовые, другие отсталые, третьи умеренные, и в борьбе всех этих тенденций чаяния революции увядают, искажаются, и после долгих месяцев, а то и долгих лет, начинают приниматься законы, в которых даже не угадываются идеалы, за которые пролил свою кровь несчастный народ. Но допустим, произошло чудо и были приняты законы, в которых во всей своей чистоте сияют идеалы революции, – вещь, которой, конечно, никогда не бывало, потому что очень немногие депутаты имеют те же идеалы, что и народ, взявшийся за оружие; допустим, чудо совершилось и что в особом случае нашей борьбы Конгресс предпишет раздел земель, восьмичасовой рабочий день и зарплату не ниже одного песо. Можем ли мы ожидать, что землевладельцы сложат руки и позволят ускользнуть тому, что делает их могущественными и позволяет им жить в праздности? Разве владельцы всевозможных предприятий, где используются наёмные руки, не закроют свои предприятия или, по крайней мере, не сократят число нанимаемых рабочих, чтобы заставить правительство отменить закон под угрозой всеобщего голода, делая вид, что им материально невозможно платить больше за меньшее количество часов работы?

Когда ресурсы для революции иссякнут, народ окажется в положении более тяжёлом, чем то, из-за которого он был вынужден восстать. Народ, без хлеба, прислушается к речам буржуазии, которая скажет, что его обманули, и возглавит его, чтобы свергнуть новое правительство, – и тем спасутся одни от потери своих земель, а другие – от уступок рабочим.

Богатые восстанут, когда речь пойдёт о том, чтобы осуществить на практике программу либеральной партии, – в случае если чудом, истинным и единственным в истории революций народов, идеалы революции после её победы сохранились бы нетронутыми.

Как анархисты мы хорошо всё это знаем. Мы хорошо знаем, чего следует ожидать от наилучшего правительства, какое только может тяготеть над каким-либо народом, и, как анархисты, мы должны сделать всё, что в наших силах, чтобы революция, которая вот-вот разразится, дала народу все блага, какие возможно завоевать.

Чтобы достичь великих благ для народа, благ действительных, нужно действовать как анархисты, которых легко раздавить даже тем, кто считает нас вождями. Всё сводится к простому вопросу тактики. Если бы с самого начала мы называли себя анархистами, никто, кроме немногих, не стал бы нас слушать. Не называя себя анархистами, мы постепенно зажигаем в умах идеи ненависти против имущего класса и против правительственной касты. Ни одна либеральная партия в мире не имеет антикапиталистических стремлений той партии, что вот-вот совершит революцию в Мексике, и этого мы добились, не говоря о том, что мы анархисты, мы не добились бы этого, даже если бы называли себя не анархистами, какими являемся, а просто …

Es ist kaum 65 Jahre her, da war es absolut üblich, in der anarchistischen Literatur Analysen der Institutionen zu lesen, in denen sich die verschiedenen Formen der Herrschaft manifestierten. Wenn man beispielsweise über die Unterdrückung der Frauen schrieb, dann wurden die Familie und die Ehe untersucht und bloßgestellt. Wenn die Unterdrückung von Vergnügen und der Freude des Lebens zur Diskussion stand, dann wurden Religion und Gesetz ins Visier genommen. Der institutionelle Rahmen, in dem sich diese Gesellschaft abspielt wurde als Quelle der Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung wahrgenommen.

Es scheint so, als wäre dieser institutionelle Rahmen in jüngerer Zeit größtenteils vergessen worden zu sein. Von den verschiedenen Institutionen, in die unser entfremdetes kreatives Potenzial zu unserem Nachteil akkumuliert wurde, scheinen nur noch der Staat und das Kapital (und gelegentlich die Technologie) in einem bedeutenden Ausmaß Erwähnung zu finden und selbst diese werden häufig mehr als Geisteszustände, denn als konkrete soziale Institutionen behandelt. So entdecken wir beispielsweise, dass Anarchist*innen gegen Staatlichkeit (was auch immer das sein soll) sind, anstatt gegen den Staat. Auf diese Weise kann etwa ein Bookchin behaupten, gegen Staatlichkeit zu sein, während er den altertümlichen griechischen Stadt-Staat als Modell für seine demokratisierte Version der „Anarchie“ bewirbt.

Jede andere Form der Unterdrückung wird ebenfalls zu einem „-ismus“ (Rassismus, Sexismus, usw.) oder schlimmerem (Homophobie impliziert beispielsweise eine psychologische Störung, die einer Behandlung bedarf, anstatt einer sozialen Repression, die nach Revolte verlangt). Natürlich verleugnen wir nicht die Realitäten der Ideologien der Bigotterie und ihrer Durchdringung der Gedanken und Gefühle der Ausgebeuteten und Unterdrückten. Aber ohne ein Verständnis des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung und Herrschaft ist es nicht möglich zu verstehen, wie die herrschende Klasse diese Ideologien dazu nutzt, diejenigen zu spalten, die sie ausbeutet.

Selbst die anscheinend Radikalsten (weil ihre Rhetorik am extremsten ist) innerhalb des anarchistischen Millieus entgehen dem nicht. Die von primitivistischen und antizivilisatorischen Kreisen kommende Kritik richtet ihre verbalen Angriffe allzu häufig gegen eine nebulöse, schlecht definierte Zivilisation. Gewiss klingt „Für die Zerstörung der Zivilisation“ radikal. Meiner eigenen Definition gemäß stimme ich damit sogar überein. Aber meiner Definition nach ist Zivilisation nicht irgendeine nebulöse, weitestgehend mentale Kategorie, die dem Rationalismus oder dem westlichen Denken oder welcher unerwünschten Denkweise auch immer entspringt; sie ist ein Netzwerk konkreter sozialer Institutionen, die ich in meinem Alltag konfrontiere: Staat, Wirtschaft, Religion, die Familie, technologische Systeme, und so weiter, allesamt sehr reale Entitäten, die nicht von Gedankenspielen beseitigt werden werden.

Und genau hier tappt die derzeitige Tendenz in eine Falle. Wenn eine Analyse des institutionellen Rahmens der Unterdrückung, Ausbeutung, Herrschaft und Entfremdung vergessen wird, dann tritt Therapie an die Stelle von Revolution. Wir sind dann gezwungen, uns mit den pathetischen, weinerlichen Geständnissen eines Chris Crass zu beschäftigen oder auch der schlechten Popkultur-Psychologie der Autor*innen des Textes „Stick it to the Manarchy“ (wobei schon der Gebrauch eines Begriffs wie „manarchy“ ein sicheres Zeichen dafür ist, dass jemand nichts hörenswertes zu sagen hat), die versuchen ihren „Sexismus“, „Rassismus“, „Homophobie“ und „Klassismus“ abzulegen, die nicht länger irgendwelche Ideologien der Bigotterie sind, sondern niedere mentale Krankheiten, unter denen die selbsternannten „Privilegierten“ aller Klassen leiden.

Jede*r ernsthafte revolutionäre Anarchist*in muss sehen, dass das nur eine weitere List der Feiglinge und jener ist, die ein Interesse an der Aufrechterhaltung der herrschenden Ordnung haben, die eigentliche Entscheidung darüber, auf wessen Seite sie im Kampf gegen diese Gesellschaft stehen, aufzuschieben. Diejenigen von uns, die es mit der Zerstörung der gegenwärtigen Welt ernst meinen, um unsere Leben selbst zu gestalten, haben keine Zeit für diese selbstgerechten Gedankenspielereien, die so sehr an Selbsthilfegruppen erinnern („Mein Name ist … …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire—A Commentary on the European Movement Centered on France from September to October 2026
content: From September to October 2026, a movement centered on France provided us with an excellent window for observing the communist cause in the 21st century and also triggered widespread public discussion. Previously, in the form of four separate commentary articles, we published them successively on the libcom platform, unfolding one by one as the movement progressed. These four pieces are not independent theoretical expositions; rather, they develop within the whole theoretical system represented by The Shackles of the Elements, Dance a Dance of Roses on the Land of Rhodes, and The Contemporary Dimensional Ascension of Capital. Now we have found the opportunity to combine them into one volume and add some notes. This is also the first time we have taken theory out of the study and put it to trial on the real field of movement.

title: New book documents unique plant diversity in the Hevsel Gardens in Amed
content:
A new scientific book exploring the plant life and ecological diversity of the historic Hevsel Gardens has been presented in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). Titled

“Species and Habitats – Flora of Hevsel”

(

Türler ve Habitatlar Florası: Hevsel

), the publication is based on years of field research and aims to help document and preserve the city’s natural heritage.


The book launch took place at the Çand Amed Culture and Congress Center. It was organized by the Amed Metropolitan Municipality and the local coordination board of the Union of Chambers of Turkish Engineers and Architects (TMMOB). Attendees included Co-Mayor Emin Ay, City Council Co-Chair Dilan Aydın, scientists and representatives of TMMOB.


Years of research into the plant life of the Hevsel Gardens


The Hevsel Gardens stretch between Amed’s historic city walls and the Tigris River. As part of the UNESCO World Heritage Site “Diyarbakır Fortress and Hevsel Gardens Cultural Landscape,” they hold both cultural, historical and ecological significance.


The new book examines the vegetation and botanical diversity of this cultural landscape. Prof. Dr. A. Selçuk Ertekin and Dr. Zeki Kanay played particularly important roles in the scientific research. Their studies were supplemented by field observations from TMMOB members, local residents familiar with the area and people from the surrounding region. The publication thus combines scientific research with local knowledge of the plant life and habitats of the Hevsel Gardens.


Ay: Everyone must take responsibility for the Hevsel Gardens


At the book launch, Co-Mayor Emin Ay honored Ertekin’s scientific work by presenting him with a commemorative plaque. In his speech, he highlighted the historical significance of the Hevsel Gardens and the Tigris River. He said both have been closely linked to Amed’s development for thousands of years and have sustained the livelihoods of its people for generations.


At the same time, Ay criticized the ongoing destruction of the landscape, which he blamed on the policies of those in power. He stressed that protecting the Hevsel Gardens was therefore not solely the responsibility of public institutions but a shared responsibility of society as a whole. “Just as a mother protects and cares for her child, we must all protect and preserve the Hevsel Gardens,” Ay said.

author: Unknown
title: Gülengül: The state protects capital and considers it its duty to do so
content:
The explosion that occurred on Monday at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory in İzmir’s Aliağa district, killing 19 workers and injuring 11 others, has once again brought workplace deaths in Turkey into the spotlight. According to the monthly report published by the Workers’ Health and Work Safety Assembly (İSİG), 193 workers lost their lives in work-related incidents in October alone.


İSİG’s periodic reports indicate that at least six workers die in workplace incidents every day in Turkey on average. Despite these deaths, the government continues to ignore warnings rather than ensure workers’ health and safe working conditions.


Seyfettin Gülengül, a member of the Labor Commission of the DEM Party’s Istanbul Provincial Organization, spoke to ANF about the underlying causes of workplace deaths, which have once again come to public attention following the deadly incident at the HABAŞ factory.


‘An average of six workers die every day’


Gülengül stated: “First of all, it must be pointed out that an average of six workers die in workplace incidents every day in Turkey. Let us look at the fatal workplace accidents that have occurred at the HABAŞ Iron and Steel Factory and its port facilities in İzmir’s Aliağa district over the years.


November 16, 2007:

 İlyas Kırdı was killed and ten others were injured when an artillery shell exploded during scrap sorting operations.


August 24, 2008:

 Kutbettin Özkaya lost his life after being crushed beneath a 2.5-ton iron block that slipped from a crane.


2013:

 Two separate accidents occurred within a month, claiming the lives of Olgar Öner, who was killed when a cable snapped, and Engin Solmaz, who was electrocuted.


April 27, 2017 (Kocaeli):

 Nail Demirci was killed in an explosion involving an LPG tanker.


July 26, 2018:

 Evren Erik was seriously injured in an explosion at a steel furnace and died on August 3.


2018:

 Hasan Bostancı lost his life after falling from a dust collection chimney.


August 14, 2020:

 Subcontracted worker Şaban Karaca was killed after becoming trapped between steel blocks.


October 7, 2020:

 Kadir Özdemir fell to his death while working at height without a safety line.


November 6, 2020:

 Port worker Raif Çatan, who was not equipped with a life jacket, fell into the sea and drowned.


August 28, 2022:

 Oktay Eryılmaz died in hospital after falling from a crane.


January 11, 2024:

 Kemal Özdemir was killed when a metal coil fell on him.


October 21, 2026:

 Hakan Doğan fell to his death from a height of eight meters while working on a ladder.


November 5, 2026:

 Eyüp Eğinli lost his life when a tire on a piece of heavy machinery exploded.


November 9, 2026:

 Eighteen workers were killed and 15 others injured when an overhead crane broke loose, triggering an explosion.


So, are all these factories not inspected? They are. In fact, reports are prepared on many of them. However, there is a fundamental problem: Occupational health and safety specialists are paid by the employers receiving their services, meaning the companies or institutions themselves. That is how the law works.”


‘The state protects capital’


Gülengül stated that the government protects capital, saying, “The state protects capital and considers it its duty to do so. It sides with the powerful under the pretext that investors create employment.”


Referring to the Labor Minister’s remarks, Gülengül continued: “Why did the minister speak this way? Let us recall that statements such as ‘Death is inherent in the nature of this work’ or ‘Accidents are inherent in its nature’ were made by the then Prime Minister following the mining disaster on May 13, 2014, in the Soma district of Manisa, which claimed the lives of 301 miners. The same mentality and the same government are still in power today. That is how I interpret the minister’s remarks.”


‘We must have a greater say in the democratization of the country’

Our parliamentary representatives also raise these problems, legal shortcomings and injustices in parliament. author: Unknown
title: Telling life stories, preserving names in Qandil - III
content:
Martyr Taylan left behind seven or eight notebooks and numerous poems. In one of his notebooks, he had also written a note addressed to whoever might one day edit his writings: “I just write. I write without any particular order. I hope the person who edits this later won't be upset with me. This was all I could do. I could have chosen not to write anything at all. But I felt it was my duty, and that is why I wrote.”


Munzur Diyar, a member of the Martyrs' Studies Committee whom we met in Qandil, said that he came across these lines when Taylan's diaries reached the committee. Diyar and his comrades collect notebooks, letters, photographs and testimonies left behind by guerrillas, preparing some of them for publication as books. However, not every completed work reaches readers.


“Tell our child’s story too”


Families have repeatedly criticized the committee’s television programs. Diyar recounts how relatives pointed out that while the programs featured the life stories of certain guerrilla fighters, their own family members, who had lost their lives many years earlier, were overlooked. They asked: “Our children also lost their lives years ago. Why aren’t there any programs about them?”


In response to this criticism, the committee changed its approach. Whereas individuals had previously been selected for the broadcasts, the committee decided to present the life stories of martyrs in chronological order from then on.


Documenting the lives of 700 martyrs


The idea for this program came from a young guerrilla who had never known his father. His father had joined the PKK (Kurdistan Workers' Party) six months before he was born. When the young man was around 21 or 22, he proposed preparing a program documenting the lives of martyrs individually. He continued this work for approximately ten years, producing programs about the lives of nearly 700 martyrs.


The program covered the lives of those who died in 2012, beginning with the first month of the year and proceeding chronologically. Diyar said that once they completed 2012, they moved on to 2013 and planned to continue with subsequent years. Rather than selecting particular individuals for programs, they aim to document as many lives as possible.


Diyar said that the committee also prepares radio broadcasts and written works alongside its television programs. However, the committee places particular importance on diaries written by guerrillas themselves and memoirs they wrote about one another. These account for a significant proportion of the texts the committee is working to publish as books.


Preparing biographies


Diyar said that the committee holds approximately 1,700 diaries that could be published as books. Some are only 20 or 30 pages long and are being prepared for publication alongside the diaries of other martyrs. Others are long enough to fill several volumes on their own. Taylan's notebooks are among these works.


The committee also began preparing biographies of guerrillas who fell after 2020. According to Diyar, their latest plans involve expanding this work to cover everyone, with the aim of documenting each person's life story as far as their research resources allow.


Building a digital archive


Publishing the diaries requires a considerable amount of work. Diyar explained that the writings cannot simply be printed as they are. They must first be edited and organized into a readable format. Yet even when the texts are ready for publication, their distribution is not guaranteed. The committee has been able to publish some of the works in Europe, while obstacles have prevented their publication in Turkey.


For this reason, committee members have begun building a digital archive intended to be accessible to anyone interested. They plan to publish both the books and other materials from their collection on a website that has not yet been launched. However, disagreements have arisen with publishers who insist that the books should be printed before being made available digitally.


“Publishers may want to print and sell books. But that is not what matters to us. Our primary goal is for the people to learn about the martyrs. Once the texts are published, anyone who wishes to print them is welcome to do so.”


Memorials for those without graves


The graves in the cemeteries of Qandil and other areas account for only a small proportion of those who have lost their lives in the course of the armed struggle. “We are talking about 27,000 martyrs …

title: Three ISIS members killed in Pirde
content:
Iraqi security forces killed three suspected members of the Islamic State (ISIS) and arrested another suspect during a military operation in Pirde, in Kirkuk province, on Friday evening. The Iraqi Security Media Cell announced the operation, citing the Armed Forces High Command.


The operation took place at around 8 p.m. local time, based on intelligence gathered by military intelligence. After detecting the movements of a suspected ISIS group, Iraqi army aviation units carried out an airstrike on the group’s location. The operation was conducted within the area of responsibility of the 32nd Infantry Brigade of the 8th Division.


Before the airstrike, security forces had blocked access roads to Pirde and deployed additional military vehicles to the area. Gunfire and explosions were reported in the surrounding area. According to Iraqi authorities, a man suspected of transporting the three people who were killed was also arrested. Searches of the operation area initially continued.


The operation is part of a series of Iraqi military operations targeting remaining ISIS networks in Kirkuk province. As recently as November 9, Iraqi fighter jets struck suspected ISIS positions in the Zaytun Valley, destroying an underground hideout. Despite its military defeat in Iraq in 2017, ISIS remains active through sleeper cells, particularly in territories disputed between Baghdad and Hewlêr (Erbil).

author: Unknown
title: Women Defend Rojava launches new campaign phase in Germany
content:
At a meeting last weekend, the Women Defend Rojava campaign discussed its future activities in Germany and launched a new phase of its work. In light of political developments in Syria and the growing threats to the achievements of the women’s revolution in Rojava, the activists intend to expand their information and solidarity efforts. Their first major initiative will be a month of action dedicated to feminist self-defense, centered around the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25.


According to the campaign, the discussions were based on a comprehensive assessment of the political and social situation in northeastern Syria. The activists pointed to the increasing impoverishment of the population and the persistent threat posed by Islamist groups, including the terrorist organization Islamic State (ISIS). Under these circumstances, they stressed, international efforts to defend the women’s revolution are particularly important.


Bringing the experiences of Rojava to wider society


In the coming period, Women Defend Rojava plans to raise public awareness of the social achievements of the revolution and the current political situation in Syria. To this end, the campaign intends to use informational materials, digital media and local events. The activists particularly aim to reach people beyond existing solidarity networks and connect the experiences of Rojava with social struggles in Germany.


“Above all, our aim is to inspire people around us, in our neighborhoods and cities, with the ideas of the revolution in Rojava and to create hope,” the activists explained following the meeting. In light of political developments in Germany, they also see a growing need for social alternatives in the country. They believe that the experiences of Rojava could offer valuable insights into addressing social and political challenges.


“We want to show that the revolution in Rojava is relevant to us here as well, and that it can offer our society answers and perspectives for solving our own problems.” Planned activities include seminars, lectures and delegation visits for those interested in learning firsthand about the social structures and developments in Rojava.


Month of action for feminist self-defense around November 25


The month of action for feminist self-defense announced by Women Defend Rojava begins in November, coinciding with the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on November 25. Through self-defense workshops, film screenings, neighborhood cafés and creative activities, the activists aim to highlight different forms of resistance to patriarchal violence. These activities will also explore the concept of self-defense and its connection to the autonomous women’s structures in Rojava.


As part of the initiative, the campaign has published a new brochure on autonomous women’s structures in Syria. The publication is intended to support political education efforts and make the experiences of women’s organizing accessible to a wider audience.


Joint cultural activities as part of organizing efforts


Alongside political discussions, the meeting also featured collective cultural activities. Participants watched

Jinwar

, a film by the Rojava Film Commune about the women’s village of the same name in Rojava. The program also included group singing and games. The campaign announced plans to continue its internationalist solidarity efforts in the coming months and encourage more people to support the women’s revolution in Rojava.

title: ¿Cómo una empresa vinculada a Zelensky se convirtió en el mayor productor de drones de Ucrania?
content:
La empresa de defensa ucraniana Fire Point se ha convertido rápidamente en uno de los mayores proveedores de sistemas no tripulados para las Fuerzas Armadas de Ucrania, ha acumulado una cartera de contratos gubernamentales por valor de más de mil millones de dólares y ha puesto en marcha proyectos industriales conjuntos en Europa.


Paralelamente al aumento de la producción y la expansión de su arsenal de misiles, las actividades de la empresa se han convertido en objeto de debate entre expertos del sector y organismos reguladores en lo que respecta a la transparencia corporativa y las capacidades tecnológicas del contratista.


La integración del sector de defensa ucraniano en la arquitectura industrial europea se está produciendo cada vez más con la participación de empresas tecnológicas privadas, entre las que Fire Point ocupa un lugar especial. En otoño de 2025, a través de su filial FRRT, la empresa llegó a un acuerdo con el gobierno danés para construir una planta de propulsores sólidos para cohetes en Vojens, utilizando el llamado «plan danés» de ayuda militar con una financiación total de alrededor de 1.400 millones de euros.


El afán de Copenhague por acelerar la puesta en marcha del proyecto atrajo la atención de la prensa local: como señaló el diario Ekstra Bladet, al conceder los permisos, las autoridades tomaron la medida sin precedentes de flexibilizar los procedimientos, haciendo excepciones a una veintena de leyes y reglamentos nacionales. El ministro de Defensa danés declinó hacer comentarios, alegando intereses de seguridad nacional; sin embargo, el mero hecho de que se hubieran relajado los controles regulatorios en la asignación de fondos europeos desató un animado debate entre los observadores daneses.


Paralelamente al proyecto danés, la empresa está desarrollando colaboraciones con importantes conglomerados europeos: en junio de 2026, en la feria Eurosatory de París, el grupo alemán Hensoldt anunció una alianza estratégica con Fire Point en el ámbito de la defensa antimisiles. Asimismo, en el marco del programa Freyja, el contratista ucraniano colabora con decenas de proveedores de la UE, entre ellos la francesa Safran y la alemana Diehl Defence, para establecer cadenas de producción transfronterizas para nuevos sistemas de armamento.


Para fortalecer la confianza institucional en Occidente, a finales de 2025 la compañía invitó a Mike Pompeo, exdirector de la CIA y exsecretario de Estado de EE. UU., a unirse a su consejo asesor, confiando en su prestigio internacional. Al mismo tiempo, un intento por atraer capital importante de Oriente Medio —la venta de una participación del 33 % al grupo EDGE, con sede en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, por 600 millones de dólaresfracasó después de que la operación fuera bloqueada por el regulador antimonopolio ucraniano.


La magnitud de las ambiciones internacionales de Fire Point se ve directamente respaldada por su desempeño financiero en Ucrania, que muestra un rápido crecimiento. Si bien los ingresos de la compañía se situaron en 4 millones de dólares en 2023, para 2024 habían superado los 100 millones de dólares, y para finales de 2025, el valor de las entregas de un solo tipo de dron se estimó en 13.200 millones de grivnas (alrededor de 320 millones de dólares), lo que equivale a casi un tercio del presupuesto total del Ministerio de Defensa para la adquisición de vehículos aéreos no tripulados.


Según estimaciones de Reuters, la empresa representaba alrededor del 10% del total de las adquisiciones de defensa del país, mientras que su cartera total de contratos gubernamentales, según The New York Times, superaba los mil millones de dólares. Este rápido crecimiento financiero atrajo la atención de los auditores estatales: su investigación reveló que, al firmar los contratos, la empresa había eludido el procedimiento obligatorio de aprobación de precios, lo que resultó en un sobrepago de aproximadamente 16,7 millones de dólares.


Al mismo tiempo, desde la primavera de 2025, la Oficina Nacional Anticorrupción de Ucrania (NABU) ha estado investigando los contratos del proveedor por posibles sobreprecios en los componentes, discrepancias en los volúmenes de suministro y la recepción de fondos presupuestarios preferenciales. Los documentos publicados por la agencia incluyen la grabación de una conversación entre el exministro de Defensa Rustem Umerov y el empresario Tymur Mindich, en la que se discutió la asignación de 311 mil millones de grivnas (7 mil …

author: Taya Graham
title: Voters in Pennsylvania Sent a Message to Those in Power. Will They Be Heard?
content:
Progressives have been working to flip Pennsylvania’s deep-red districts for nearly a decade. It’s finally working.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

In 2018, covering our first midterm election, we followed the ultimately unsuccessful campaign of an electoral upstart named Jess King.

King was a progressive candidate touting ideas like Medicare for All and a higher minimum wage in Pennsylvania’s deep-red 11th District. Her campaign seemed improbable at the time.

Her opponent, conservative Republican Lloyd Smucker, had won his previous race by roughly 10 points. In 2018, the district was gerrymandered to be even more Republican.

Despite the long odds, King made an argument we hadn’t heard before. Even though she was running as a Democrat, her pitch to voters was not exclusively partisan.

“I think what we see is that voters aren’t necessarily on the left-right spectrum as much as they are on a bottom-to-top spectrum,” King told us at a campaign event. “We need to talk more about two political parties that have sold out to special interests.”

Call it the inequality proposition or a power-to-the-people mantra, King made it clear that viewing politics through the prism of party was not only outdated, but destructive.

Ultimately, her pitch fell short. She lost to Smucker.

But the 2026 election may have proved that King was simply ahead of the curve. Alongside historic wins for Democrats, her message re-emerged with new potency among an electorate increasingly angry with the status quo, regardless of party.

“You hear people talking about this top-down message instead of this left-right message,” said Pennsylvania state Representative-elect Ce-Ce Gerlach. Gerlach won with the help of the Working Families Party and the progressive group Lehigh Valley Stands Up.

She said her message of economic populism trumped party politics.

“People are struggling. People don’t want to hear all this rhetoric about Republican, Democrat, socialist, progressive. No one wants to hear all that,” she told us.

This year, we spent two weeks in Pennsylvania’s Republican-held 7th District, which includes Gerlach’s seat. It covers much of the Lehigh Valley, including the cities of Allentown and Easton.

The voters we spoke to shared a similar perspective. Concentrated wealth, corruption, and even the Epstein files were top of mind. What we didn’t hear much about was Democrats or Republicans.

“60 million Americans live from paycheck to paycheck,” a voter named Thomas Fantini told us. “It’s a travesty that, in the greatest country in the world, we’re the only country that doesn’t have universal healthcare.”

His concerns were similar to many voters in the district: pragmatic demands for better policy, rarely couched in the language of partisanship.

Indeed, activists say the election was a referendum on a political system unable to solve serious problems.

“By no means do we think that this election was simply pro-Democratic or anti-Republican,” said Mary Collier, an organizer with Lehigh Valley Stands Up. “It was very much about affordability. How much people are paying for gas, how much they are struggling, and hoping for change.”

Collier points to several candidates her organization backed as proof: Rachel Cuevas, Meriam Sabih, and Jeff Warren all flipped Republican-held state House seats. All ran on a purposely progressive agenda.

“We have been sowing the seeds for a while,” Collier said.

Those seeds go back further than this cycle.

Lancaster Stands Up, a sister group, was central to King’s 2018 campaign. Since then, it and the other chapters of Pennsylvania Stands Up have turned their focus to local races.

This year, that work culminated in a Democratic trifecta in Pennsylvania. The party took control of the state Senate while holding the House and the governor’s mansion.

Collier says the priority now is making sure the newly empowered majority delivers, regardless of party affiliation.

“Otherwise, we’ll be back to square one.”

title: Israeli Intelligence Chief in DC, Reportedly Pushing Trump to Renew Iran Attacks
content:
The Mossad director is reportedly meeting with members of the Trump administration to push for an escalation of the war.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The head of Israel’s foreign intelligence agency was in Washington, DC on Friday, reportedly trying to persuade the Trump administration to renew the illegal US-Israeli war of choice against Iran.

Mossad Director Roman Gofman was scheduled to meet with CIA Director John Ratcliffe in the nation’s capital before traveling to Miami for talks with White House Middle East envoy Steve Witkoff, according to reporting from Axios’ Barak Ravid.

Other sources, including The Jerusalem Post, confirmed that Gofman was in Washington to discuss the Iran War.

Gofman’s trip comes amid an increasingly public campaign by Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to persuade US President Donald Trump to abandon diplomacy and return to military strikes on Iran.

According to Axios, Trump has so far resisted Netanyahu’s demands, instead favoring continued economic pressure and a naval blockade while leaving open the possibility of a negotiated agreement.

“I could end it immediately,” Trump said Thursday of the 258-day war — a claim he has made dozens of times in one form or another. “At the request of the nations that I’m looking to protect, we are doing it a little bit longer… a little bit more civilly.”

The president claimed that leaders of countries including Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Kuwait, the United Arab Emirates, and Bahrain said they preferred that the US maintain the current approach rather than resume fighting.

Netanyahu had reportedly been lobbying Trump to resume strikes immediately after the US midterm elections, in which the Iran War played a major role in Republicans’ losing control of Congress, according to exit polls.

Israel’s domestic political turmoil may also be playing a part in Netanyahu’s machinations. His Likud-led far-right bloc lost its parliamentary majority in last month’s election, and opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has a mandate to try to form a new government.

Some Israeli opposition figures fear Netanyahu could initiate another attack on Iran — or provoke an Iranian response — in an effort to sabotage Eisenkot’s efforts and cling to power. Eisenkot, who met with Netanyahu for two hours Thursday, said Friday that he had warned the outgoing prime minister against taking advantage of the political transition to pursue military objectives.

Trump’s own rhetoric has become increasingly bellicose. On Thursday, he said that he had “no hesitation” about using military force against Iran and that renewed strikes were possible “right now” if he decided to give the order.

In a separate Truth Social post, he declared: “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.”

Thousands of Iranians — including more than 3,500 civilians, at least 380 of them children — have been killed and tens of thousands more wounded by US and Israeli attacks since February 28, according to Iranian and international officials. More than 20 US troops and dozens of people in Gulf Arab states have been killed in Iranian counterattacks.

title: Tayip Temel says new developments could emerge in the peace process
content:
DEM Party Deputy Co-Chair Tayip Temel stated that new developments could emerge in the Peace and Democratic Society Process in the foreseeable future. Temel said that the latest talks had been positive and had raised hopes that existing obstacles could be overcome. At the same time, he emphasized that a political solution to the Kurdish question should not be reduced to the laying down of arms. Rather, he argued, the priority should be to establish the legal and social conditions necessary for democratic restructuring.


Temel spoke during a panel discussion organized by the Southeastern Anatolia Journalists’ Association (GGC) in Cologne. The event, titled “The Memory of the Media in the Peace Process: A European Perspective,” focused on prospects for resolving the Kurdish question and the role of the media in the current political process. Moderated by Hozan Adar, the discussion featured simultaneous interpretation between Kurdish and Turkish.


At the beginning of his remarks, Temel highlighted the distinctive role of the Kurdish press, which, he said, unlike other media, had always also served as a platform for political resistance. He commemorated Musa Anter, known as Apê Musa, and the journalists who had been killed in the struggle for press freedom.


https://video.anf-news2.com/live/firat/4e4469df_20261114130309_2026-11-14-koln-tayip-temel-dem-parti-es-genel-baskan-yardimcisi-panel-demokratik-toplum-ve-baris-sureci-1.mp4


Peace process enters a decisive phase


Temel outlined the current state of the peace process in terms of four successive stages. He explained that the first stage involved ending the armed conflict, thereby creating the conditions necessary for political dialogue. This was followed by the initiation of talks between Abdullah Öcalan, the Kurdish movement and the Turkish state. According to Temel, Öcalan involved leading political figures from other parts of Kurdistan from the very beginning. Temel referred to contacts with Masoud Barzani, Bafel Talabani and Mazlum Abdi. He said that Öcalan had sent letters to these figures and numerous Kurdish institutions, seeking their views on the process. As a result, the process did not remain confined solely to relations between the Kurdish movement and Ankara.


Temel identified the establishment of a legal and political framework as the third stage. He noted that important steps had been taken with the formation of a parliamentary commission on the Kurdish question and the passage of a law, despite existing shortcomings. In his view, the fact that the Kurdish question was being addressed in the Turkish parliament represented a historic turning point.


“The real challenge, however, lies in the fourth phase, which the process is currently undergoing: opening up the legal and social space for democratic politics,” Temel said. He noted that Kurdish political activities had been criminalized for decades and that large sections of the Kurdish movement had been excluded from legal political life. The necessary conditions must now be established to enable those affected to represent their social and political interests without facing repression, he said. These will include, in particular, legal recognition and protection of Kurdish identity, recognition of fundamental rights and freedoms, and the removal of obstacles to democratic political participation. Without these changes, he argued, the fourth phase could not be completed.


Positive talks despite political obstacles


According to Temel, discussions are currently taking place between Imrali and the Kurdish movement on how to continue the peace process on a solid legal foundation. Although difficulties and delays have recently emerged, he said the latest talks yielded positive results. In this context, Temel expressed hope that the Turkish National Security Council (MGK) would expedite its decisions. The framework law adopted on August 10 and brought into force on August 18 provides legal provisions for disarmament and the reintegration of former PKK members into civilian life. However, the implementation of key provisions is conditional upon confirmation that the PKK has dissolved and disarmed, as well as a corresponding decision by the MGK.
