title: KJAR: Society cannot be liberated without women’s freedom
content:
The Free Women’s Society of Eastern Kurdistan (KJAR) called for resistance against state repression, patriarchal violence and the systematic deprivation of women’s rights in Iran. In a statement on the occasion of November 25, International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, KJAR painted a picture of escalating violence, ranging from executions and enforced disappearances of politically persecuted individuals to femicides, economic dependence and social discrimination. At the same time, it paid tribute to the resistance of political prisoners and called for the various social struggles to be united through collective organization. November 25, it said, must not remain merely a symbolic day of remembrance but should become an expression of everyday resistance against violence and oppression.


The full statement by KJAR reads as follows:


State repression in the shadow of war


“As November 25, the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, approaches, the political situation in the region is being shaped by profound crises and conflicts, including the war between the United States, Israel and the Iranian regime. In such a tense situation, the greatest danger is that the war the regime is waging against society within the country, particularly the structural violence against women, will be overlooked. Historical experience shows that repressive systems of rule exploit external crises to consolidate their power domestically.


Over the past year, repression by the security forces and judiciary has intensified at an unprecedented scale and pace. Reports have documented a wave of enforced disappearances in Kurdistan, Balochistan and other parts of the country. People are being arrested without any information being provided about their whereabouts, prisoners are being transferred to secret detention facilities run by the security services, and death sentences continue to be handed down and carried out without interruption. According to the organization Iran Human Rights, at least 528 people were executed in the first eight months of 2026 alone. This alarming figure demonstrates that spreading fear has become a central instrument of the government in its efforts to keep all forms of opposition under control.


Femicides and patriarchal impunity


While state violence continues, society is also facing an unprecedented scale of femicides and killings within families and tribal communities. According to available data, this violence claims the life of a woman in Iran every day, or at least every few days. Gaps in legal protections, a judiciary that facilitates crimes committed under the pretext of so-called honor, and the patriarchal ideology perpetuated by the structures of power grant perpetrators widespread impunity.


One harrowing example is the murder of 28-year-old Meryem Yarmohammedi on Qeshm Island. She was tortured and mutilated by her brother and killed with the involvement of her husband. Rallies were subsequently held in support of the perpetrator. This case demonstrates the extent to which violence legitimized by reactionary traditions and laws has escalated. The victims of this violence also include 21-year-old Soraya, a mother of three who was beaten to death with a hammer, and Ayda Haydariyan from Sine. A society that fails to protect women’s right to life and freedom is condemned to remain trapped in a complex cycle of violence.


The invisible forms of violence


In 2026, less visible forms of violence against women also continued in Iran, including systematic economic disadvantage, unjustified legal discrimination, and psychological and cultural pressure imposed under the pretext of protecting honor, as well as the practice of blaming victims themselves. These invisible forms of violence are further exacerbated by economic and social crises and the absence of effective laws for protection and prevention. They normalize the subordination of women in everyday life, undermine their independence and create fertile ground for overt, often deadly violence.


Prisons have become centers of resistance


Despite these various forms of oppression, the country’s prisons have become centers of resistance, the struggle for justice and political awareness. The resistance of women such as Zeynab Jalalian, Varisheh Moradi and Pakhshan Azizi, along with the ongoing struggle of those subjected to enforced disappearance and state persecution, including Zehra Pirdehqan, Parvin Raseq …

title: Peoples march for climate justice against ecological destruction in Antalya
content:
The Antalya Labor and Democracy Forces gathered at Aydın Kanza Park to protest the COP31 negotiations, ecological deception and environmental destruction. The demonstrators then marched to Cumhuriyet Square. The gathering brought together environmental organizations, trade unions, political parties and thousands of citizens from across Turkey and Kurdistan, as well as hundreds of participants from 90 different countries. Tülay Hatimoğulları, Co-Chair of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party (DEM Party), and DEM Party members of parliament also attended the demonstration.


Hundreds of participants in the international procession chanted slogans against the climate crisis and Israel’s attacks on Palestine, while also singing protest songs. Some participants from different countries joined the march wearing traditional clothing. The international procession featured colorful scenes, with puppet performances, musical instruments and effigies expressing opposition to Trump. Delegations from various countries marched with banners highlighting their demands concerning the ecological destruction taking place in their respective countries.


At Cumhuriyet Square, Çağrı Sert and Erol Malçok read out a joint statement on behalf of the demonstrators. The statement expressed skepticism and distrust towards the COP31 negotiations, emphasized the participants’ demand to have a say in the process, and accused governments of continuing their hypocrisy. The statement stressed that COP31 meetings were dominated by government officials and representatives of fossil fuel companies and other major corporations.


“For 31 years, this pattern has remained unchanged, and unfortunately, they have never surprised us. The vast majority of countries participating in these summits have not only avoided putting concrete proposals capable of providing genuine solutions to the climate crisis on their agendas, but have also failed to make progress toward ensuring that the decisions adopted are legally binding. Meanwhile, the desperate cries of Pacific island nations, whose lands and living spaces will be submerged in the very near future, have gone unanswered. The demands for justice from the peoples of countries that have contributed the least to polluting the planet have been met with attempts by major polluters to buy them off through the establishment of carbon markets.


Yet what peoples demand is genuine climate justice based on lasting, structural solutions, not hush money or superficial approaches involving ‘greenwashing.’ Children, young people, farmers, workers, the unemployed, retirees, caregivers, refugees, women and LGBTI+ individuals, who are among those most affected by the climate crisis, demand justice, not oppression and marginalization.”


The statement recalled that Turkey, as the host country, had paved over large areas of agricultural land in Aksu to facilitate transportation for international delegations arriving to discuss the climate crisis. It continued:


“The government is spending billions of liras in public funds on cosmetic improvements to the city rather than addressing its structural problems. While promoting its ‘zero waste’ campaign, the government is simultaneously turning the country into a dumping ground for Europe’s plastic waste. It also deliberately avoids making any commitments to phase out fossil fuels.


Like all other capitalist countries, host countries such as Turkey and Australia continue their hypocrisy by holding climate summits while simultaneously destroying and poisoning nature and all living beings through mining, hydroelectric power plants, thermal and nuclear power stations, massive fossil fuel consumption, speciesist practices of domination and exploitation that deprive animals of their lives and freedom, and wars.”


Emphasizing that war constitutes a crime against humanity and an act of ecocide, the statement further said the following:


“For giant corporations and states whose sole concern is selling weapons, the lives of humans, animals and natural vegetation are of no importance. For them, the only thing that matters is money, and more money.


In the war between Russia and Ukraine, which has been ongoing for years, tens of thousands of civilians and hundreds of thousands of soldiers have been killed or injured. More than 3,000 people were killed in the war between the United States and Iran, including at least 254 children.


As a result of Israel’s actions in the Gaza Strip since …

title: Saturday Mothers demand answers over the disappearance of Bekir Demir
content:
For more than three decades, Bekir Demir’s family has been trying to find out what happened to him after he was detained by Turkish soldiers at the age of 29. Although numerous witnesses saw him being taken away during a military operation in October 1993, his fate remains unknown. Investigations were closed on the grounds that the statute of limitations had expired, while military records remained classified. At their 1,129th vigil in Istanbul’s Galatasaray Square, the Saturday Mothers therefore called for the case to be reopened and the military archives to be made public.


The Saturday Mothers initiative, which has been fighting for decades to uncover the truth about enforced disappearances in Turkey, commemorated Demir alongside human rights defenders. Participants carried photographs of the disappeared and those who had been killed, as well as red carnations. The statement issued by the Commission Against Enforced Disappearances in Custody of the Human Rights Association (IHD) was read out by Zeynep Yıldız.


Taken away by soldiers in front of his family


Bekir Demir was originally from Batman, lived with his family in Adana and earned his living as a taxi driver at the bus terminal. In October 1993, the father of four traveled with his wife and their 18-month-old child to the hamlet of Badi, part of Alacakepir village in the district of Kulp in Amed. A colleague had invited him there to buy honey, walnuts and other winter provisions from his father-in-law.


At the time, the Turkish army was conducting extensive military operations in the region under the command of General Yavuz Ertürk. On October 13, 1993, the second day of the family’s visit, soldiers also entered Badi. Around 30 residents were rounded up in the village square, where their identity documents were checked.


Because Demir was not from the village, he was singled out. Under the pretext that the commander wanted to see him, soldiers took him to a military helicopter and flew him away. His wife and numerous villagers witnessed the incident. Demir has not been seen or heard from since that day. The family subsequently appealed to the provincial authorities, the gendarmerie and various public prosecutors’ offices. However, their appeals yielded no results. Although eyewitnesses described his detention, the authorities initially claimed that there was insufficient evidence.


Military archives allegedly submerged in water


Further criminal complaints filed by the family in 1995 and 2002 also failed to shed light on Demir’s fate. Instead, the authorities claimed that no military operation had taken place in the area at the time of his disappearance. However, official documents that later came to light confirmed that units of the 2nd Commando Brigade from Bolu had been deployed there.


The handling of military operational records is particularly troubling for the family. On November 6, 2011, the military prosecutor’s office had requested that the Commando Brigade in Bolu disclose the identities of the officers and non-commissioned officers who had participated in the operation in Alacakepir. The requested information was not provided. The explanation given was that the building housing the archives had been flooded, making the documents inaccessible.


As a result, the identities of the military personnel responsible remained unknown. On November 3, 2014, the public prosecutor’s office in Kulp ultimately closed the investigation on the grounds that the statute of limitations had expired. An appeal filed by the family was rejected on March 5, 2015, by a court in Amed (Diyarbakır). An application to the Turkish Constitutional Court also failed to shed light on the case. The complaint alleging a violation of the right to life was declared inadmissible on the grounds that the application deadline had been missed. The family subsequently turned to the European Court of Human Rights.


The Saturday Mothers criticized the failure to thoroughly examine either the detailed eyewitness testimonies or the military operational records. They argued that an effective investigation could have helped establish the truth about the case years ago. “The response to Bekir Demir’s family’s 33-year search for justice cannot consist of decisions based on statutes of limitations and explanations about missing archives,” Zeynep Yıldız said. She emphasized that the authorities must fulfill their international obligations to investigate enforced disappearances and bring …

author: Amy Maxmen
title: The US Has Officially Lost Its Measles Elimination Status
content:
In the past two years, over 830 people have been hospitalized in the US due to preventable measles outbreaks.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The U.S. has officially lost its status as a country where measles is eliminated, a public health triumph secured a quarter century ago.

Researchers with direct knowledge of the deliberations on the country’s status told KFF Health News that the Pan American Health Organization reached the conclusion this week: Measles has reestablished regular transmission in the country. PAHO had planned a public announcement on Nov. 17. In public health parlance, measles elimination depends on a country’s sporadic outbreaks ending within a year. That’s no longer happening in the United States.

“It’s a very sad moment,” said Anne Schuchat, an epidemiologist and a former deputy director at the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention who was not involved in PAHO’s decision. “Measles causes so much unnecessary suffering, everything from a high fever and missed work and school to long-term complications like progressive degenerative nerve disease and death.”

Measles outbreaks are entirely preventable: Two doses of the measles-mumps-rubella vaccine prevent about 97% of infections, so when almost everyone in a community is fully vaccinated, the virus can’t spread.

In the past two years, over 830 people have been hospitalized with measles in the U.S. More than 8,000 people have been sickened in outbreaks that have cost roughly $125 million in medical care, public health response, and productivity losses, Johns Hopkins University researchers estimate. States have reported 13 measles-associated deaths, including a 7-month-old in New York and infants in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin in recent months. Babies typically aren’t vaccinated before they’re a year old.

PAHO, an international group that oversees health in the Americas and works with the World Health Organization, based its assessment on two analyses: one by the CDC and another by an independent group of measles experts. Researchers anticipated this conclusion after an outbreak in Utah surpassed the one-year mark in June.

A spokesperson for the Department of Health and Human Services, Emily Hilliard, attributed the resurgence of measles to vaccination gaps that opened years before this administration. Indeed, rates of childhood vaccination have steadily declined since the COVID pandemic started.

But many scientists also blame the Trump administration for spreading vaccine misinformation and stifling a swift, strong response to outbreaks. For example, the administration cut millions of dollars from children’s immunization programs run by state health departments and terminated funds for research on vaccine hesitancy.

After health secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. sacked CDC director Susan Monarez in August 2025, she told Congress she was fired because she would not preapprove changes to vaccine recommendations “without reviewing the evidence.” She added that “we already have seen the largest measles outbreak in more than 30 years” and that, “if vaccine protections are weakened, preventable diseases will return.”

Spokespeople for HHS and the White House defended the administration, including Kennedy, who led a prominent anti-vaccine organization before he took the helm at HHS. “The President and the Secretary have repeatedly encouraged measles vaccination, coordinated with states, and facilitated the deployment of vaccine doses across the country,” White House spokesperson Allison Schuster wrote in an email.

For more than three decades, the federal government treated measles as a preventable tragedy, with sizable outbreaks triggering national efforts to boost vaccination and stop the virus from spreading. That’s no longer the case, said Patsy Stinchfield, executive director of the Measles Collaborative, a new initiative that educates the public about vaccines and assists health workers responding to outbreaks.

Stinchfield was a pediatric nurse at a children’s hospital in Minnesota during the nation’s last surge of measles before elimination, from 1989 to 1991. She recalled an entire ward devoted to children with measles and the enormous effort required to prevent the virus from spreading to kids with cancer and weakened immune systems. Two children at the hospital died of measles. “That changed my career forever,” she said.

L’anarcho-syndicalisme n’est pas un mouvement sans doctrine. Il constitue dans une large mesure un retour aux principes bakouniniens.

Force importante entre les deux guerres, sa disparition de la scène internationale n’est pas tant due à son incapacité à s’adapter à l’évolution de la société capitaliste qu’à son extermination physique par le fascisme et le stalinisme.

La modernité fournit des atouts considérables au mouvement s’il se montre capable d’en tirer parti.

Cela implique, là encore, l’exigence d’une réflexion nouvelle sur la notion de travail productif, qui ne peut plus se limiter aux critères élaborés par les penseurs socialistes du siècle dernier, et sur la fonction du travail dans la société d’aujourd’hui.

Le texte présenté est celui d’une brochure de 64 pages publiée en 1976 par l’Alliance syndicaliste révolutionnaire et anarcho-syndicaliste, dite ASRAS. L’expérience de l’Alliance dura une dizaine d’années et se situe en gros à une période qui fit la transition entre Mai 68 et l’arrivée au pouvoir de la gauche en 1981. L’existence de l’organisation fut donc courte, mais intense.

En 1976, nous avons publié une brochure sur l’anarcho-syndicalisme parce que le besoin se faisait sentir de proposer aux militants et aux sympathisants un document exposant de manière synthétique à la fois l’histoire de notre mouvement et les grands thèmes qu’il développait.

Quelques remarques sont cependant nécessaires au lecteur de ce début de XXIe siècle. Lorsque la brochure fut publiée, l’URSS existait encore ; certains militants du mouvement libertaire d’aujourd’hui n’étaient pas encore nés.

Aucun d’entre nous, à l’époque, ne pensait que l’Union soviétique allait s’effondrer de notre vivant. C’était à nos yeux un régime de capitalisme d’État dans lequel tous les critères définissant le capitalisme étaient présents. Et d’ailleurs, Lénine lui-même n’avait-il pas défendu ce système ? Le nœud de la critique du trotskisme passait par là. Les trotskistes s’en tenaient à une définition très formelle de ce qu’était le capitalisme : en Union soviétique il n’y avait pas de Bourse des valeurs ni de propriété privée des moyens de production, disaient-ils schématiquement. C’était donc une société objectivement socialiste. Il ne s’agissait donc pas d’y faire une révolution sociale mais une révolution politique pour remplacer la direction en place par une « bonne » direction. D’ailleurs, disaient-ils, la crise du mouvement ouvrier international était la crise de la direction du mouvement ouvrier.

À ce moment-là, on en tenait pour la thèse selon laquelle la concentration du capital – idée qu’on trouve aussi bien chez Proudhon que …

title: Genel müdür ve yardımcısı tutuklanmıştı: Türkiye Sigorta fondan 1.6 milyar lira kazanç sağlamış
content:
Eski Genel Müdürü Taha Çakmak ve Genel Müdür Yardımcısı Gürol Sami Özer’in tutuklandığı Türkiye Sigorta ve Türkiye Hayat Emeklilik fon kazancının enflasyon etkisi düşüldükten sonra hesaplanan 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin liralık bölümünü TMSF’ye iade etti.

Kamuyu Aydınlatma Platformuna (KAP) yaptığı açıklamada, tasfiye sürecine alınan yatırım fonlarından geçmişte elde ettiği kazancın yaklaşık 1.6 milyar liralık bölümünü Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’na (TMSF) iade ettiğini belirten Türkiye sigorta, bu tutarın 1 milyar 599 milyon 887 bin 908 lira olduğunu açıkladı.

Türkiye Sigorta tasfiye kapsamındaki fonların bir bölümüne geçmişte yatırım yaptığını, söz konusu yatırımların yapıldıkları tarihlerde yürürlükte bulunan mevzuata ve şirketin yatırım politikasına uygun olduğunu ileri sürmüştü. Türkiye sigorta TMSF ve Sermaye Piyasası Kurulu (SPK) ile yapılan görüşmelerin ardından kazancın “gönüllü iade” kapsamında iade edildiğini açıkladı.

Şirketin açıklamasına göre iade tutarı, fonlardan elde edilen alım-satım kazancından yatırım süresine karşılık gelen enflasyon etkisinin çıkarılmasıyla hesaplandı.

title: CINQUE GENERAZIONI ALLA RICERCA DI JOSÉ MIGUEL. (risposta alle richieste di intervista)
content:
Si chiama José Miguel. José Miguel Rodríguez Rodríguez, ha 29 anni ed è scomparso il 18 giugno 2026 a Salamanca, nello Stato di Guanajuato, insieme a Wendy Ángela Ruiz Luna e Brisa Johana Flores Luna. Sono passati quasi 6 mesi.

Qualche giorno fa vi ho raccontato come, durante un discorso tenuto dal SubMoisés alla delegazione zapatista – nell’ambito della sua preparazione –, fosse stato sottolineato che la cosa più importante era la persona scomparsa. L’assenza, appunto. E lui, il SubMoy, insisteva sul fatto che quella scomparsa fosse come un buco, come una voragine, come un morso nella vita dei suoi familiari e delle persone a lui vicine. Un vuoto che non poteva essere colmato se non con la presenza di chi mancava, cioè con il ritrovamento dell’assente.

Che non c’era nessuna promessa, nessun discorso politico, nessun provvedimento giudiziario, nessun intervento della polizia o delle autorità ministeriali, nessuna marcia, nessun comizio, nessuna denuncia, nessun conteggio, nessuno striscione, nessun cartello, nessun canto, nessuna statistica, nessun grido che potesse “colmare” quella mancanza.

E allora faceva come se fosse proprio la persona scomparsa a parlare, a rivolgersi ai suoi familiari, agli amici, alle persone care. Cosa diceva loro? Si metteva così nei panni della persona scomparsa e si rendeva conto che qualcosa non quadrava. Che, proprio come lui mancava ai suoi familiari, anche a lui mancavano la sua famiglia, il suo lavoro, i suoi studi, il suo amore, i suoi amici, la sua vita, insomma. Anche a lui, a lei, era stato strappato via un pezzo di sé, del proprio essere, e gli era rimasto un vuoto altrettanto grande, altrettanto doloroso, altrettanto angosciante.

E lui o lei gridava loro che era lì, dietro quella porta, quella recinzione, quella terra, quella prigione. E si disperava perché la sua voce non arrivava lontano, veniva soffocata dal rumore, si perdeva tra le altre grida.

Ma, proprio come chi lo cerca spera di trovarlo, anche lei o lui sperava di essere trovato. Questo era ed è ciò che conta. Ritrovarsi. E diceva ai suoi familiari di trovare forza e coraggio. E di gridare anche loro. Loro per farsi ascoltare, lui o lei per farsi trovare.

1530 uomini, donne, otroas, bambini e bambine, appartenenti a ben cinque generazioni lo ascoltavano in silenzio. C’erano uomini e donne di oltre 70 anni, bisnonni e bisnonne, la maggior parte dei quali veterani e veterane dell’insurrezione del 1994 e della clandestinità in cui prese forma la guerra contro l’oblio.

Adulti di età superiore ai 50 anni, che sono scesi in campo anche loro per lottare, per sfidare, per opporsi a un sistema, a uno Stato, a un governo, a un esercito, a una polizia, a un sistema giudiziario, alla storia e al destino, con la giovinezza e la rabbia che derivano dall’essere dimenticati.

Madri e padri di famiglia, sposate e single, di età compresa tra i 30 e i 40 anni, cresciuti nella resistenza e nella ribellione e che hanno imparato che, se organizzati, potevano vivere con dignità. Sono autorità autonome, promotori di salute e istruzione, miliziane e miliziani, insurgentes, responsabili organizzativi a livello locale, regionale, di zona e interzonale. Parte del tutto che costituisce la nuova direzione organizzativa zapatista.

Altri che, lottando, si sono conquistati un posto degno all’interno della comunità. E grazie a quel posto, si sono guadagnati rispetto e ammirazione.

Ragazze e ragazzi, dai 12 ai 20 anni, che sanno leggere e scrivere, utilizzano con disinvoltura tecnologie che i loro genitori non avrebbero nemmeno immaginato, che si avvicinano alle arti realizzando opere teatrali, film, dipinti, poesie, canzoni, balli, traducendo in quei linguaggi peculiari propri delle arti le loro vite, le loro storie, i loro sogni, i loro amori e le loro delusioni amorose, il loro retaggio, la loro lingua, la loro cultura, il loro essere comunità, con il cuore spezzato appena ieri, e oggi di nuovo sano e integro.

Bambine e bambini, il fatidico “Comando Palomitas”, il cui numero varia a seconda che ci siano o meno dolci al momento della ricreazione, l’infanzia di tutte le lingue, tutte uguali nel gioco e nelle marachelle, la risata infantile come vaccino contro tutte le frontiere umane.

Se guardiamo al calendario, ci sono cinque generazioni. Sei, se si conta quella che sta già arrivando e che si intravede nei ventri gonfi delle giovani madri. Tutte, tutti, todoas delle comunità indigene. Tutte, tutti, todoas con il sangue delle radici maya …

author: Administrador
title: FÜNF GENERATIONEN AUF DER SUCHE NACH JOSÉ MIGUEL (Antwort auf die Interviewanfragen)
content:
FÜNF GENERATIONEN AUF DER SUCHE NACH JOSÉ MIGUEL (Antwort auf die Interviewanfragen)

So heißt er: José Miguel. José Miguel Rodríguez Rodríguez. Er ist 29 Jahre alt und verschwand am 18. Juni 2026 in Salamanca, Guanajuato, zusammen mit Wendy Ángela Ruiz Luna und Brisa Johana Flores Luna. Das ist jetzt fast 6 Monate her.

Vor ein paar Tagen habe ich erzählt, wie SubMoisés in einem Vortrag vor der zapatistischen Delegation – als Teil ihrer Vorbereitung – darauf hinwies, dass das Wichtigste der Vermisste, die Vermisste sei. Also das Fehlen. Und er, SubMoy, betonte immer wieder, dass dieses Verschwinden wie eine Lücke, wie ein Loch, wie ein Biss im Leben der Angehörigen und Nahestehenden sei. Eine Leere, die nur durch die Anwesenheit der vermissten Person gefüllt werden könne, also durch das Auffinden des abwesenden Menschen.

Dass es kein Versprechen, kein politisches Geschwätz, kein Ermittlungsverfahren, keinen polizeilichen oder staatsanwaltlichen Einsatz, keine Demonstration, keine Kundgebung, keine Anzeige, keine Zählung, kein Transparent, kein Plakat, keinen Gesang, keine Statistik und keinen Schrei gebe, die dieses Fehlen „vollständig machen“ könne.

Und dann tat er so, als wäre er die verschwundene Person selbst, die sprach, die sich an ihre Angehörigen, Freund:innen und Nahestehenden wandte. Was sagte er ihnen? Er versetzte sich so in die Lage der vermissten Person und merkte, dass etwas nicht stimmte. Dass dieser Mensch, genauso wie er seinen Angehörigen fehlte, ebenfalls seine Familie, seine Arbeit, sein Studium, seine Liebe, seine Freund:innen, also sein Leben vermisste. Auch ihm war ein Stück von sich selbst, von seinem Wesen, entrissen worden, und da war eine ebenso große, ebenso schmerzhafte, ebenso quälende Lücke zurückgeblieben.

Und dass dieser Mensch ihnen zurief, dass er da sei, hinter dieser Tür, hinter diesem Zaun, hinter dieser Grenze, in diesem Gefängnis. Und er verzweifelte, weil seine Stimme nicht weit reichte, im Lärm erstickte, sich in anderen Schreien verlor.

Aber genauso wie diejenigen, die diesen Menschen suchen, darauf hoffen, ihn zu finden, hofft der Mensch selbst darauf, gefunden zu werden. Das war und ist das Wichtigste. Vollständig werden. Und er sagte seinen Angehörigen, sie sollten Kraft und Mut fassen. Und sie sollten auch schreien. Sie, damit er sie hörte, er, damit man ihn fände.

1530 Männer, Frauen, Andere, Jungen, Mädchen aus bis zu fünf Generationen hörten schweigend zu. Da waren Männer und Frauen, die über 70 Jahre alt waren, Urgroßväter und Urgroßmütter, die meisten Veteranen und Veteraninnen des Aufstands von 1994 und des Untergrunds, in dem der Krieg gegen das Vergessen einst vorbereitet wurde.

Erwachsene über 50, die ebenfalls losgezogen waren, um gegen ein System, einen Staat, eine Regierung, eine Armee, eine Polizei, ein Justizsystem, die Geschichte und das Schicksal zu kämpfen, sich gegen sie zu widersetzen und sie herauszufordern mit der Jugend und der Wut, die Vergessensein auslöst.

Väter und Mütter, verheiratet und ledig, zwischen 30 und 40 Jahren, die im Widerstand und in der Rebellion aufgewachsen sind und gelernt haben, dass sie – wenn sie sich organisieren – in Würde leben können. Sie sind autonome Autoritäten, Gesundheits- und Bildungspromotor:innen, Milizionäre und Milizionärinnen, Aufständische oder leiten die lokale, regionale, zonale und interzonale Organisation. Ein Teil des Ganzen, das die neue zapatistische Organisationsführung ausmacht.

Andere, die im Kampf einen würdigen Platz in der Gemeinschaft gefunden haben. Und sich mit diesem Platz Respekt und Bewunderung verschafft haben.

Jugendliche zwischen 12 und 20 Jahren, die lesen und schreiben können, die mühelos mit Technologien umgehen, von denen ihre Eltern nicht einmal zu träumen wagten, die in die Welt der Kunst eintauchen, indem sie Theaterstücke, Filme, Gemälde, Gedichte, Lieder und Tänze erschaffen und dabei ihr Leben, ihre Geschichten, ihre Träume, ihre Lieben und Enttäuschungen, ihr Erbe, ihre Sprache, ihre Kultur, ihr Gemeinschaftsgefühl in deren ganz eigene Sprachen übersetzen mit einem Herzen, das gestern noch gebrochen war, aber heute schon wieder gesund und ganz ist.

Mädchen und Jungen, das schicksalsträchtige „Comando Palomitas“, dessen Anzahl davon abhängt, ob es beim Durchzählen Süßigkeiten gibt oder nicht, die Kindheit aller Sprachen, die sich im Spiel und im Unfug einander angleichen, das kindliche Lachen als Impfstoff gegen alle menschlichen Grenzen.

Wenn wir uns den Kalender …

author: Administrador
title: UNA SCUSA.
content:
Ai collettivi di famiglie e familiari buscadoras della Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos.

Una scusa. O tante, in modo che raggiungano tutte e ciascuna delle familias buscadoras che si riuniscono alla Glorieta de las y los Desaparecidos.

Ci siamo sentiti aggrediti e feriti. Abbiamo risposto, per mio tramite (i compagni di solito sono più duri) e voi vi siete sentiti altrettanto o ancora più offesi.

Per quanto riguarda le nostre parole, la responsabilità è interamente mia, capitán insurgente primero de infantería Marcos. Le mie parole sono state interpretate come un’aggressione nei vostri confronti. Ne sono sinceramente dispiaciuto.

Vi chiedo scusa di cuore per avervi offeso, ferito e aggredito. Non serve a nulla dire che non era mia intenzione o addurre come scusa “lo stress” causato dalle aggressioni da parte dei tre livelli di governo. Avrei dovuto essere più attento e prudente nell’uso delle parole e nel tono. Spero che questo mi serva per imparare a rivolgermi con delicatezza e attenzione a chi cerca la verità e la giustizia.

È chiaro, crediamo, che occorra rispettare modalità, geografie e calendari. Da parte nostra, vi diciamo con sincerità che speriamo possiate avere successo nel vostro impegno e che riusciate a colmare il più possibile tutte le assenze. E che troviate sempre il modo di abbracciare chi cerca da sola, senza altro sostegno che la propria rabbia.

Perché a volte ci si può dimenticare che è proprio questo il punto: trovare chi manca.

Vi porgo nuovamente le mie scuse. Spero davvero che troviate nei vostri cuori la generosità necessaria per accettarle.

Per il resto, a ciascuno il proprio modo di fare, il proprio calendario, la propria geografia… e la propria agenda.

Dalle montagne del Sud-Est Messicano.

P.S.- Per quanto riguarda l’iniziativa, non abbiamo altri contatti all’esterno oltre al Frayba, nessun altro. Solo quando viene fissato un punto in agenda, contattiamo direttamente i gruppi e collettivi di familias buscadoras o singole familias buscadoras, ma sempre informando il Frayba, che si occupa della registrazione.

author: Mag
title: Explosion im Stahlwerk im westtürkischen Aliağa mit 19 Toten und vielen Verletzten: Nicht der erste Arbeitsmord im Industriekonzernn HABAŞ
content:
„…

Die Explosion ereignete sich am Montagvormittag während des laufenden Betriebs. Nach ersten Angaben des Gouverneursamtes von Izmir brach während eines Gießvorgangs ein Deckenkran ab und stürzte in einen Industrieofen. Die dadurch ausgelöste Explosion verursachte einen Brand, über dem Werksgelände stiegen dichte Rauchwolken auf. Es war bereits der dritte tödliche Vorfall innerhalb weniger Wochen. Im Oktober war der Leiharbeiter Hakan Doğan aus etwa acht Metern Höhe gestürzt und ums Leben gekommen. Am 5. November starb der 20-jährige Leiharbeiter Eyüp Eğinli, als beim Aufpumpen eines Reifens an einer Arbeitsmaschine eine Explosion ausgelöst wurde. Zusammen mit den Opfern der jüngsten Katastrophe sind damit innerhalb kurzer Zeit 20 Beschäftigte bei HABAŞ ums Leben gekommen

…“

ANF-Beitrag vom 10.11.2026


 („Hatimoğulları: Das ist nicht der erste Arbeitsmord bei HABAŞ“) und mehr Informationen auch zu den anhaltenden Protesten und der Repression dagegen:


Protest gegen tödliche Arbeitsbedingungen bei HABAŞ: „Brechen wir das Schweigen!“


„

Nach einer tödlichen Explosion im HABAŞ-Stahlwerk in Aliağa haben Gewerkschafter:innen und linke Organisationen in Istanbul protestiert. Sie werfen dem Konzern und der Regierung vor, Profite über Menschenleben zu stellen.


Nach der Explosion im Stahlwerk des Industriekonzerns HABAŞ im westtürkischen Aliağa mit 18 Toten und zahlreichen Verletzten haben Gewerkschafter:innen, linke Parteien und Jugendorganisationen vor einem weiteren Werk des Unternehmens in Istanbul protestiert. Unter massiver Polizeipräsenz prangerten sie die systematische Missachtung des Arbeitsschutzes, fehlende staatliche Kontrollen und die Straflosigkeit bei tödlichen Arbeitsunfällen an. Die Protestierenden machten deutlich, dass die Todesfälle keine unvermeidbaren Unglücke seien, sondern das Ergebnis einer Wirtschaftsordnung, in der die Profitinteressen der Unternehmen über dem Leben der Beschäftigten stünden.

Auf einem Transparent war zu lesen: „Die Kassen von HABAŞ sind mit Arbeiterblut gefüllt – sie werden Rechenschaft ablegen.“ Die Teilnehmer:innen skandierten unter anderem „Wir wollen nicht bei der Arbeit sterben“, „Die Regierung schaut zu, die Arbeiter sterben“ und „Das ist kein Schicksal, sondern Mord“. Neben dem HABAŞ-Konzern wurde auch die Regierungspartei AKP in Sprechchören für die Todesfälle verantwortlich gemacht.


Anwalt berichtet von wiederkehrenden Todesfällen


Der Rechtsanwalt Lütfi Sabri Batı, der Beschäftigte aus der Bergbau-, Metall-, Hafen- und Logistikindustrie in der Industrieregion Aliağa vertritt, schilderte die lebensgefährlichen Arbeitsbedingungen in den dortigen Betrieben. Er habe am Vortag gemeinsam mit einer Delegation das HABAŞ-Werk aufgesucht, in dem sich die Explosion ereignet hatte.


„In diesem Walzwerk sterben Arbeiter, weil sie in Schmelzpfannen mit tausend Grad heißem Stahl stürzen und verbrennen. Deshalb sind die Arbeiter heute nicht mehr identifizierbar“, erklärte Batı. Nach seinen Angaben komme es in dem Werk nahezu jeden Monat zu einem tödlichen Arbeitsunfall, bei dem Beschäftigte verbrennen. Wie viele Menschen dort in den vergangenen 20 Jahren ums Leben gekommen seien, werde nicht einmal systematisch erfasst.

Batı machte politische und wirtschaftliche Verflechtungen für die ausbleibende Aufarbeitung verantwortlich. (…)


Mindestens 1.930 Beschäftigte bei der Arbeit gestorben


In einer gemeinsamen Presseerklärung riefen die beteiligten Organisationen dazu auf, das Schweigen über die tödlichen Arbeitsbedingungen zu durchbrechen. Hinter den Todesfällen in Fabriken und anderen Betrieben stünden überhöhte Produktionsvorgaben, die Profitgier der Unternehmer und mangelnde Kontrollen. Die Regierung sichere das durch Privatisierungen, Leih- und Subunternehmerarbeit entstandene Ausbeutungssystem gesetzlich ab, hieß es in der Erklärung. Statt ihrer Verpflichtung nachzukommen, sichere Arbeitsbedingungen durch wirksame Kontrollen in Fabriken, Bergwerken und auf Baustellen durchzusetzen, würden die zuständigen Ministerien neue Gesetze zur Verschärfung der Angriffe auf die Arbeiterklasse erlassen.


Unter Berufung auf Daten des unabhängigen Rats für Arbeitssicherheit und Gesundheitsschutz (ISIG) verwiesen die Organisationen darauf, dass im laufenden Jahr bereits mindestens 1.930 Beschäftigte bei der Arbeit ums Leben gekommen sind. (…)


Forderung nach unabhängiger Untersuchung und Rücktritt des Arbeitsministers

author: Bruno Fonseca
title: Nordeste não aceita mais ser subalterno e isso irrita, diz professor sobre novela
content:
Gerou ultraje. A nova novela da Rede Globo

Lá na Minha Terra

 decidiu botar uma mulher para beber água de uma cabaça numa cidade nordestina fictícia chamada Lavra Seca. Um retirante vai a São Paulo em pau de Arara. Dira Paes toma banho num cercadinho de madeira a céu aberto. Filmagens em tom sépia, cenários de casas de taipa, figuras de barro. Um combo de representações do Nordeste usadas há décadas para mostrar pobreza, atraso e falta de recursos.


A revolta começou nas redes sociais. Foi repercutida por pesquisadores. Perfis de

prefeituras nordestinas

 abraçaram a chacota. No dia 11 de novembro, o Ministério da Cultura entrou na discussão com uma

postagem

 sobre a diversidade cultural da região, afirmando que “a cultura nordestina não cabe em estereótipos”. No dia 13, a emissora se manifestou. Segundo a

imprensa

, em comunicado, José Luiz Villamarim, diretor de Dramaturgia da emissora, afirmou que a empresa está aberta a rever escolhas artísticas e realizar mudanças na trama.


A estreia da novela acontece em um momento no mínimo complicado. Há três semanas, a vitória de Lula (PT) sobre

Flávio Bolsonaro

 (PL) levou novamente a comentários xenófobos nas redes sociais contra o Nordeste, onde o petista tem vantagem. As próprias eleições foram marcadas pela instrumentalização da região, como no

vídeo

 publicado pelo deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL), que simulou um “Nordeste sem filtro”, no qual pessoas falavam sobre a falta de serviços básicos e criticavam o governo petista. Nos bastidores, a produção do vídeo omitiu uma antena parabólica e uma caminhonete de luxo, que contrastavam com a pobreza que queriam representar.


A representação de um Nordeste parado no tempo em 2026 é uma agressão – e também um projeto político de um grupo que não aceita o novo lugar que a região ocupa no Brasil, afirma o historiador e professor visitante da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN) Durval Muniz de Albuquerque Jr.

 A

Agência Pública

 conversou com o autor de “A Invenção do Nordeste e outras artes”, obra que é referência na pesquisa sobre a criação da imagem política e cultural do Nordeste.


“Você acha que as elites do Sudeste, do Sul, que inclusive financiam a Rede Globo, estão satisfeitas com o fato que o Nordeste vem decidindo eleições após eleições? O pessoal da Faria Lima está contente com o Nordeste ter dado pela quarta vez a vitória a Lula, de ter quatro estados governados pelo PT?”, questiona. “O fato é que o Nordeste, ao se recusar ocupar o lugar que ocupava anteriormente, irrita essas elites, que patrocinam essas patacoadas”, critica o professor.


Albuquerque comenta que, apesar de ser importante a autocrítica – afinal, a sua obra mostra como a imagem do Nordeste “pobre” e “seco” foi criada e usada pela própria elite nordestina –, é necessário destacar que a reação à novela é válida e proporcional à narrativa feita pela mídia concentrada no Sudeste repetidamente.


“A elite nordestina viveu da exploração da miséria, do trabalho dos miseráveis e da representação dos miseráveis e dos pobres, do ponto de vista cultural […] Nós não podemos perder o senso crítico para o que acontece aqui por causa desse ataque que vem de fora. Mas é claro que a gente também não pode deixar de responder esse ataque”, comenta.


Durval Muniz de Albuquerque Jr. é historiador e professor visitante da Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN)


Leia a entrevista abaixo:


A nossa conversa parte da nova novela da Rede Globo,


Lá na Minha Terra

, que gerou muitas críticas sobre mais uma representação estereotipada do Nordeste. Eu gostaria de ouvir sua avaliação sobre essa representação, e também sobre as críticas.


Eu acho que a reação é proporcional à agressão. Finalmente, os nordestinos estão reagindo com mais ênfase às sucessivas construções depreciativas da região.


Primeiro, evidentemente, como eu já discuti em toda a minha obra, esse imaginário sobre um Nordeste pobre, parado no tempo, foi construído pela própria elite nordestina para conseguir manter os seus privilégios, sua dominação, seus recursos, dentro das lutas regionais no país.


Ora, o que aconteceu?

O que aconteceu é que, dos anos 1970 para cá, e notadamente nas últimas décadas, a região se transformou profundamente e esse imaginário ficou completamente descolado da realidade regional.


Por exemplo, hoje você tem mais de 80% da população do Nordeste morando em cidades. Não dá para você sustentar uma representação rural, agrária do …

author: Evanilton Gonçalves
title: Um motorista com o coração partido
content:
Eu nunca pensei que fosse escutar, por vontade própria, um álbum de uma dupla sertaneja. Também nunca pensei que fosse, por vontade própria, a um show de uma dupla sertaneja. E as duas certezas absolutas se mantêm quase intactas, porque minha apreciação por uma grande variedade de estilos musicais tem um limite e nunca incluiu afinidade pelo gênero sertanejo. É simples. Atribuo isso ao fato de minha sensibilidade musical não dialogar muito com a abordagem específica dos temas, os timbres e os ritmos dos cantores. Também poderia elencar os conceitos aristotélicos de ethos, pathos e logos para justificar, de forma pedante, minhas preferências sonoras ou meu desajustamento artístico, mas não é o caso. Percebi que a expressão “Eu nunca” é uma armadilha que a vida faz questão de desmontar com as ironias do destino.


De repente, me vi numa cena de “A vida de Chuck”, filme baseado em um texto de Stephen King, cujo drama fantástico e existencial se move, de trás para a frente, no sentido de uma celebração emocionante da vida. O filme, dividido em três capítulos, começa em um mundo colapsado, com desastres ambientais por toda parte e o que parece ser o fim de nossa sociedade. No meio de todo esse caos, anúncios em outdoors e em telas exibem uma mensagem enigmática: “Obrigado, Chuck”. Quem é Chuck e por que o mundo estava agradecendo a ele foi a pergunta natural que me fiz, e o filme se encarrega de responder magistralmente. A cena em que, de repente, me vi está no segundo capítulo do filme, quando o personagem encontra uma certa alegria por meio da música e da dança e demonstra desenvoltura sem qualquer constrangimento público.


Eu estava voltando para casa em um carro por aplicativo quando tudo aconteceu, mas parecia que o pequeno e confortável espaço do BYD Dolphin tinha criado uma nova plasticidade espacial, uma espécie de ilusão de amplitude que me projetava para um ambiente maior, diferente. O jovem motorista dirigia seu carro elétrico com habilidade e uma certa dose de imprudência. Na enorme tela do sistema multimídia, vi dois cantores, ambos de óculos de sol, segurando microfones. Um usava um chapéu de estilo country e uma camisa sem mangas. O outro tinha o cabelo curto penteado para cima, tatuagens visíveis nos braços e no pescoço, e vestia uma camisa aberta também. Quem são esses caras? Foi a pergunta que me fiz, num misto de flagrante ignorância e de surpresa pelo impacto que causavam ao motorista. Do lado de fora, o trânsito continuava existindo. 


Dentro do carro, o motorista cantava a plenos pulmões, sem o menor pingo de vergonha, com a convicção de quem era a própria voz da dupla sertaneja. Sozinho no seu próprio mundo (mesmo com todos os assentos ocupados por passageiros), ele balançava a cabeça, marcando o ritmo com gestos expressivos. Segurando um microfone imaginário, acompanhava cada verso com a precisão de quem conhecia a própria dor de trás para a frente. É verdade que ele errou o trajeto duas vezes até me deixar no meu destino. Mas era compreensível; havia uma entrega genuína ali: cada faixa do álbum parecia uma urgência confessional, como se cada música fosse uma resposta direta e tardia do motorista para alguém que, infelizmente, partiu seu coração.

title: Vendors in Baclaran displaced due to ASEAN Summit
content:
The Philippine government has started clearing operations in Baclaran, Parañaque City since November 1 as part of the preparations for the incoming 49th ASEAN Summit on November 15 to 17. Street vendors have been affected by the operations, depriving them of opportunities to earn a living.

Vendors now struggle to sell their products due to the low number of buyers and the constant threat that authorities might confiscate their goods and arrest them.

One of the vendors, Marlyn, retorted in Filipino, “How can we sell if we are going to be arrested? How can we feed our family?”

author: Kodao Productions
title: Day of infamy for Sara
content:
November 12, 2026 would go down in history as the day when the defense of Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio crashed in flames, with its witnesses digging the grave for Sara and adding more fuel to the fire that has engulfed their case since the impeachment trial commenced in July 2026.


The witnesses, all of them proven pals, associates or underlings of Sara and her husband Atty. Manases Carpio, took turns in torturing the Senate impeachment with irrational answers to pointed questions from the prosecution. Grilled to a crisp was Atty. Anel Martin Antero, who admitted that he earns from Carpio’s law office and is a firm adherent of Dutertism (whatever that means) and avid defender of Sara to the extent that he questions the legitimacy of the articles of impeachment and the “harassment” of Sara and his very close friend Mans Carpio. His social media posts and his larping (live action role play) showed his credibility is shot.


Stunned by the question of Atty. Amando Virgil Ligutan about the P580,000 check he had received from Carpio in 2020, Antero could not remember receiving the amount. The documents from the Anti-Money Laundering Council (AMLC) showed that he did. Selective amnesia is naturally dubious and it would not help him or Sara if he resorts to eternal equivocation. Lying before an impeachment court is

malum in se

 or inherently wrong. But as the old saw says, even in death, a lawyer still lies. Asked by Ligutan about the banquet for 11 in Tokyo for which Carpio spent more than ₱205,000, Antero tried to claim that he forked over ₱40,000 for the meal but could not produce photos or receipts that proved he paid his share. Carpio, Antero argued, used his credit card to pay the amount so he could earn more points, which is akin to overspending at Starbucks to secure 19 stickers that entitles him to a 2027 planner.


In yet another woeful episode, defense witness Chadrin Parian, whose son is a teammate of Carpio’s son, said the 11 players received a pair of Nike shoes each, but the total purchase in Kuala Lumpur was ₱256,000 for 25 pairs of Nike shoes. Pressed by prosecutor Rey Robles, Parian said the parents and guardians of the players were also gifted with expensive Nike shoes. Parian’s justification was that “the kids and parents deserved to be given such a treat.” It was not the first time that the ultra-generous Carpio gave a treat to the boys, as other documents secured by the prosecution showed. For other young but poor Filipino basketball players, such flex of munificence is outrageous since they have to solicit cash for their uniforms and shoes before they could join tournaments.


Antero’s riposte is similar to the series of “I don’t know,” “I prefer not to respond,” “it is not my duty to look into other people’s SALNs,” and “I don’t remember” answers that Gencorp Industries Inc. counsel Atty. Suzette Balucanag-Punay dished out when she was on the hot seat. Punay’s case is bewildering as she tried to protect Sara at the outset, insisting that the respondent is not a Gencorp stockholder but admitted Sara had received ₱2,142,369.14 as “return of capital” from the company from 2022 to 2025, broken down as follows: ₱337,500 in 2022; ₱555,750 in 2023; ₱612,419.14 in 2024, and; ₱636,700 in 2025. Then there is Punay’s inventing Sara’s “loose investments” to justify earnings from a franchise she was not even supposed to benefit from.


In her testimony, Punay tried to impress the impeachment court that what Sara’s SALNs listing of her stock-holdings was wrong and that her Gencorp. records were truthful. This was a case of “honest mistake” from a respondent who horribly claimed that sincerity, honesty and credibility are traits not needed in politics. Punay worsened the case of Sara as she, like Antero, failed to bring her documents to debunk the allegations of the prosecution. Lead defense counsel Atty. Sheila Sison, who has had a tough time putting her ducks in a row, should perhaps reassemble her troops and arm them with better arguments and solid evidence to pierce the ramparts of the prosecution’s mighty fortress.


If Sison were to remember her DHM (Dialectical Historical materialism), she should resurrect her genius, turn the thesis and its antithesis into a synthesis that should resolve the issues in her favor. However, relying on the pleasure of Sara Zimmerman Duterte Carpio to divine an invincible legal theory might just turn out to be a *nefandous option. Of course, Sison is still not afflicted …

author: Daron Letts
title: Iqlauit gets sneak peek at Aqqusariaq Recovery Centre
content:
Nunavut’s $83.7-million Aqqusariaq Recovery Centre gave the public its first look inside Friday, approximately seven months before staff will welcome the first 24 full-time residents inside.


Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. President Gloria Uluqsi, left, says she looks forward to the leadership provided by Annie Aningmiuq, executive director of Aqqusariaq Corp., the arms-length nonprofit organization established to run the centre. (Photo by Daron Letts)


Hiring, trauma-informed care training for new staff, programming decisions, and operational preparations continue before services can be delivered, said Annie Aningmiuq, executive director of

Aqqusariaq Corp., the arms-length nonprofit organization established by Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. to run the centre.


However, outpatient care will begin early in the new year, she added, during an interview.


“

We have a gorgeous sewing room – we can have cultural programming here before we have people living upstairs to do their their treatments

,” she said. “We can also connect other services that are available.”


The facility also features a classroom, withdrawal recovery rooms, a nursing station and exam room, a cultural food processing area, a daycare, and a group therapy room. Inuit art is displayed throughout the building.


So far, two other employees have been hired, with three more core positions to be filled in coming months, Aningmiuq said.


Alcoholics Anonymous and other related community programs may choose to use space in the centre before the facility offers its full menu of programs next summer, she said.


A lighted mural on the ceiling of the Aqqusariaq Recovery Centre includes many depictions of iconic imagers from northern life. (Photo by Lilli Akpaleeapik)


Friday’s open house comes after a decade of

planning

 and nearly three years of

construction

 in Iqaluit.


“It’s been a long time coming for Inuit. Inuit have been struggling for a very long time,” Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. President Gloria Uluqsi said in an interview, her voice breaking with emotion.


“It’s a celebration among all Inuit in Nunavut and in Canada. We’re making this history. This is for Inuit, by Inuit, and we should continuously support each other.”


More than 300 people attended the event.


Several elders, including qulliq-lighter Elisapi Aningmiuq, took part in the ceremony.


The Inuksuk Drum Dancers performed.


Health Minister Janet Brewster led a moment of silence to remember those who struggled and are no longer here.


“Many of us have experienced these challenges ourselves or have watched people who have struggled to find care and support,” she said.


The centre represents lessons learned from those lost to addiction, those who have survived, and elders and professionals who can help guide a path forward, she said.


MP Lori Idlout spoke about the need for community-wide healing from intergenerational trauma, seeming to hold back tears.


Members of the culture and lived experiences advisory committee join with MP Lori Idlout, Kitikmeot Inuit Association executive director Paul Emingak, and NTI president Gloria Uluqsi to cut the sealskin ribbon at the open house for the Aqqusariaq Recovery Centre (Photo By Lilli Akpaleeapik)


Community members also had the opportunity to tour the facility and learn about the planning, design and cultural considerations that shaped its development.


The new 24-bed facility has space for inpatient addictions and trauma recovery services, including counselling, on-the-land healing camps, and aftercare, to Nunavummiut coming through its doors for help.


The Government of Nunavut will cover the delivery cost of the centre’s services with $9.7 million in ongoing annual operational funding from Indigenous Services Canada.


The centre is at the end of Akausigiarvik Road, which means “to feel better road,” named by

Iqaluit elders

. It is located across from the Arctic Winter Games Arena along the road to Apex.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Manitoba group needs $17M to bring 3,000 Indigenous artefacts home
content:
A Manitoba-based organization is trying to raise $17 million to bring 3,000 Indigenous artefacts home from Switzerland.

“It doesn’t matter what tribe you’re from, it’s important that our people come together to bring these home to our Nations,” said Karl Stone, spiritual advisor of the group Return the Sacred. “And have these stored in a place where they can be kept for our own medicine people, within our own communities.

Return the Sacred, formerly called the Bringing Them Home Project, is a grassroots organization formed in 2025.

“That’s the way these sacred bundles should be taken care of, I believe. And these sacred bundles should be taught to the next generation.”

The group, headed by executive director Coleen Rajotte, returned from a week-long trip to Switzerland Thursday and held a news conference in Winnipeg.

Since June 2025, the group has been in communication with a private collector, Vincent Escriba, who ran the Indian Land Museum in Gossau, Switzerland.

The museum contained over 5,000 artefacts from North and South America, as well as several countries in Africa. They’re all part of Escriba’s private collection, which he has been growing for the majority of his adult life.

“He is actually a kind, gentle person,” Rajotte said. “He became enamoured with Indigenous people and Indigenous culture.”

She said he “spent his entire life travelling to North America,” 50 trips overall, collecting the items and purchasing other private collections in full.

“That’s how he’s collected such a vast quality,” she said. “We do believe him that he wants to work with us,” she said. “He’s now 70 years old, he’s put all his energy and all his money into this collection, and now he wants to sell it back.”

The Indian Land Museum closed in December 2025, when Escriba decided to retire. Since then, the artefacts have been stored in boxes in a private warehouse, awaiting sale.

Prior to its closure, the chief of Pikangikum First Nation, a community located in northern Ontario, had been advised of the collection’s fate. The chief told Gerald Neufeld, a long-time researcher based in Winnipeg, who created the group in an effort to bring the artefacts home.

The collection includes headdresses, unopened medicine bags, medicine and corn husk masks, pipes, totem poles, canoes, and several other types of artefacts that carry spiritual and cultural weight, Rajotte said.

Escriba also owns several boxes of textbooks, both in English and German.

Over several days, the group met with Escriba and took hundreds of photos of descriptions, contained in stacks of binders, which identified each object, along with its origin, in German.

They have not been able to confirm when all of the artefacts were made, but estimate most left Canada between 1840 and 1860.

Similarly, Rajotte said she is still working to figure out what came from where, but has so far been able to confirm several objects were from Nations in southern Alberta and North Dakota.

They also negotiated with Escriba and determined how much it would cost to purchase the items and return them to North America: $14.5 million, as well as an additional $3 million to cover transportation and handling of the items.

“Of course, there’s lots of opinions,” Rajotte said about Escriba’s decision to sell, rather than donate, the items back to the Nations they originally came from.

In California, she continued, the California Native American Graves Protection and Repatriation Act requires that all state-funded agencies, museums and universities must return any Indigenous cultural items, without a cost, by law.

However, even if the same laws existed in Canada, the situation with Escriba would be different, Rajotte said, due to his collection being private.

She said they are planning to negotiate with Escriba about lowering the price, or a long-term payment plan, but she doesn’t believe he’ll budge when it comes to the bill.

However, he has extended the sale’s deadline, which was originally set for payment by the end of December 2026.

Rajotte said she predicts it will take “at least” a year to appraise, document and pay for the entire collection.

So far, Heritage Canada has covered the initial trip to Switzerland, but there have been no additional conversations with public or private funders regarding the price of the collection itself.

“Our peoples’ sacred belongings that are in museums all over the world should be returned to the original people of this true land,” Stone said …

author: David Swanson
title: Reflections on Testimonies of Korean Victims of the U.S. Atomic Bombs for the International People’s Tribunal for the Victims of the 1945 U.S. Atomic Bombings
content:
By U.S. Army Colonel (Retired) Ann Wright, World BEYOND War, November 14, 2026


First, an Apology from a United States Citizen


My name is Ann Wright.  I served 29 years in the U.S. Army and retired as a Colonel. I was also a U.S. diplomat for 16 years.  I resigned in 2003, 23 years ago in opposition to the Bush war on Iraq.


I was invited to share my reflections on the testimonies of the Korean victims of the U.S. Atomic Bombs for the International People’s Tribunal for the Korean Victims of the 1945 U.S. Atomic Bombings


First, as a U.S. Army Colonel (Ret) and a former U.S. diplomat and as a citizen of the United States, I want to give my deepest apology to the Korean victims of the U.S. atomic bombing of Hiroshima and Nagasaki on August 6 and 9, 1945. I am wearing a shirt that says “I apologize to the Korean victims of the Atomic Bombs.”


I have previously given in other conferences my apology to Japanese victims of the atomic bombs, but this is the first time I have been able to give my apologies to Korean victims and survivors and the victims as well as to the survivors of many other countries who were in both cities when the U.S. dropped the two atomic bombs on them in August 1945.


Today we were honored at the Tribunal with the remarkable presentation at the opening session  with a reenactment of the difficult life of Kim Hyung-ryul, a second-generation Korean victim of the 1945 atomic bombings, who brought the issue of genetic transfer of radiation effects to the international arena.


photo by Ann Wright


poster held by Father of Kim Hyeong Yul at the United Nations


Testimonies of Korean atomic bomb survivors


photo of Korean Survivors of Atomic Bombs. Photo by Ann Wright


Then later today, what we heard today from First-Generation Korean victims Jeong-sun Park, So-sa Jeon, Yun-gyu Park, Jin-tae Shim and Kee-youl Lee and from Second Generation victims Hyeong-yul Kim, represented by his family, and Jeong-sun Han underscored the horrific physical and emotional injuries of first and second generations that for decades went undiagnosed and untreated by the medical profession and largely ignored by the United States, Japanese and Korean governments.


The oral and written testimonies of Korean survivors of the atomic bombs and second-generation survivors are heartbreaking and demonstrate that the harm caused by the atomic bombings in 1945 is by no means an event confined to the past but has continued for 81 years.


The continuing reality of nuclear harm across generations also reveals the long-term and intergenerational consequences left by the use of nuclear weapons and the question of responsibility and accountability.


The Korean hibakusha, the Korean survivors of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, have campaigned for recognition, compensation and medical support for decades and to this day the response of the authorities has been inadequate.


The U.S. is Responsible for War Crimes: Atomic Bombs and Fire-Bombing of Japanese Cities


81 years after the dropping of the atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki in August 1945, there is still a debate in the United States and other nuclear weapons countries concerning the ethical and legal justification for the bombings.


Supporters of the use of the atomic bombs, mainly in the government of the United States even 8 decades later, argue that the atomic bombings were necessary to bring an end to the war with Japan that would prevent a greater loss of life on both sides than an invasion of the Japanese mainland would have caused..


Critics of the use of the atomic bombs argue that the bombings were unnecessary for the war’s end and were a war crime, raising moral and ethical implications of specifically testing the bombs to determine their effects on the human body.


I firmly believe that the use of atomic weapons on those in Hiroshima and Nagasaki was a war crime.


The callous attitude of the government of the United States in dropping the atomic bombs to test their effects on humans was a war crime, as were the fire-bombings of Tokyo and 64 other cities in Japan.  Over 100,000 persons were killed in one night in the U.S. firebombing of Tokyo.


The World War 2 Target Committee of the U.S. identified five cities that could be the targets of the atomic bombs, cities that were largely untouched during the nightly U.S. bombing raids on the major cities of Japan.


The Army Air Forces agreed to leave Hiroshima and Nagasaki off the fire-bombing target list so …

Συγκεντρώσεις αλληλεγγύης στη 12χρονη επιζώσα του Κολωνού ενόψει Εφετείου


>Μικροφωνική – συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στη 12χρονη επιζώσα, υπόθεση Κολωνού


ΣΥΛΛΟΓΟΣ ΕΚΠΑΙΔΕΥΤΙΚΩΝ Π.Ε. «Ο ΑΡΙΣΤΟΤΕΛΗΣ»


Ξεκινά το εφετείο της πρώτης δίκης της υπόθεσης παιδοβιασμού και εμπορίας ανθρώπου στον Κολωνό. Σάββατο 14/11 μικροφωνική – συγκέντρωση στις 12:30/ Δευτέρα 16/11 συγκέντρωση στο Εφετείο στη Λουκάρεως στις 09:00


Στις 16 Νοεμβρίου ξεκινά σε δεύτερο βαθμό η δίκη της δυσώδους υπόθεσης παιδοβιασμού και εμπορίας της 12χρονης τότε, μαθήτριας από τον Κολωνό.

Έχουν περάσει 4 χρόνια από τον Οκτώβριο του 2022 όταν και αποκαλύφθηκε η φρίκη.

 Η μαθήτρια φοιτούσε σε σχολείο του Κολωνού, περιοχή που καλύπτει το σωματείο μας, ενώ τα δύο μικρότερα παιδιά της οικογένειας εξακολουθούν να φοιτούν σε σχολείο της περιοχής.


Από την πρώτη στιγμή συμμετείχαμε

 και εξακολουθούμε να συμμετέχουμε μαζί με τη Λαϊκή Συνέλευση Κολωνού, Σεπολίων, Ακ. Πλάτωνα, φεμινιστικές οργανώσεις και πολιτικές συλλογικότητες

στην «επιτροπή αλληλεγγύης στη 12χρονη»

 δημιουργώντας ένα δίχτυ προστασίας για να μπορέσουμε να υπερασπιστούμε αυτό το παιδί.


Αρχικά το εφετείο ήταν να ξεκινήσει τον Ιανουάριο του 2026,

 ωστόσο είχε αναβληθεί.

Πρωτόδικα, τον Μάρτιο του 2024, το δικαστήριο έκρινε ένοχο τον Ηλία Μίχο

 για βιασμό, μαστροπεία, κατάχρηση, πορνογραφία και εμπορία ανήλικου, παράνομη κατοχή όπλων και πυρομαχικών, ενώ αθωώθηκε για το αδίκημα της εμπορίας ανθρώπων.

Ένοχοι κρίθηκαν οι 19 από τους 24 κατηγορούμενους, μεταξύ των οποίων ο 57χρονος «Μιχάλης»

, για διακεκριμένη μαστροπεία και άλλα αδικήματα, καθώς προωθούσε σε τρίτους πορνογραφικό υλικό και διευκόλυνε την περαιτέρω έκθεση της 12χρονης στην πορνεία.

Περαιτέρω έρευνα του κυκλώματος εμπορίας ανθρώπων

 για τη σύνδεσή του με αυτό της Ηλιούπολης (υπόθεση Αμαρρυλίς) και της Greek Police Mafia, όπως θα όριζαν οι συνδέσεις που προέκυψαν,

δεν έγινε!


Η μητέρα κηρύχθηκε αθώα για τις βασικές κατηγορίες της διακεκριμένης μαστροπείας και της διακεκριμένης περίπτωσης πορνογραφίας ανηλίκου με τις ψήφους των 4 ενόρκων

, σε αντίθεση με τους 3 τακτικούς δικαστές, που συντάχθηκαν με την εισαγγελική πρόταση, και αποφυλακίστηκε μετά από ενάμιση χρόνο καταχρηστικής προφυλάκισης στον Κορυδαλλό!

Η επιζώσα μαθήτρια, τα αδέρφια της και το κίνημα αλληλεγγύης από την αρχή φώναζαν για την αθωότητά της.


Ενόψει του εφετείου που ξεκινάει, ο βασικός κατηγορούμενος Ηλίας Μίχος (με διασυνδέσεις όπως αποκαλύφθηκε με τη ΝΔ, την εκκλησία και το ΑΤ της περιοχής) και πολλοί από τους δράστες, θα προσπαθήσουν να αποδείξουν την αθωότητά τους και να απαλλαγούν από τις κατηγορίες που τους αποδόθηκαν, μετακυλίοντας και πάλι την ευθύνη στην οικογένεια και ειδικά στη μητέρα. Γεγονός είναι πως όταν η μητέρα κατήγγειλε τη σεξουαλική εκμετάλλευση του παιδιού στο ΑΤ Κολωνού εκδιώχθηκε αδικαιολόγητα, ενώ ο Μίχος συνελήφθη 40 μέρες μετά την καταγγελία.


Η απαλλαγή του Μίχου πρωτόδικα από την κατηγορία της εμπορίας, όπως και η εισαγγελική προσφυγή και η αμφισβήτηση της πρωτόδικης απόφασης που αθώωσε τη μάνα του κοριτσιού, φανερώνουν πως

η αστική δικαιοσύνη είναι βαθιά ταξική και πατριαρχική και πως το σύστημα συγκάλυψης δεν ανέχεται καμία παρέμβαση από το κίνημα αλληλεγγύης.


Απεναντίας, εξυπηρετώντας αταλάντευτα την αρχική γραμμή συγκάλυψης με σκοπό να αποκρυφτεί η εμπορία παιδιών και να αθωωθούν ο Μίχος και οι βιαστές-μαστροποί,

χρειάζονται την ενοχή της μάνας ως αντίβαρο στο εφετείο.


Το κρατικό, αστυνομικό και δικαστικό σύστημα και τα κυκλώματα μαφίας ενεργοποιούνται ξανά απέναντι στην κοινωνία.

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Narwhal, seals and more adorn University of Ottawa wall
content:
Aija Komangapik painted a grey seal as part of a mural project at the University of Ottawa because it is an animal she knows well.


Cyclists ride past as Inuk artist Aija Komangapik looks at a new collaborative mural along a bike pathway at the University of Ottawa in Ottawa on Nov. 5. Komangapik was one of five Indigenous artists from across Canada who painted sections of the campus project. (Photo by Nehaa Bimal)


“The grey seal is the one I catch, the one I use to prepare sealskins. It’s the one I hunt to provide people with meat,” said the 28-year-old artist and hunter.


She included the animal in her section of a new mural on the wall beside the university’s train station entrance, which also serves as a bike pathway.


Her section begins with a painting of the sea goddess Sedna’s severed fingers, which then leads to illustrations of a blue whale, a two-tusk narwhal, a beluga whale, a walrus and seals.


“The creation for all the animals starts in the ocean, and for Inuit, it starts with Sedna,” she said on Nov. 5, while standing in front of the mural as cyclists sped past.


Komangapik, who was born in Iqaluit but now lives in Ottawa, began hunting on the water in her 20s, after she moved down south when she was 12.


“I’ve been feeling very close to my culture again and hunting has really helping me get back in touch with myself,” she said. 


The mural features Algonquin artist Miskomin Twenish of Kitigan Zibi Anishinabeg, Métis artist Bre Quirion of Manitoba, Cree artist Chris Chipak of Red Pheasant Cree Nation, and Kanien’kehá:ka artist Victoria Ransom of Akwesasne First Nation.


Each artist’s territory is represented in different sections, which, taken together, show water moving from the ocean to rivers, across the plains and toward the mountains, said Komangapik. 


“It made for a more cohesive, more beautiful art piece as we were playing with each other’s colours and speaking with each other as artists,” she said.


“The mural gives off a similar feeling because of it.”


The university’s Office of Indigenous Affairs organized the mural. The project grew out of an earlier effort to recognize Indigenous languages and cultures on campus, said

Tareyn Johnson, director the office, in an interview.


A sign near the bike pathway in 2019 that had greetings in five Indigenous languages, including Inuktitut, was

repeatedly being vandalized, Johnson said. 


Instead of fixing the damages, administrators reimagined how to enliven the alley-like area.


“Beautifying these spaces is a way of reclaiming land on campus,” Johnson said.


The mural was mostly completed in October. One section, which will feature Komangapik’s painting of Sedna, remains unfinished because that wall is owned by the City of Ottawa.


The university is awaiting approval to complete the work, likely next spring or summer.


“What I appreciate most is that the artists worked together to create something harmonious while still allowing for different contrasts and styles,” Johnson said.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Conadu Histórica de paro en defensa de los salarios y la Universidad Pública
content:
Ayer empezó una semana de paro docente universitario convocada por Conadu Histórica contra el incumplimiento de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario por parte del Gobierno.


Así lo resolvió CONADU HISTÓRICA en su Congreso Extraordinario realizado el pasado 6 de noviembre para deliberar sobre el plan de acción gremial en el último tramo del año y resolver las medidas que emergen de las asambleas y diferentes consultas en todo el país.


Ochenta y un congresalas y congresales de las asociaciones de base de todo el país resolvieron por unanimidad dar continuidad el plan nacional de acción gremial, poner en consulta nacional la afectación de los exámenes en diciembre y comenzar la discusión de las medidas para el inicio del 2027 si el Gobierno Nacional sigue incumplimiendo la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario.


El Congreso resolvió por amplia mayoría sostener un paro de una semana, del 12 al 18 de noviembre de 2026, y por unanimidad un paro de 24 horas el día en que se trate el Presupuesto 2027 en el Congreso de la Nación.


La Federación exige el cumplimiento efectivo de la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario y el pago de la deuda salarial que el Estado nacional mantiene con la docencia universitaria y preuniversitaria, en abierto incumplimiento de la medida cautelar dictada por la Justicia.


El Congreso rechazó por insuficiente el proyecto de Presupuesto 2027 presentado por el Poder Ejecutivo Nacional y reclama una asignación presupuestaria que respete la Ley de Financiamiento Universitario


Por otra parte, el jueves 5 de noviembre sesionó el Congreso Ordinario de la Federación que aprobó por amplia mayoría la Memoria y el Balance correspondientes al período comprendido entre el 1 de julio de 2025 y el 30 de junio de 2026.


Ambos congresos sesionaron bajo las presidencias honorarias de Patricia Walsh, hija de Rodolfo Walsh, exdiputada nacional y luchadora incansable contra la impunidad de los responsables de los crímenes de lesa humanidad cometidos durante la última dictadura cívico-militar, y de Elsa Pavón, Abuela de Plaza de Mayo y protagonista de la lucha por la restitución de la identidad de las nietas y los nietos apropiados durante el terrorismo de Estado.


CONADU HISTÓRICA reafirmó su compromiso con la defensa de los derechos de la docencia universitaria y preuniversitaria, la universidad pública y la continuidad de la lucha colectiva. Frente a la profundización del ataque del gobierno de Milei a la clase trabajadora, a nuestro sustento salarial, al ahogamiento presupuestario de las universidades públicas, el congelamiento de las becas estudiantiles reivindicamos la capacidad y disponibilidad de la docencia universitaria y preuniversitaria para sostener esta persistente lucha en unidad y con organización.


¡La Ley de Financiamiento Universitario se cumple!


¡Por salarios dignos, presupuesto y universidad pública!

author: David Swanson
title: Ukrainian Pacifist and WBW Board Member Yurii Sheliazhenko’s Trial Postponed in Kyiv
content:
Photo by Mauro Zanella


By

Pressenza

, November 14, 2026


On November 11

th

  2026 the Pechersk District Court of Kyiv conducted a hearing in the criminal case of Ukrainian Quaker and pacifist Yurii Sheliazhenko, accused of justification of Russian aggression in a pacifist statement that condemned the invasion and called for nonviolent resistance.


The crime is punishable with 5 years of prison with possible confiscation of property according to Article 436-2 (2) of the Criminal Code of Ukraine.


Judge Anna Gridasova denied consideration of requests, including a request to delete from the website of the Security Service of Ukraine a publication saying that Yurii Sheliazhenko is a criminal and enemy’s agitator, in violation of right to presumption of innocence.


In 2022, Yurii Sheliazhenko sent to the President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy a statement called “Peace Agenda for Ukraine and the World”, asking to end the war by peaceful means and to protect human right to conscientious objection to military service. In 2023 his house was searched, mobile phone and computer seized, he was accused in justification of Russian aggression on the ground of sending the statement and held in house arrest until February 2024.


The statement explicitly supports condemnation of Russian aggression against Ukraine by the United Nations General Assembly and calls to resist war by nonviolent and unarmed methods.


“The accusation is based on linguistic expert conclusion alleging that pacifists shift blame from Russia saying that tragic mistakes were made on both sides of the conflict and that demonized enemy with whom it is impossible negotiate is a myth. I have another conclusion of licensed forensic linguists, one with academic degree, saying there is no justification of Russian aggression in the statement and actually it condemns Russian aggression” says Yurii.


Amnesty International in 2023 report mentioned Yurii’s case and suggested that Article 436-2 of the Criminal Code of Ukraine is a threat to freedom of speech.


Yurii explains that the article was introduced to stop widespread Russian propaganda of war based on narratives that Putin voiced on his February 24

th

 2022 speech when he invaded Ukraine.


“Any propaganda of aggressive war indeed should be prohibited by law, as the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights envisions. So I understand the reasons of our lawmakers, but they adopted a vague law allowing to persecute for pacifism, including as a pretext to stop advocacy of right to conscientious objection, especially in atmosphere of weak procedural safeguards and strategic communications of the national defense sector demonizing pacifists. This saying, I wish we could overcome lies with popular literacy and ability to discuss different ideas, dismissing falsehoods and immorality typical to propaganda of war. I don’t support state suppression of freedom of speech, exept some reasonable safeguards against clear and dangerous lies, not leaving space for discussion and fact-checking and creating immediate harm, like the panic in crowded place after false fire alert”, explains Yurii.


In Yurii’s view, Kremlin’s information warfare, along with other forms of warfare, should be resisted nonviolently, by peaceful communication and civil disobedience: “Putin’s justifications of his brutal unjustifiable war of conquest upon my country are false, though they were tailored to appeal some mindsets and discourses in certain circles of the East and West. Post-Soviet people of old age were taught in compulsory education system that Russians and Ukrainians are one people, and those in the West who followed Soviet official discourse of Cold War era also used to this idea being not aware that it serves assimilation of Ukrainians and imperial ambitions of Moscow. Non-interventionists in the United States used to blame their own government in every war and regime change, exaggerating to a degree of history-making a background role of covert operations that ride the wave of political trends. They are ready to deny Ukrainians in agency and independence, accepting Putin’s arrogant claim he was provoked to invade Ukraine by security arrangements of Western countries, including Ukraine.
