author: Anonyme Anarchist*innen
title: 20. November: Schulstreik – Generalstreik – Aufstand!
content:
Endlich kommt es zu großen Demonstrationen und Revolten. Mit der Jugend ganz vorne gehen in Frankreich, Belgien, Albanien, Italien und Spanien die Menschen in Massen auf die Straße. In den letzten Jahren ist nochmal ganz klar geworden, dass dieses kapitalistische System uns nichts zu bieten hat. Lockdowns, Krieg, Genozid, Waffenproduktion, Arbeitszwang, Armut sind dazu da, uns auszubeuten und die Reichen reicher zu machen und die Mächtigen mächtiger. Viel zu lange war es still in Europa, waren wir überfordert mit der ganzen Scheiße, die uns täglich vorgesetzt wird.


Auch hier in Deutschland haben die Proteste gegen die Wehrpflicht über das Jahr regelmäßig tausende von Leuten auf die Straße gebracht. Und jetzt gibt es die ersten Schulbesetzungen, die ersten militanten Demos und Aktionen, die sich an denen in Frankreich orientieren. Worum es geht ist klar: in Opposition zu diesem System zu gehen, dass uns gegeneinander ausspielt und ins Verderben jagt. Statt dessen solidarisch und selbstbestimmt leben. Wir brauchen keinen Staat und keine Herrscher. Wir brauchen eine Bewegung von unten.


Was als Schülerprotest begonnen hat, hat sich zu einer generellen Revolte entwickelt. Politik und Massenmedien wollen das hier in Deutschland verhindern, denn sie haben Angst um ihre Macht und ihr Geld. Es wird gehetzt. Gegen Migrant*innen. Gegen Erwachsene, die sich den Schülern anschließen. Gegen angebliche Extremist*innen.


Damit wollen sie uns gegeneinander aufbringen und eine generelle Revolte verhindern. Doch das soll nicht klappen!


Am 20. November wird es wieder einen bundesweiten Schulstreik geben und Europaweit ist zu Demonstrationen und Aktionen aufgerufen. Machen wir diesen Tag zu einem generellen Streik- und Kampftag! Lasst uns die Flamme der Revolte endlich auch hier entzünden! Gemeinsam können wir den Kapitalismus besiegen und uns zurückholen was sie uns geklaut haben, was uns aber immernoch gehört: unsere Straßen, unsere Viertel, die Kontrolle über unsere Leben und damit die Freiheit.


Am 20. November: alle auf die Straße!


Macht Pläne! Achtet auf Ankündigungen! Achtet aufeinander!

title: İstanbul'da bazı vapur seferleri lodos nedeniyle iptal edildi
content:
Fotoğraf: Hüma H. Yardım/Unsplash

İstanbul - Meteoroloji Genel Müdürlüğü'nün uyarılarının ardından dün etkisini göstermeye başlayan lodos, bugün İstanbul'da şiddetini artırdı. Kuvvetli rüzgar nedeniyle deniz ulaşımında aksamalar yaşandı.

İDO tarafından yapılan duyuruda, olumsuz hava koşulları nedeniyle; Yenikapı-Yalova 09.45, Yalova-Yenikapı 09.45, Kadıköy-Yenikapı-Bandırma 11.30, Yenikapı-Yalova 11.45, Yalova-Yenikapı 11.45, Bursa-Armutlu-Yenikapı-Kadıköy 12.30 ve Kadıköy-Yenikapı-Armutlu Tatil Köyü-Armutlu-Bursa 14.50 seferlerinin iptal edildiği bildirildi.

Şehir Hatları'ndan yapılan açıklamada ise elverişsiz hava koşulları nedeniyle ikinci bir duyuruya kadar Bostancı-Moda-Karaköy-Kabataş, Büyükada-Sedef Adası, Maltepe-Büyükada-Heybeliada-Burgazada-Kınalıada, Beşiktaş-Adalar, Anadolu Kavağı-Rumeli Kavağı-Sarıyer, Sarıyer-Beykoz ve Bostancı-Adalar Ring hatlarındaki seferlerin gerçekleştirilemeyeceği belirtildi. Ayrıca 10.05 Kabataş-Kadıköy-Adalar seferinin de iptal edildiği duyuruldu.

title: Lula mohra xwe li roja çaremîn a COP31ê da
content:
Lûtkeya Rêberan a ku du rojan di civîna COP31ê ya li Antalyayê de domiya, bi dawî bû. Serokdewletê Brezîlyayê Lula da Silva mohra xwe li roja duyemîn a Lûtkeya Rêberan da. 


Lula di saetên êvarê de li salona duyemîn a mezin a desteya giştî ya bi navê Deryaya Spî (Akdeniz), bi nûnerên rêxistinên civaka sivîl ên Brezîlyayê re civiya û li Antalyayê hema bêje pîrozbahiyeke hilbijartinê jî li dar xist. Gotinên Lula û axaftvanên din gelek caran bi dirûşmeyan hatin birîn.


Roja dawî ya Lûtkeya Rêberan


12 Mijdar 2026


Şandeya Brezîlyayê di saetên sibehê de jî civîneke bi heman rengî li dar xistibû. Brezîlyaya ku salek berê li Belemê mazûvaniya civîna COP30yê kiribû, li Antalyayê derbarê armanca devjêberdana sotemeniyên fosîl (petrol, komir û gaz) de nexşerêyek ragihand û bang li welatên din kir ku vê pêvajoya ku bi salan e tê paşxistin, bileztir bikin. 


Serok Lula jî di axaftina xwe ya di civîna êvarê de got ku Brezîlya dê di parastina jîngehê de bibe welatê herî baş û bal kişand ser nexşerêyê. Her wiha Lula behsa wê yekê jî kir ku di COP15a li Kopenhagê de bi Serokê berê yê DYAyê Barack Obama û Serokdewletê Çînê Wen Jiabao re axiviye û çawa alî razî kirine ku salane 100 milyar dolar bidin welatên di pêvajoya pêşketinê de ne.


Di saetên sibehê de çalakvana avhewayê Greta Thunberg, damezrînerê Enstîtuya Filistînê ya ji bo Stratejiya Avhewayê Mohammad Usrof, nûnera civakên herêmî yên ji Awistralyayê Rikki Dank û Celine Isimbi ya ji Rwandayê bi hev re civîneke çapemeniyê li dar xistin. 


Tevî akredîtasyonê jî çapemenî di Lûtkeya Rêberan a COP31ê de hat sînordarkirin


11 Mijdar 2026


Greta Thunbergê di axaftina xwe ya vekirinê de bi van gotinan dest pê kir: “Em hemû li vir in ji ber ku em dizanin krîza avhewayê heye û ev êdî bûye meseleya jiyan û mirinê.”


Thunbergê diyar kir ku gavên ku kesên li vir desthilatdar in davêjin, bi temamî ji rastiyê dûr in û got ku em can, ekosîstem û cureyên biqîmet ên ku dê careke din qet venegerin, winda dikin. Thunbergê weha got;

“Krîza avhewayê krîzeke bêedaletiyê ye ku kesên herî kêm berpirsiyarê vê krîzê ne, bi awayê herî dijwar û herî bilez jê bandor dibin”

 û destnîşan kir ku petrola ku ji Tirkiyeyê diçe Îsraîlê qirkirinê gur dike û xwest ku Tirkiye ambargoya enerjiyê deyne ser Îsraîlê. Mohammed Usrof jî di axaftina xwe de got ku baranên beriya hefteyekê 70 hezar malbat ji cih û warên wan kirine û wiha li axavtina zêde kir:


“Ji ber ku hemû di konên pînekirî û rizyayî de dijîn. Hefteya borî li Şerîaya Rojava di demekê de ku 3 hezar Filistînî ji cihên xwe dihatin koçberkirin, bi dehan kesan jiyana xwe ji dest da. Û tekane sedema vê yekê, encamên qirkirina ku bi piştgiriya DYA û Îngilîstanê û bi beşdariya petrola Tirkiyeyê ji aliyê artêşa Îsraîlê ve tê meşandin e. Ji ber vê yekê petrola Tirkiyeyê, ligel komira Kolombiya û Afrîkaya Başûr ku rasterast ji tora elektrîkê û sîstema leşkerî ya Îsraîlê re tê veguhestin, hêzê dide qirkirinê ku Îsraîlê didomîne.”


Tirkiyeyê di roja çaremîn a COP31ê de îmze avêt bin peymanên enerjiyê. Wezîrê Enerjiyê Alparslan Bayraktar bi rayedarên Komara Gel a Çînê re peymannameyeke lihevkirinê ya bi bihayê 15 milyar dolarî îmze kir ku santralên ba û rojê, tesîsên depokirina elektrîkê û xetên veguhastinê li xwe digire. Bi şîrketa AtkinsRealis a Kanadayê re jî ji bo lêkolîna pêkanbûnê (fîzîbîlîte) ya santraleke nukleerî ku dê ji 6 reaktoran pêk bê û bi giştî xwedî hêza 4500 megawatan be,peyman hat îmzekirin. Her wiha bi şîrketa ACWA ya Erebistana Siûdî re jî ji bo fînansekirina santrala rojê ya 2 hezar megawatî ya ku di encama peymana berê de avakirina wê dihat plankirin, îmze hatin avêtin.


Serokwezîrê Brîtanyayê Andy Burnham jî hat Antalyayê û raporeke bi navê Nexşerêya Elektrîkîkirina Paqij a welatê xwe eşkere kir. Rapor ji aliyê rêxistinên jîngehê ve hat rexnekirin ji ber ku nehatiye diyarkirin ka dê elektrîk ji kîjan çavkaniyan bê hilberandin û hat destnîşankirin ku divê hilberîna elektrîkê tenê ji çavkaniyên enerjiya nûjenbar bê kirin.


Greenpeaceya ku berê li Qada Şîn (Blue Zone) a ku muzakere lê didomin enstalasyonek vekiribû û nîşan dabû ku sotemeniyên fosîl berpirsiyarê germbûna 1,5 pileyî ne, dê roja Înê 13ê Çiriya Paşiyê ya 2026an jî li ber Şaredariya Konyaaltiyê peykerekî hespê Troyayê yê şeş metre bilind veke.


Şopînerê Çalakiya Avhewayê (Climate Action Tracker) dê di civîna çapemeniyê ya ku îro (13ê Çiriya Paşiyê) li dar bixe de, xebata xwe ya dawî ya ku hesab dike ka sozên heyî yên hikûmetan dê cîhanê ber bi germbûneke çend pileyî …

title: COP Bike Ride: 2 binden fazla bisikletçi, 20 bin kilometre yol kat etti
content:
COP Bike Ride, ulaşım kaynaklı karbon emisyonlarının azaltılmasında bisikletin daha etkin bir ulaşım aracı olarak kullanılmasını savunan, dünya çapında yurttaşların inisiyatifiyle oluşmuş uluslararası bir bisiklet topluluğu.


İstanbul’da buluştuğumuz COP Bike Ride ekibi şimdi Antalya’da.


COP30’un yapıldığı Brezilya Belém’den yola çıktılar, sıfır fosil yakıt tüketerek yelkenliyle okyanusu geçtiler ve bugün Antalya’dayız. 2 bin 200’den fazla bisikletçi rotaya katıldı, yaklaşık 20 bin kilometre yol bisikletle kat edilmiş oldu. Sadece Türkiye’de bin 300 kilometreyi kat ettik bisikletlerimizle. –

 Nihan Lafcı


Bisikleti iklim dostu ulaşımın temel unsurlarından biri haline getirmeyi amaçlayan topluluk, 10 maddelik talep listesini COP31 Başkanı Murat Kurum’a ulaştırmaya çalışıyor.


COP Bike Ride Türkiye Koordinatörü Nihan Lafcı ile bu kez COP31 alanında buluştuk; Brezilya’dan İstanbul’a uzanan yolculuğu ve bu süreçte edindikleri deneyimleri konuştuk.


COP Bike Ride’dan 10 talep


Ekip, 10 Ekim’de Kadıköy’de düzenlediği basın açıklamasında karar vericilere yönelik 10 talebini kamuoyuyla paylaşmıştı:


2030’a kadar, özellikle şehirlerarası ve günlük yolculuklar için çok modlu bağlantıyı da içeren temel bir bisiklet yolu ağı oluşturun. Temel zaten mevcutsa, daha iddialı olun!


Hem hızı hem de araç sayısını sınırlayarak araç trafiğini azaltın.


2030’a kadar bisiklet kullanımını geliştirmeye yönelik, tüm olanakları kapsayan özel planlar tasarlayın! (Bu planlar, özel bütçeyle desteklenmeli ve bisiklet topluluklarının da dahil olduğu düzenli uygulama inceleme süreçlerini içermeli.)


Okulların, toplu taşıma merkezlerinin, yerel işletmelerin ve yeşil alanların yakınında bisiklet ve yaya için ayrılmış alanları 2030’a kadar önemli ölçüde artırın.


2030’a kadar ulaşım merkezlerinde, alışveriş alanlarında (!), okullarda, ofislerde, evlerde (kargo bisikletleri dahil) uygun bisiklet depolama kapasitesini genelleştirin.


Bisiklet sürmeye yönelik bir zaman ve mekan yaratın: geniş bir kitleye hitap etmek için her yıl düzenlenen büyük bir bisiklet etkinliği + bisiklet tamiri, eğitimi, buluşması gibi etkinliklerin düzenleneceği bir “bisiklet evi”...


Özellikle 12 yaş altı çocuklar ve kadınlar için daha iyi bisiklet sürüş ve güçlendirme konusunda eğitim; bisikletin finansal faydalarının tanıtımı.


İlgili ekonomik sektörü (imalat, tamir, bisiklet turizmi, kiralama, paylaşım vb.) özel vergi teşvikleri/destekler yoluyla geliştirin.


“Son kilometre” teslimatları için kargo bisikleti lojistiği geliştirin.


Kaza oranları, memnuniyet anketleri, ayrılmış bisiklet ağı uzunluğu ve ulaşım türlerinin dağılımı gibi göstergeleri düzenli olarak ölçüp izleyerek kamuoyuyla paylaşın.

author: Daniel Avalos
title: Iglesia y Estado: una separación que todavía se reclama en la calle
content:
La consigna apareció este miércoles en la movilización de jubilados. La reciente visita del papa León XIV volvió a poner en escena el vínculo entre el poder político y la Iglesia católica, una relación que también se expresa en el presupuesto público.


La visita del papa León XIV terminó, pero la discusión sobre el vínculo entre la Iglesia y el Estado sigue abierta. En la movilización de los jubilados, volvió a aparecer un pedido que lleva años recorriendo las calles y que aún debe resolverse.


En medio de los reclamos por los derechos de nuestros viejos, la consigna puso sobre la mesa una discusión que suele quedar relegada. No se trata de cuestionar la fe de nadie ni el derecho de las comunidades religiosas a expresarse. La discusión pasa por otro lado: qué relación debe mantener el Estado con una institución religiosa y qué lugar ocupa esa institución en las decisiones y los recursos públicos.La visita del Papa dejó imágenes de cercanía entre las autoridades políticas y la jerarquía católica. Pero ese vínculo no se agota en los encuentros oficiales ni en las ceremonias. También tiene una dimensión económica.


 


El presupuesto nacional sigue contemplando partidas destinadas a la Iglesia católica. Es cierto que el financiamiento directo se redujo en los últimos años. En diciembre de 2023, los obispos renunciaron a las asignaciones mensuales que recibían del Estado. Sin embargo, eso no significó el fin de las transferencias.


Para 2026 se proyectaron 155 millones de pesos destinados a obispados, arzobispados y parroquias, según datos oficiales. También se mantienen mecanismos de asistencia a sacerdotes de zonas de frontera y a seminaristas. A esto se suman otros vínculos económicos que no resultan sencillos de dimensionar: el presupuesto no permite identificar de manera global cuánto dinero público llega a instituciones católicas a través de programas educativos o sociales.


Millones de pesos destinaron la Nación $20.400, CABA que no informó su aporte oficialmente pero que si quedó en la mira por su «carpa vip» con lujos extravagantes , la Provincia de Buenos Aires $12.000 y la Provincia de Córdoba $9.300. La iglesia solo aporto $5.400 que fueron acercados por empresas como Santander, Toyota, Techint, Corporación América y otras.


La discusión, entonces, no pasa por desconocer el trabajo que realizan esas instituciones ni por limitar la libertad religiosa. Pasa por preguntarse por qué una confesión en particular conserva un vínculo de financiamiento y reconocimiento institucional con el Estado, mientras este debe garantizar derechos para una sociedad con distintas creencias y también para quienes no profesan ninguna.


La fiesta de la Iglesia fue pagada casi en su totalidad por un Estado que no reconoce leyes ni atiende necesidades de su pueblo. Por eso el reclamo encontró su lugar en los carteles y las voces de los jubilados.


Hoy más que nunca. Separación de la Iglesia del Estado!

author: Kodao Productions
title: Makabayan solon asks why Sandro’s district is getting biggest 2027 infra allocation
content:
ACT Teachers Representative and Deputy Minority Leader Antonio Tinio called on all fellow legislators who proposed infrastructure allocations in the proposed 2027 national budget to come forward and disclose their projects.


Tinio said that while the passed version of House Bill 10858 mostly arrange infrastructure projects under an agency, often DPWH’s Central Office or one of its 202 District Engineering Offices, proposals may be identified in the legislative districts where they would be built.


“This is precisely the information that the general public wants to know. ‘Anong mga proyekto ng congressman sa aming distrito?’ The public wants full transparency and accountability. Sa kasamaang palad, hindi ito binibigay ng House,” he said.


Tinio’s office reviewed 18,338 line items worth Php 641.3 billion under five categories: 1) DPWH District Engineering Offices, 2) DPWH Central Office, 3) Department of Agriculture farm-to-market roads, 4) DOH health facilities, and 5) NIA irrigation projects.


Of these, it placed 17,059 items, or 93.0 per cent, worth Php 541.7 billion, in specific districts.


Infographic by R. Villanueva/Kodao


Why disclosure is important


Tinio noted the approved House version of the 2027 national budget proposal does not show who the proponents are, even though the rules of the House require that they be disclosed.


A project in a district may have been proposed by its representative, but also by a partylist representative or even another district representative, a senator, or an executive official or agency, the Makabayan solon revealed.


“Nevertheless, certain questions are inevitable: why are there so many projects and such large sums allocated to some districts, while others receive so little?” he asked.


Tinio said it is noteworthy that—considering the overall picture, not just the DPWH allocations, but also including farm-to-market roads, irrigation projects, and health facilities—the total for the 1st District of Ilocos Norte, represented by Rep. Sandro Marcos (House Majority Leader and son of the President), reaches P10.03 billion.


Meanwhile, only P50 million is allocated to the 4th District of Rizal—the lowest amount among the 252 districts that received projects.


“These projects are funded with public money, much of it borrowed, while the public pays for the debt. Every representative, senator and executive official who proposed a project should say so,” Tinio said.


He added it is not enough to know where the funds go; it is also necessary to know who provided them, so that they, too, can be held accountable should any irregularities arise in the implementation of the project.


“We call on the House and the Senate to publish the list of proponents of every line item insertion before the bicameral conference finalizes the budget, and on the DBM, the DPWH, and other agencies to do the same for what they put in the NEP. Let the public see the projects and the names behind them,” he ended. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

author: Fraser Needham
title: ISC minister says she was not expecting Kinew’s comments about abolishing the Indian Act
content:
Indigenous Services Minister Mandy Gull-Masty says she was as surprised as anyone when Manitoba Premier Wab Kinew raised the idea of abolishing the Indian Act last month and was hoping for more information on what role the province would play.

“I think it’s interesting to see somebody who’s a provincial premier wanting to frame up that space,” she said. “Clearly, in his role he would have to indicate his responsibility in the provincial seat and how you would serve those off-reserve community members.

“I think that’s the initiative I was hoping to see as a minister coming out of that space because you have to increase the responsibility, the partnership, the role of the provincial government in the path beyond the Indian Act.”

The idea of getting rid of the Indian Act was raised by Kinew during a press conference at the First Nations First Ministers meeting in Ottawa on Oct. 26.

“What you saw was a spontaneous moment where premier Kinew wanted to speak about status. Wanted to speak about the Indian Act.”

The Indian Act, passed in 1876, continues to govern matters of Indian status, First Nations governance, and reserve lands. The federal government has tried, and failed, to abolish it a number of times in the past 50 years.

At a later press conference, Prime Minister Mark Carney said he was open to the idea as long as it was co-developed with First Nations and has tasked some of his ministers to look into the issue.

He said he was directing Gull-Masty to chart a path with First Nations on amending or abolishing the act.

Conservative MP Billy Morin says the 2026 federal budget is disappointing on a number of levels.

“This might be the most overrated Prime Minister (Mark Carney) I’ve seen in quite some time,” the MP for Edmonton Northwest said. “Even more overrated than his predecessor (Justin Trudeau). This guy’s apparently a banker, a guy who knows how to do finances.

“He’s running deficits bigger than Trudeau. Bigger deficits than Trudeau and he takes great pride in that?”

The budget projects deficits of well over $50 billion over each of the next five years.

The 2023/24 deficit, the last budget under Trudeau, came in at $61.9 billion and the 2026/27 deficit is projected to be $62.3 billion.

Morin is the Indigenous Services critic for the Conservatives.

The president of the Manitoba Métis Federation says leaving Métis people out of the 2026 federal budget is not a mistake the Carney government can afford to make.

“It shouldn’t be something that we need to worry about whether it’s a budget or not,” David Chartrand said. “It should be automatic. It’s part of the fiduciary responsibility and constitutional responsibility of Canada,” he said.

The 2026 budget makes roughly $50 billion over ten years in investments in Indigenous priorities but makes no mention of Métis-specific investments.

Some have expressed fears the government is returning to a non-distinctions-based funding model that largely focuses on First Nations people.

Chartrand said the government collects billions of dollars in taxes from Métis people every year and it needs to invest that money back in their communities.

Fraser spent the last 20 years working in both print and radio in Saskatchewan – mostly in the northern part of the province. Before joining APTN’s Ottawa bureau, he was news director for the Missinipi Broadcasting Corporation working out of their Prince Albert office. He holds a bachelor of arts degree in political science from Carleton University and a diploma of journalism from Algonquin College.

Osvaldo Bayer hoy: rebeldía necesaria para un presente incómodo.

 Del 13 al 19 de noviembre habrá jornadas para revisitar la obra y el legado de este enorme escritor, historiador, periodista de las luchas obreras y anarquismos. Se propone un recorrido por sus múltiples facetas: Bayer como historiador del movimiento obrero, como novelista, periodista y mediador cultural entre Argentina y Alemania. Proyecciones, presentaciones de libros, teatro y mesas de debate.

Por ANRed.

Eduardo Misch

 


Annemarie

A través de su archivo, testimonios familiares y la obra de Heinrich, la directora emprende una búsqueda que trasciende el retrato de una artista para convertirse en una reflexión íntima sobre la memoria, la familia, el paso del tiempo y la propia mirada.  13, 14, 15, 16, 17 y 18 de noviembre a las 19:45 hs en el Gaumont.

Una identidad cultural común entre Argentina y México, una forma de entender la literatura y un modo de habitar la lengua. A partir de libros, fotografías y objetos, la exposición explora la amistad con

Alfonso Reyes

, las coincidencias con

Juan Rulfo

, los viajes a México -en 1973, 1978 y 1981- y las muchas demostraciones de respeto y admiración del pueblo mexicano por Jorge Luis Borges.

author: Administrador
title: CINCO GENERACIONES BUSCANDO A JOSÉ MIGUEL. (Respuesta a las solicitudes de entrevistas)
content:
CINCO GENERACIONES BUSCANDO A JOSÉ MIGUEL. (respuesta a las solicitudes de entrevistas)

Así se llama: José Miguel. José Miguel Rodríguez Rodríguez, tiene 29 años y desapareció el 18 de junio de 2026 en Salamanca, Guanajuato, junto con Wendy Ángela Ruiz Luna y Brisa Johana Flores Luna. Hace casi 6 meses.

Hace unos días les conté cómo, en una plática que daba el SubMoisés a la delegación zapatista -como parte de su preparación-, se señalaba que lo más importante era el desaparecido, la desaparecida. La ausencia, pues. E insistía él, el SubMoy, en que esa desaparición era como un hueco, como un hoyo, como un mordisco en la vida de sus familiares y cercanos. Un vacío que no podía ser llenado más que con la presencia de quien faltaba, es decir, con el encuentro del ausente.

Que no había promesa, rollo político, diligencia fiscal, intervención policíaca o ministerial, marcha, mitin, denuncia, conteo, manta, cartel, canto, estadística, grito que pudiera “acompletar” ese faltante.

Y entonces hacía como que era el desaparecido el que hablaba, el que se dirigía a sus familiares, amistades, cercanos. ¿Qué les decía? Se ponía así en el lugar del faltante y veía que no estaba cabal. Que, así como a sus familiares él les faltaba, también a él le hacía falta su familia, su trabajo, su estudio, su amor, sus amigos, su vida pues. A él, a ella, le habían también arrancado un pedazo suyo, de su ser, y le habían dejado un hueco igual de grande, igual de doloroso, igual de angustiante.

Y que él o ella les gritaba que ahí estaba, detrás de esa puerta, de ese cerco, de esa tierra, de esa cárcel. Y se desesperaba porque su voz no llegaba lejos, se ahogaba por el ruido, se perdía entre otros gritos.

Pero, así como quien le busca espera encontrarle, ella o él esperaba ser encontrado. Eso era y es lo importante. Acompletarse. Y le decía a sus familiares que agarraran fuerza y coraje. Y que gritaran también. Ellos para que les escuchara, él o ella para que le encontraran.

1530 hombres, mujeres, otroas, niños, niñas, de hasta 5 generaciones lo escuchaban en silencio. Había ahí hombres y mujeres de más de 70 años, bisabuelos y bisabuelas, la mayoría veteranos y veteranas del alzamiento en 1994 y de la clandestinidad en que se gestó la guerra contra el olvido.

Adultos mayores de 50, que también salieron a pelear, a desafiar, a retar a un sistema, a un Estado, a un gobierno, a un ejército, a una policía, a un sistema judicial, a la historia y al destino, con la juventud y la furia que provoca ser olvidados.

Padres y madres de familia, casadas y solteras, de entre 30 y 40 años, que crecieron en la resistencia y la rebeldía y aprendieron que, organizados, podían vivir dignamente. Son autoridades autónomas, promotores de salud y de educación, milicianas y milicianos, insurgentas e insurgentes, mandos organizativos locales, regionales, de zona y de Inter zona. Parte del todo que es la nueva dirección organizativa zapatista.

Otroas que encontraron, luchando, un lugar digno en la comunidad. Y con ese lugar, lograron respeto y admiración.

Jóvenas y jóvenes, de entre 12 y 20 años, que saben leer y escribir, manejan con soltura tecnologías que sus padres y madres ni soñaban, que incursionan en las artes haciendo obras de teatro, películas, pinturas, poesía, canto, bailables, traduciendo a esas lenguas peculiares que tienen las artes, sus vidas, sus historias, sus sueños, sus amores y sus desamores, su herencia, su lengua, su cultura, su ser comunidad, con el corazón roto apenas ayer, y de nuevo sano y completo hoy.

Niñas y niños, el fatídico “Comando Palomitas”, cuyo número varía dependiendo de si hay o no dulces a la hora de pasar revista, la niñez de todas las lenguas igualadas en el juego y la travesura, la risa infantil como vacuna contra todas las fronteras humanas.

Si nos referimos al calendario, hay ahí 5 generaciones. 6 si se cuenta la que ya viene en camino y se adivina en los vientres hinchados de jóvenes madres. Todas, todos, todoas de pueblos originarios. Todas, todos, todoas con la sangre de raíz maya palpitándoles en la mirada apenas visible por entre cubrebocas y pasamontañas.

Y todas, todoas, todos, no ocultando las lágrimas que les ruedan por mejillas de piel oscura, al imaginarse el dolor de quien es buscado. Porque el llorar por el dolor ajeno es de humanos cabales y no avergüenza, sino que enaltece. Porque ocultar el rostro no es ocultar los sentimientos.

Y esas lágrimas son también por José Miguel, y por otros, otras y …

author: Aline Melo
title: Organizações lançam carta defendendo projeto que regula mercados digitais
content:
A regulamentação dos mercados digitais no Brasil, os chamados

Marketplaces

, está em disputa. De um lado, empresas e organizações sociais lançam uma carta que defende a aprovação do Projeto de Lei 4.675/2025.

 A proposta cria regras para ampliar a transparência e fiscalizar a concorrência nesses ambientes, incluindo a atuação do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica, o Cade, criando uma superintendência específica para avaliar os negócios digitais. A carta deve ser divulgada nos próximos dias, após uma reunião convocada pelo Governo Federal, por meio da Secretaria de Comunicação Social da Presidência (Secom), com representantes desses grupos para alinhar estratégias para a aprovação do PL 4675.


Do outro lado da disputa, o projeto tem sido alvo do lobby das Big Techs, que o associa ao aumento do controle estatal sobre a internet.

 A estratégia reproduz argumentos utilizados em outras discussões sobre regulação no Brasil, como ocorreu durante a tramitação do PL das Fake News, e chama o projeto de “PL da censura”.


A proposta teve origem no Governo Federal, a partir de trabalhos do Ministério da Fazenda e do Conselho Administrativo de Defesa Econômica (Cade), e recebeu um substitutivo apresentado pelo deputado Aliel Machado (PV-PR) em agosto deste ano.


O argumento pela regulamentação dos mercados digitais


Na avaliação de Rafael Zanatta, diretor executivo da Data Privacy Brasil — uma das organizações envolvidas na carta em defesa do 4.675/2025 —,

a regulação pode beneficiar especialmente startups, desenvolvedores independentes, varejistas e empresas brasileiras que dependem de grandes plataformas para oferecer seus produtos e serviços.


“Esse PL está trazendo um ambiente digital mais competitivo, mais transparente, melhor para startups, melhor para desenvolvedores independentes, melhor para varejistas. E os únicos afetados aqui são empresas muito específicas”, afirma.


Um dos exemplos citados pelo diretor da Data Privacy é o controle da Apple sobre a loja de aplicativos do sistema iOS e as restrições impostas a desenvolvedores quanto aos meios de pagamento. Para Zanatta, a possibilidade de utilizar alternativas, como o Pix, e de reduzir taxas de intermediação pode ampliar a concorrência e diminuir custos para empresas e consumidores.


Zanatta critica a repercussão de que a proposta reproduziria modelos autoritários de controle estatal. “O Partido Novo fala que esse seria um projeto do governo para aumentar poderes, instituir censura e controle na vida do cidadão. Esse projeto não tem nada a ver com moderação de conteúdo, não tem nada a ver com controlar a vida das pessoas. Estão falando que o PL é inspirado nas ‘ditaduras’ da China e Cuba”, afirma.


Na realidade, a proposta brasileira tem como referência experiências regulatórias adotadas em democracias europeias, especialmente o Digital Markets Act (DMA), legislação da União Europeia em vigor desde 2023. A norma estabelece obrigações para grandes plataformas digitais classificadas como controladoras de acesso (gatekeepers), com o objetivo de tornar os mercados digitais mais competitivos e impedir práticas comerciais consideradas desleais. Entre as regras estão a proibição de favorecer serviços próprios em detrimento de concorrentes e a possibilidade de desenvolvedores utilizarem sistemas de pagamento alternativos nas lojas de aplicativos.


O projeto brasileiro também prevê instrumentos de atuação preventiva do Cade sobre grandes grupos econômicos, com obrigações específicas voltadas à proteção da concorrência. Embora existam diferenças entre os dois modelos, ambos tratam da regulação econômica de mercados digitais e da limitação do poder de grandes plataformas, não do controle sobre conteúdos ou opiniões publicados por usuários.


“O PL 4675 protege o Pix, protege infraestruturas públicas digitais e protege que empresas brasileiras possam surgir e crescer sem serem limadas desse processo, ou mesmo compradas”, acrescenta.


Segundo Zanatta, o projeto também daria ao Cade instrumentos para impedir ou reverter operações de fusão e aquisição que possam prejudicar a concorrência, inclusive quando grandes grupos econômicos tentarem comprar empresas brasileiras emergentes. Ele cita como exemplos hipotéticos uma eventual aquisição do Jusbrasil pelo Google ou da Magazine Luiza pela Amazon.


Além da Data Privacy Brasil, participaram da articulação da carta organizações como Artigo 19, Ctrl+Z e Instituto Brasileiro de Defesa do Consumidor (Idec), e …

author: Francesco Rota
title: FILM AFRICA Press Release
content:
The Royal African Society Announces the Successful Conclusion of the 2026 Film Africa Festival


London, United Kingdom,  9th November 2026


The Royal African Society is delighted to announce the successful conclusion of its 125

th

 Anniversary edition of Film Africa Festival which took place from 23 October to 1 November.

 Now in its 13

th

 year, Film Africa celebrated the richness, diversity, and creativity of African cinema and brought together audiences, filmmakers, industry professionals, and supporters for an inspiring celebration of African storytelling. The festival screened 38 films from 30 African countries, and hosted two symposia, across 11 venues in London, Sheffield, Bristol, and Plymouth.


The festival provided a vibrant platform for African filmmakers to share compelling stories, highlighted diverse perspectives, and engaged audiences through the power of film. This year’s Film Africa Festival provided a special focus on

 The Role of African Women in Cinema, and the Importance of Sustainable Finance, Intellectual Property and Digital Technology

for the future of African Cinema.


We are deeply grateful to everyone who contributed to making this year’s festival a memorable success. We extend our heartfelt appreciation to all our members, guests, and members of the public who attended screenings, participated in discussions, engaged with filmmakers, and supported the festival throughout its programme. Your enthusiasm, curiosity, and commitment to African cinema were central to the festival’s success.


We are particularly appreciative of our 125

th

 Anniversary sponsors:


Platinum category:

 Afreximbank / CANEX and Nuvion


Gold category:

 Africa Finance Corporation and Oando


Bronze category:

 DLA Piper, Omenaa Foundation, Nigerian Exchange Group, Oakwood Green Africa, and Air Peace.


We also thank the filmmakers, directors, producers, our industry partners, venues, volunteers, and the wider creative community for their invaluable contributions and continued support.


Film Africa remains committed to celebrating African cinema, amplifying African voices, and creating opportunities for cultural exchange and meaningful dialogue through film. The 2026 festival has once again demonstrated the power of cinema to connect communities, inspire conversations, and deepen understanding of the many stories shaping the African continent and its diaspora.


We look forward to welcoming audiences back for future editions, and continuing to celebrate the extraordinary talent and creativity of African filmmakers. To join us and to partake in our future events, please see:

https://royalafricansociety.org/events/


For further partnership opportunities, kindly send us an email to:

ras_director@soas.ac.uk

.

author: Qassam Muaddi
title: Palestinian Opinions Are Divided as Elections Are Now Postponed Until 2027
content:
Although some in Gaza welcomed the prospect of elections, many are looking for solutions to more urgent problems.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On October 10, Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas issued a presidential decree postponing the legislative and presidential elections from November 2026, the original scheduled date, until September 2027.

Amid obstacles imposed by the Israeli occupation, the postponement was justified by a need to create appropriate political, security, and on-the-ground conditions for free, fair, and inclusive elections.

According to the official Palestinian news agency WAFA, the decree aims to allow for comprehensive national dialogue to strengthen Palestinian unity, preserve Palestinian territory, safeguard the political system, address challenges that the electoral process is facing, and ensure the participation of Palestinians in Jerusalem, the West Bank, and the Gaza Strip while protecting their political and constitutional rights.

While some expected the postponement, in light of the cancellation of Palestinian elections in 2021, it nevertheless came as a surprise to observers.

In the Gaza Strip, reactions to the decision have been divided. Some consider it to be in the national interest, arguing that the current conditions in Gaza do not permit elections. Others believe that postponing the vote, after more than 20 years without elections, undermines the national democratic process and marginalizes the role of Gaza’s residents in determining their political future.

Fadi al-Sheikh Youssef, head of a youth-led electoral list that had been preparing to contest the elections, described the postponement as an unjust and direct denial of the Palestinian people’s democratic right.

“The elections should have continued after nearly 20 years of freezing the democratic process in Palestine,” he said. “If the Israeli occupation has imposed obstacles, the elections should have become a political battle fought by all parties against the occupation. This electoral process should have been a new opportunity to expose the occupation to the world and reveal the falsity of its claims about democratic practices and its supposed respect for freedom of expression and Palestinians’ right to political participation.”

He added that the postponement appeared to reflect an agreement among political parties to reproduce the same political landscape.

“Unfortunately, we see this postponement as part of an effort by the parties to recreate the same political scene. Even the justification of national consensus does not reflect the real wishes of the Palestinian people. If there had truly been national consensus, it should have been achieved over the past 20 years, not now, as the political landscape is being reshaped through a democratic process,” he said.

Al-Sheikh Youssef described the decision as deeply unjust and ill-suited to the current political landscape, arguing that it excluded new groups and political actors seeking to enter the arena and defend what remains of people’s dignity.

In a statement, Hamas said it viewed the decision to postpone the elections until next year as a step in the right direction, given the absence of the political, security, and on-the-ground conditions necessary for free and fair elections throughout the occupied Palestinian territories, including Jerusalem.

Hamas said the postponement should lead to comprehensive, serious and productive national dialogue. It also expressed its readiness to participate in discussions aimed at reaching clear and binding agreements for all parties, including mechanisms to reorganize Palestinian political institutions, particularly the Palestinian National Council and the Palestinian Legislative Council.

Furthermore, some Palestinian political analysts and academics offered a broader assessment of the political calculations behind the postponement and its potential consequences for the Palestinian political system.

Political analyst Adel Shadid told Mondoweiss that “despite the Palestinian demands and European pressure on the Palestinian Authority to hold elections, the PA are afraid of elections, because they know its officials know that there are real possibilities of losing, and despite that, I was surprised by the postponement of elections.”

title: Ücret artışı olmadan daha uzun çalışma dayatan Mercedes-Benz, Almanya'da yeni yatırımları durdurdu
content:
Mercedes-Benz, iş gücü maliyetlerini düşürmek için işçi temsilcileriyle yürüttüğü görüşmelerde ilerleme sağlanamaması üzerine Almanya’daki tesislerine yönelik yeni yatırımları durdurdu. Şirket yönetiminin, ülkedeki bazı fabrikaların kapatılmasını da değerlendirdiği belirtildi. İnsan Kaynakları Direktörü Britta Seeger, Reuters’ın gördüğü şirket içi söyleşide yakın zamanda anlaşma beklemediklerini ve hangi tesislerin mevcut maliyetlerle işletilebileceğini incelemeye başladıklarını söyledi.

Görüşmelerde haftalık çalışma süresinin ücret artışı olmadan 35 saatten 40 saate çıkarılması gündeme geldi. Yönetim ayrıca kâr payı, tatil ve Noel ödemeleri gibi ek ödemeleri de görüşmeye açmak istiyor. Çalışan temsilcileri ve IG Metall sendikası ise 35 saatlik çalışma haftasını temel bir kazanım olarak görüyor ve bu dayatmaları reddediyor.

Üretim Direktörü Michael Schiebe, maliyetler düşürülemezse Almanya’da bir otomobil montaj fabrikası ile bir parça üretim tesisinin kapanabileceğini daha önce belirtmişti. Şirketin Sindelfingen, Rastatt ve Bremen’de montaj fabrikaları bulunuyor. Schiebe, anlaşma sağlanamazsa yeni modellerin yalnızca yurt dışında üretileceğini söyledi.

Schiebe’ye göre Almanya’daki üretim tesislerinde saatlik iş gücü maliyeti, bazı durumlarda Doğu Avrupa’daki tesislerin beş katına ulaşıyor. Macaristan’daki fabrikasını genişleten şirket, gümrük vergilerini, zayıflayan talebi, fiyat baskısını ve özellikle Çinli üreticilerin rekabetini de gerekçe gösteriyor. Mercedes-Benz’in binek otomobil biriminin satış kârlılığı ocak-eylül döneminde yüzde 3,3’e geriledi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Jillian Kestler-D’Amours
title: Refugee Groups Sue to Stop Canada From Handing Over Asylum Seekers to ICE
content:
The lawsuit says handing asylum seekers over to the abuse-perpetrating US is a violation of Canada’s constitution.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Canada is violating its own constitution by turning asylum seekers away at the border with the United States, where they face serious threats under U.S. President Donald Trump, Canadian legal experts and rights advocates say.

Amnesty International Canada, the Canadian Council for Refugees, and the Canadian Council of Churches are in court this week to challenge a decades-old pact that allows Canadian officials to summarily send most refugees back at the U.S. border.

People rallied in Toronto and Montreal, the two largest cities in Canada, on Monday to show support for the case and call on the Canadian government to rip up the Safe Third Country Agreement (STCA).

In Montreal, dozens of protesters held posters that read, “Canada must protect, not send back” and “Humanity has no borders.”

“If Canadians don’t feel safe in the United States, we can be sure that refugees aren’t safe either,” Lauren Lallemand, co-executive director of the Canadian Council for Refugees, told the crowd.

“The asylum system in the U.S. is failing, and those who flee in search of safety deserve to be protected.”

The Safe Third Country Agreement, which came into force in 2004, is premised on the idea that Canada and the U.S. each offer people access to a robust refugee protection system.

In practice, it means that asylum seekers can seek protection in the first country they arrive in, but not both: someone in the U.S. cannot apply for asylum in Canada, or vice versa.

For years, the restriction applied to asylum claims made at official crossings along the border.

But if people entered Canada irregularly between ports of entry (via farmers’ fields or rural roads, for example), they could circumvent the pact — and as Trump began to crack down on immigration during his first term, tens of thousands of people made dangerous crossings into Canada to request protection.

In 2023, amid public and political pressure to crack down on immigration, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau and President Joe Biden closed the loophole, extending the Safe Third Country Agreement to the entire 5,525-mile border.

Now, only people who meet specific conditions — such as unaccompanied minors or individuals with relatives who are already in Canada — are exempt from being turned away under the Safe Third Country Agreement.

The lawsuit being heard in Federal Court in Toronto this week argues that the Safe Third Country Agreement violates equality rights under Section 15 of Canada’s constitution, known as the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms.

According to the complainants, that’s because the pact disproportionately harms racialized asylum seekers, including women fleeing gender-based violence, children, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

Julia Sande, a lawyer at Amnesty International Canada, explained that Section 15 applies to everyone who is physically in the country, including refugee claimants.

“Canada cannot deport people to face torture, harm [and] persecution in another country,” she said. “It would be a violation of their Charter rights, even if it’s another country doing the harm, because it’s Canada’s decision to send them out … [and] to put them in [harm’s way] when harm is reasonably foreseeable.”

While conditions for asylum seekers and refugees in the U.S. have been concerning for a long time, Sande said the situation has deteriorated dramatically under the administration of U.S. President Donald Trump.

She pointed to the expansion of immigration detention as one example. “Things are obviously extremely urgent and extremely harmful,” she said.

“We all act in horror at what’s unfolding in the United States. You hear Canadian citizens talking about being afraid to go there, being afraid of ICE.”

“We all act in horror at what’s unfolding in the United States. You hear Canadian citizens talking about being afraid to go there, being afraid of ICE,” she told Truthout.

“I have a hard time believing that you could find anyone here who would say, ‘Yeah I’d really like my government to hand a child over to ICE to be thrown in detention … and ultimately sent back to a country where they fled gang violence.’”

author: The Canadian Press
title: Shelter-in-place advisory issued near Squamish, B.C., due to flooding from heavy rain
content:
A shelter-in-place advisory has been issued north of Vancouver, where roads have flooded due to dam run-off triggered by storms that have drenched parts of southern British Columbia with more than 300 millimetres of rain in 48 hours.


The rains that are forecast to ease Thursday before a weaker system arrives Friday have also forced evacuation orders for parts of Vancouver Island, the Lil’wat First Nation in the central Interior, and parts of the Village of Pemberton, about 150 kilometres north of Vancouver.


The entire Village of Pemberton is under an evacuation alert, while the District of Squamish about 90 kilometres to the south has told residents of Paradise Valley to shelter in place after dam discharge swamped local roads.


British Columbia’s emergency information system says residents in areas including Sunwolf Lodge and Cheekye Ranch should stay indoors if they can.


The District of Squamish says in a statement that the spill level from the Cheakamus Dam at Daisy Lake peaked at approximately 5 a.m. and was expected to decrease slowly throughout the day.


The district says the spill level decrease was to create room in the reservoir for another upcoming storm, as well as to eventually allow for roads to be re-opened.


It says a rainfall warning ended this morning and that heavy rain is no longer expected through Friday.


It also says river levels are expected to peak Thursday and begin to drop as rainfall from the storm works its way through the river system.


A string of weather systems has slammed southwestern B.C since last week, with 306 millimetres of rain falling at Port Mellon in the Howe Sound region since Tuesday.


The Village of Pemberton’s evacuation order covers properties on Airport Road, including the community’s airport, wastewater treatment facility, wildland fire management base and a public golf course due to flooding and “high-risk river levels.”


The B.C. Ministry of Transportation’s DriveBC website says Highway 99 east of Pemberton has been shut in both directions.


The Lilʼwat Nation has also expanded an evacuation order and alert for the area from Kwetsa7 along the Lillooet River corridor to Lillooet Lake.


Elsewhere, the Strathcona Regional District issued a water conservation notice for the village of Sayward on the northeast coast of Vancouver Island, as high flows in Newcastle Creek led to extra sediment in the water.


An evacuation order due to flooding and landslide risks remains in place for about 30 properties in the village of Zeballos on northwest Vancouver Island.


While rains have eased in parts of the province including Metro Vancouver, orange rainfall warnings remain in place for west and inland Vancouver Island, indicating severe storms that are likely to cause significant damage and disruption.


“A strong frontal system over the area will weaken today. Rain will continue to ease as the front weakens,” Environment Canada said Thursday.


A less-severe yellow rainfall warning is active for the Sunshine Coast and parts of east Vancouver Island.


Environment Canada says several locations reported more than 100 millimetres of rain in the last 48 hours, including Kennedy Lake on Vancouver Island (248 mm), Port Alberni (123 mm), Porteau Cove on the Sea to Sky Highway (140 mm), Whistler (138 mm), and Squamish (134 mm).

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik’s new sex-education curriculum takes shape
content:
Nunavik’s sexuality education pilot project will initially cover four subjects, including healthy relationships, pregnancy, sexually transmitted infections and contraception.


Kativik Ilisarniliriniq — Nunavik’s school board — and the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services

rolled out the curriculum

 this month in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq.


The program is intended for students from kindergarten to Grade 11 (Secondary V), with lessons adapted to their ages and stages of development.


At a Nov. 4 parent information session in Kuujjuaq, school commissioner Eva Kauki-Gordon said age appropriateness had been her main concern but after reviewing the material, she was satisfied that lessons would differ between grade levels.


Kauki-Gordon said she hopes the program will help young people feel more comfortable discussing their bodies and sexual health.


Growing up, she said, sexuality and puberty were rarely discussed at home. She recalled finding it difficult to speak to her mother about getting her first period.


“I think this would help for them to be more open,” she said of students.


Five parents attended the Kuujjuaq information session. Kauki-Gordon encouraged more families to get involved in their children’s education.


“Be involved in the education that is being given,” she said. “You have [a] responsibility for your child.”


The health board developed the curriculum after consulting health-care professionals, parents, teachers and people of different ages across Nunavik.


Teaching materials or lesson plans won’t be released yet because the content may change based on findings from the pilot project.


“What is covered in kindergarten levels is very surface-level information, compared to other primary grades,” Andreas Schaffhauser-Carpentier, a media liaison with the health board, said in a written response to Nunatsiaq News.


Secondary students will also discuss topics that are more relevant to address after puberty.


The pilot project does not cover every subject planned for what will eventually become the full curriculum. Topics such as body image and a broader understanding of sexuality will be added later. The health board said the wider program will also address consent, bodily autonomy, personal boundaries and sexual abuse prevention.


The final curriculum will include a parental component with cue cards sent home after each module to explain what students learned and suggest ways families can discuss the subjects together.


“Our goal is to give students a range of options and objective information on sexual education,” Schaffhauser-Carpentier said.


The pilot runs next week at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq, following sessions that were held in the first week of November at Jaanimmarik and Pitakallak schools in Kuujjuaq.


Feedback from the pilot will help the two organizations revise the curriculum before considering a wider rollout across the region’s schools.

title: Bodrum Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri: HABAŞ’ta yaşanan kaza değil iş cinayeti
content:
Antalya – İzmir Aliağa HABAŞ Demir Çelik Fabrikası’nda meydana gelen patlamada 19 işçinin hayatını kaybetmesi ve en az 15 işçinin yaralanması sonrası Bodrum Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri, basın açıklaması ve eylem yaptı. Açıklamada, “Üretim zorlaması, taşeronlaştırma ve denetimsizlik nedeniyle yaşanan bu facia bir kaza değil, göz gör e göre gelen bir iş cinayetidir” diyerek yaşanan işçi ölümlerine tepki gösterildi.

Bodrum Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri adına Belediye meydanında açıklamayı yapan Hakkı İlbeyi, aynı fabrikada son 10 yılda en az 7 işçinin daha hayatını kaybetmiş olmasının, ihmallerin sistematik hale geldiğini göstergesi olduğunu belirterek, “üretimin büyük ölçüde taşeron firmalar üzerinden yürütülmesi, bakım çalışmaları sırasında dahi üretimin durdurulmaması ve makine ile ekipmanların denetlenmemesi işçilerin yaşam hakkını hiçe saymaktır” dedi.

HABAŞ’taki güvencesiz ve denetimsiz çalışma düzeninin, başta Bodrum olmak üzere tüm Muğla genelinde de hüküm sürdüğünü belirten İlbeyi, “Bodrum’daki şantiyelerde, otellerde ve turizm işletmelerinde; Muğla genelindeki Yeniköy, Kemerköy ve Yatağan termik santralleri ile maden ve mermer ocaklarında işçiler kadrolu, taşeron ve yüklenici ayrımıyla ağır koşullarda çalıştırılmaktadır. İş güvenliği önlemlerinin maliyet unsuru olarak görüldüğü bu düzen devam ettiği sürece, bölgemizde de benzer faciaların yaşanması kaçınılmazdır” diye konuştu.

Emek Partisi Bodrum ilçe örgütü de eylem sonrası dağıttığı bildiride yaşanan işçi ölümleri, işçi cinayetlerine değinerek “Bodrum’daki inşaat ve turizm alanları başta olmak üzere Muğla’daki tüm termik santrallerde, maden ve mermer ocaklarında derhal gerçek bir denetimin yapılması ve denetim sonuçlarının şeffaf biçimde kamuoyuyla paylaşılması” çağrısı yaptı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Doug Bock Clark
title: A Tool Built by Election Deniers Said These Voters Were Dead — They Aren’t
content:
After the midterm, a GOP election board member in Georgia challenged dozens of ballots using a controversial data tool.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Ahead of the midterms, conservative election activists discussed plans to wield a powerful new weapon in the war against fraud: a data tool built by one of their own that could identify suspicious voters and help with contesting their ballots.

The system was put to the test this week in Forsyth County, Georgia, where a member of the county’s election board provided other officials with what he suggested was evidence of wrongdoing: four allegedly dead voters.

But it turns out all four are alive and well, ProPublica determined. The board rejected the attempt to challenge their ballots.

The effort, though, shows that even after last week’s blue wave, those who believe the 2020 election was stolen have continued to relentlessly search for ways to contest Republican losses. In Georgia, Democrats swept statewide offices.

The board member who initiated the Forsyth County challenge, Max Clavijo, is a member of the Election Integrity Network, a group led by conservative lawyer Cleta Mitchell that works to restrict voting and tighten election laws and rules. Mitchell worked closely with Donald Trump in his attempt to overturn his defeat in the 2020 election and, since he retook the presidency, has been central to his push to assert greater federal control over voting.

In the run-up to the midterms, on right-wing media and on private organizing calls, EIN participants outlined plans to search voter rolls with a software tool known as ELLY’s Election Monitor and contest ballots the tool deemed suspicious.

ELLY was developed by EIN member Rick Richards. It aggregates public data from state voter files, federal change-of-address records, tax documents, obituaries, property websites like Zillow and other sources. In Georgia, State Election Board members and top staffers have urged counties to use the tool to search their voter rolls for signs of fraud.

Richards talked about ELLY’s national potential on a podcast in late September, on which right-wing media personalities and activists touted its capacity to help GOP candidates contest their defeats. “We can prove the fraud that’s gone on in every state,” one commentator said. “This data will be able to set up challenges to those who lose.”

The following month, on a private call with EIN members and other conservative activists, Richards promised to provide data from more than 3,000 counties to “citizen monitors” and GOP candidates to try to prove fraud, according to a recording reviewed by ProPublica.

In an interview, Richards told ProPublica that he gave Clavijo data on Forsyth County at Clavijo’s request. He said in a subsequent email that their actions were meant to inform the board and remain confidential. Clavijo didn’t respond to questions from ProPublica.

Richards refused to answer questions about whether Clavijo’s effort was part of a wider EIN campaign to contest votes cast in the midterms.

“That’s irrelevant,” he said. “The data is the data. People can use it for what they want to.”

Mitchell, EIN’s leader, didn’t respond to questions about the group’s plans related to ELLY, either in Georgia or nationally.

In the months since some on Georgia’s State Election Board started promoting ELLY’s use, its accuracy has been much debated. The tool doesn’t have access to personal identifiers such as voters’ Social Security or driver’s license numbers or full dates of birth, which increases the potential for mismatches involving people with the same names.

Voting rights groups have called ELLY error-prone. The Cherokee County election director complained to the state board after the tool falsely flagged a county board member’s spouse as dead.

State Election Board members and Richards have defended ELLY. Accusations that the data is unreliable were “horse hockey,” Richards told ProPublica, explaining this was “a Southern colloquialism for B.S.”

Late last week, according to several people familiar with the matter, Clavijo circulated documents to board members and Forsyth County’s election director. Based on data from ELLY, Clavijo questioned whether the names of more than 22,000 people on the county’s voter roll were correct and disputed the eligibility of 69 voters. In addition to four he claimed were deceased, he alleged others had moved out of the …

title: CHP seçmeni AKP'ye MHP seçmeninden çok güveniyor
content: Yöneylem Sosyal Araştırmalar Merkezi’nin Türkiye Siyaset Paneli Ekim 2026 araştırması, seçmenlerin fon krizine yaklaşımını, ülke yönetimine ilişkin değerlendirmelerini ve oy tercihlerindeki değişimi ortaya koydu. Araştırma, 21–28 Ekim 2026 tarihlerinde 81 il ve 12 istatistiki bölgede 2 bin 400 panelistle bilgisayar destekli telefon görüşmesi (CATI) yöntemiyle gerçekleştirildi. Yöneylem, araştırmanın Türkiye geneli sonuçları için yüzde 95 güven düzeyinde hata payını ±2 yüzde puan olarak açıkladı.Bulgular, bazı AKP’li siyasetçilerin fon krizinden haksız kazanç sağladığı iddialarını inandırıcı bulanların, AKP ve MHP seçmenleri arasında da önemli bir kesim oluşturduğunu gösteriyor. Araştırmaya katılanların yüzde 50,6’sı fon kriziyle ilgili gelişmeleri “yakından”, yüzde 24,7’si “biraz” takip ettiğini belirtti. Böylece gelişmeleri takip edenlerin toplamı yüzde 75,3 oldu. Katılımcıların yüzde 12,6’sı krizi hiç duymadığını, yüzde 11,6’sı ise yalnızca duyduğunu söyledi. Yüzde 0,5’lik kesim soruyu yanıtsız bıraktı. Fon krizini takip etme oranı parti tercihlerine göre farklılaştı. Gelişmeleri biraz veya yakından takip edenlerin toplamı İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 95,9, Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 91,3, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 86,8 ve DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 86,3 olarak ölçüldü. Aynı oran AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 59,2, CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 57 oldu Bazı AKP’li siyasetçilerin fon krizinden haksız kazanç sağladığı iddialarını katılımcıların yüzde 45,4’ü “çok inandırıcı”, yüzde 26,4’ü “inandırıcı” buldu. İddiaları inandırıcı bulanların toplamı yüzde 71,8’e ulaşırken, yüzde 9,6’lık kesim “pek inandırıcı değil” veya “hiç inandırıcı değil” yanıtını verdi. Katılımcıların yüzde 9’u değerlendirme yapacak kadar bilgisi olmadığını belirtti. Söz konusu iddiaları inandırıcı veya çok inandırıcı bulanların oranı AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 47,6, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 74,6 oldu. Bu oran Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 90,7, İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 91 ve DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 88,5 olarak kaydedildi. CHP seçmenlerinde ise yüzde 62,4’te kaldı. Değerlendirme yapacak kadar bilgisi olmadığını söyleyenlerin oranı CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 16,5, AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 14,5 olarak ölçüldü. “Sizce Türkiye nasıl yönetilmektedir?” sorusuna katılımcıların yüzde 55,7’si “kötü yönetilmektedir” yanıtını verdi. Ülkenin iyi yönetildiğini düşünenlerin oranı yüzde 21,5 olurken, yüzde 21,8’lik kesim “ne iyi ne kötü yönetilmektedir” seçeneğini işaretledi. Katılımcıların yüzde 1’i ise bilmediğini belirtti. Türkiye’nin iyi yönetildiğini söyleyenlerin oranı AKP seçmenlerinde yüzde 65, MHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 49,6 oldu. Kötü yönetildiğini düşünenlerin oranı ise Yeni Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 89,2, İYİ Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 87,8, DEM Parti seçmenlerinde yüzde 87,1 ve CHP seçmenlerinde yüzde 73,6’ya ulaştı. AKP seçmenlerinin yüzde 8,3’ü ve MHP seçmenlerinin yüzde 10,7’si de ülkenin kötü yönetildiğini belirtti. Katılımcıların yüzde 16’sı son bir ayda oy vermeyi düşündüğü partiyi değiştirdiğini, yüzde 83,2’si ise tercihinin değişmediğini söyledi. Tercihini değiştirenlerin yüzde 31,1’i önceki ay AKP’ye, yüzde 26,1’i CHP’ye, yüzde 7,6’sı Yeni Parti’ye ve yüzde 6,7’si MHP’ye oy vermeyi düşündüğünü belirtti. Bu dağılım, tercih değiştiren grubun önceki yönelimini gösteriyor; partilerin kendi seçmenleri içindeki kayıp oranlarını veya net oy değişimini ortaya koymuyor. Oy tercihini değiştirme gerekçelerinde “ekonomi, geçim ve istihdam” yüzde 21,5 ile ilk sırada yer aldı. Bunu yüzde 11,7 ile “yolsuzluk, fon krizi ve usulsüzlük”, yüzde 10,3 ile “parti içi gelişmeler, liderlik ve kayyım”, yüzde 9,1 ile “parti politikaları, söylemler ve tutumlar” izledi. Fon krizi diğer iki konuyla aynı başlıkta değerlendirildiği için, yalnızca bu krizin tercih değişimindeki payı verilerden ayrıştırılamıyor. Hane içindeki siyasi tercihlere ilişkin soruda katılımcıların yüzde 57,9’u herkesin aynı partiye oy vermeyi düşündüğünü söyledi. Yüzde 16,6’sı hanede farklı partileri tercih edenlerin bulunduğunu, yüzde 3,6’sı ise tercihi belli olanların yanında kararsız veya oy kullanmayı düşünmeyen kişilerin de yaşadığını belirtti. Hanedeki hiç kimsenin tercihinin belli olmadığını söyleyenlerin oranı yüzde 8,7, hiçbirinin oy kullanmayı düşünmediğini belirtenlerin oranı yüzde 5,5 oldu. Yüzde 7,7’lik kesim diğer hane üyelerinin tercihini bilmediğini söyledi. author: Daron Letts
title: Nunavut earns second-highest score from leading credit rating agency
content:
The Government of Nunavut received the second-highest possible credit score from Moody’s Ratings, a leading New York-based international credit rating agency.


The Aa1 rating was granted because the Canadian government financially backs the territory, according to the company’s report.


“This rating is an important milestone for Nunavut and reflects the strength of our financial position,” said Premier John Main, who is also finance minister, in a news release issued Monday.

“It recognizes our government’s responsible financial management and the stability provided by our relationship with the Government of Canada.”


The company’s ratings system ranges from Aaa, the highest, to C, the lowest. 


Although Nunavut’s own-source revenue was only 17 per cent of total revenue in 2025-26, reflecting a narrow tax base due to its small population, the report concluded that there is “a high likelihood that the Government of Canada would provide extraordinary support should Nunavut face acute liquidity stress.”


Federal transfers account for approximately 80 per cent of the territory’s revenue, which bridges the gap between high expenditure needs and limited revenue capacity, the report states.


From 2018 through 2025, the government’s annual credit ratings were provided by Chicago-based DBRS Morningstar.


In 2025, that agency awarded the territory a rating of “AA stable trend,” which was an upgrade from the 2024 rating of “AA (low) stable trend.”


Both those scores fall within the second-highest level of the company’s rating structure.


Prior to that, Nunavut maintained an Aa1 rating from Moody’s Ratings from 2012 through 2017, according to the Moody’s Ratings website.

author: Chris Walker
title: House Democrats Vow to Investigate White House Despite Trump Admin Threats
content:
The counsel to the president claimed that recent statements by Democrats “may cross the line into blatant criminality.”

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The White House has sent a threatening letter to House Democrats, warning that lawmakers could face repercussions if they open investigations into the Trump administration once they take control of Congress.

The letter, sent by Will Scharf in his official role as counsel to the president, was delivered just days after President Donald Trump demanded investigations into Democrats who stated that they were planning inquiries into the administration in the wake of the “blue wave” in this month’s midterm elections. Trump falsely called those statements “illegal” and “criminal.”

Scharf’s letter, first revealed by Punchbowl News, was sent to Rep. Robert Garcia (D-California) on Monday, according to the date on the letter, though the House Oversight Committee said midweek that it had not yet received an actual copy of the document. Garcia, currently the ranking member of the committee, is likely to become its chair after Democrats take control of the House in January.

Citing several Election Night social media posts by Democrats — including comments from Garcia urging the administration to “lawyer up” — Scharf claimed that there are “foundational” constitutional limits “on congressional investigations and subpoenas,” and accused incoming Democrats of having personal reasons for planning inquiries into the White House.

“We are monitoring the abusive and capricious threats that are now proliferating from Democrat legislators who seek to abuse the legislative process to intimidate and to interfere with the lawful functioning of government,” Scharf said.

The comments by Democrats “may cross the line into blatant criminality,” Scharf added, though he provided no basis for that claim.

The letter is highly unusual — while past presidents have criticized subpoenas and inquiries into their actions, the ability of the House Oversight Committee to conduct such investigations has long been considered a basic function of its work, and Supreme Court precedent has protected those powers. The statements by both Scharf and Trump are also hypocritical, given that Trump’s predecessor, former President Joe Biden, faced investigations by Republicans into his executive branch actions, including into his family members.

Garcia suggested that the letter indicates the administration has “something to hide.” He added:

The Trump administration continues to weaponize the government with threats of unconstitutional attacks on Congress. … [We] will not be deterred by baseless threats from a weaponized DOJ or from the president’s lawyers.

House Democratic leader Rep. Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York), who is poised to become the next Speaker of the House, also criticized Scharf’s letter, describing it as “outrageous” and “factually inaccurate…in terms of the Constitution.”

Peter M. Shane, constitutional legal scholar and adjunct professor at NYU School of Law, agreed that the letter contained false claims about the limits of congressional oversight.

“Our Constitution protects legislators from the threat of criminal prosecution while performing official duties as an essential bulwark to repel executive overreach and defend checks and balances,” Shane told The New York Times. “Congressional oversight and the issuance of subpoenas by definition cannot be the focus of legitimate criminal prosecution. It may be that an occasional subpoena may be quashed as outside the committee’s jurisdiction or for some other reason, but that is not a criminal offense.”

Donations are down for Truthout at a time when media is under immense pressure. Google’s AI search has driven our traffic down by 15 percent, Trump is arresting journalists, and many independent media organizations face heartbreaking cutbacks and closures.

At the same time, movement media is vital in the fight against Trump’s authoritarian reign. Our mandate to tell the truth, share strategies for resistance, and speak against fascism is ever more urgent in this deluge of political censorship and misinformation. Yet, we are struggling to meet our publishing costs when our work is so urgently needed.

We are fundraising right now for those basic operating expenses — we need $44,000 in the next 7 days. If you can support Truthout …

title: DEM Party emphasises priority tasks of new period
content:
The DEM Party Council began its second meeting following the congress by commemorating Tuncer Sağlam and Nesrin Aslan.


According to the final statement, the meeting included a comprehensive assessment of political, economic and social developments in Turkey, the Middle East and the world.


The statement said that, guided by the political vision set out at the congress and an awareness of its historical responsibilities, the Council had reached the following conclusions in order to determine the course of struggle for the period ahead:


Solidarity is our fundamental principle


1. The world is going through a period in which people's aspirations for peace, equality, freedom and democracy are confronting governments' policies of war, violence and hegemony. In response to the poverty, unemployment and inequality deepened by the capitalist system, youth, labour and popular movements stretching from France to Serbia and from Latin America to Europe are demonstrating the possibilities of a democratic and egalitarian way of life. Solidarity with struggles against exploitation, oppression, discrimination and lawlessness is our fundamental principle.


In the Middle East, policies of war directed against Iran, conflicts extending from Palestine to Lebanon and from Syria to Yemen, and efforts to establish regional alliances threaten the will and democratic future of the peoples of the region. Rather than becoming part of these policies, Turkey should assume responsibility for regional peace, equality among peoples and democratic solutions. We oppose the government's orientation towards the Mecca Pact, the Badr Agreement and its new relationships with regional powers, as these carry the risk of aligning Turkey with policies of war and hegemony.


The future of a multilingual, multi-faith and multicultural Middle East cannot be built through military alliances and sectarian policies, but through the equality and free will of its peoples. Recognition of the national, cultural and democratic rights of all peoples in the region is indispensable.


Kurda must come together on common ground


2. Overcoming political divisions within the Kurdistan Regional Government and bringing Kurdish political forces together is of historic importance for the unity of the Kurdish people, their shared future and the protection of their achievements. Political differences must not be allowed to weaken the people's collective will. We call on all Kurdish political forces to overcome their divisions through dialogue and come together on common ground for the unity of the Kurdish people.


Political and legal steps must be taken in the second phase of the process


3. The Peace and Democratic Society Process represents a historic opportunity for Turkey's democratic future. For developments aimed at ending conflict and violence as methods of resolving disputes to lead to lasting peace, democratic political channels must be expanded and all sections of society must be able to participate. The process concerns the shared future of society as a whole, not merely the parties involved, and also places responsibility on pro-democracy forces.


Political and legal steps for the second phase must be taken without delay. It is essential to implement the requirements of the legislation adopted by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey (TBMM), establish legal safeguards suited to the needs of the process, and resolve fundamental issues, particularly the right to hope and the status of Mr Abdullah Öcalan.


Ending the appointment of trustees in place of elected local authorities, recognising the will of the people, implementing the rulings of the Constitutional Court (AYM) and the European Court of Human Rights (ECHR), and guaranteeing the life and health rights of sick prisoners are indispensable requirements for democratisation.


Peace is not simply the silencing of weapons; it means confronting the truth, establishing equal citizenship, securing rights and freedoms, ensuring justice and building a democratic society. A democratic and peaceful resolution of the Kurdish question is one of the fundamental conditions for Turkey's transformation into a democratic and social republic. Our party remains determined to maintain its constructive and responsible approach in order to ensure the success of this historic opportunity.


Democratic forces must preserve platforms for joint struggle

title: Ayşe Berktay: Women's direct participation is essential to peace
content:
Writer Ayşe Berktay, who participated in peace initiatives organized by women during previous resolution processes and met with women in many cities, spoke to ANF about the Peace and Democratic Society Process and the role women should play in it.


Ayşe Berktay recalled the work carried out by women's movements during the 2013–2015 resolution process, stressing that women should not merely support peace but must also be directly involved in decision-making mechanisms.


Ayşe Berktay emphasized the importance of building social support for peace, stating that the process cannot be reduced to negotiations between political actors. She stressed that the Kurdish freedom movement, particularly women, would not allow such an approach and said that women's organized will must be brought to the forefront to achieve a democratic solution.


'Women must participate as decision-makers at every stage of peace processes'


Ayşe Berktay stated that the 2013–2015 resolution process did not begin suddenly and should be understood as part of the search for a political solution to the Kurdish question that emerged in 2009.


She said that efforts to achieve peace could be traced further back to 2005 and even 1993, highlighting the importance of joint work between the Kurdish women's movement and feminist and socialist women from Turkey.


Ayşe Berktay said: "It is both possible and necessary to trace the process that emerged in July 2009 under the name 'Democratic Opening' further back to 2005 and, when viewed as a whole, as far back as 1993.


In the years around 2009, as the possibility of peace began to be felt, both the Kurdish women's movement and socialist and feminist women's movements in Turkey began coming together, holding discussions and organizing in solidarity against repression to spread the message, aspiration and language of peace.


The Democratic Free Women's Movement (DÖKH) inviting a large group of women to Amed (Diyarbakır) for discussions was critical in this regard. Ankara followed, then Berçelan-Taksim and the Peace Points. The Women's Initiative for Peace (BIKG) emerged from these joint efforts.


The Democratic Free Women's Movement was important in establishing a more structured platform for feminist and socialist women to meet, discuss, build relationships and work together.


These preparations formed the foundation and background for the activities carried out during the 2013–2015 process. Women examined peace experiences around the world and shared their findings with the public. The relationship between violence against women, militarism and war was addressed.


The need for women to participate as equal decision-makers at every stage of the peace process was constantly kept on the agenda. Women established various commissions and produced reports, activities and materials concerning different aspects of the process.


Following the Paris Massacre, there was a powerful collective commitment both to Sara, Rojbîn and Ronahî (Sakine Cansız, Fidan Doğan and Leyla Şaylemez, the three Kurdish women activists assassinated in Paris on 9 January 2013) and, through them, to the resolution process itself.”


'The importance of women's work became evident a decade ago'


Ayşe Berktay recalled that a woman representing the Kurdish women's movement joined the delegation when visits to Imralı began. She also stated that women from Turkey established the Women's Freedom Assembly (KÖM) to develop their collective voice and will.


Ayşe Berktay said that women's organizations prepared reports on the peace process through the commissions they established and carried out activities in different cities.


She said: "Efforts were made to establish an organized structure capable of bringing women's collective will to the negotiating table through commissions and reports. Throughout this process, both the Women's Initiative for Peace and the Women's Freedom Assembly worked tirelessly.


Women carried out work through monitoring commissions and truth commissions in Lice, Varto, Dersim, Suruç and along the Kobanê border. The importance and urgency of expanding this work became evident."


'

Women must participate in decision-making mechanisms'


Ayşe Berktay stated that raising the demand for peace and supporting the process were important but insufficient on their own. She stressed that women must participate directly in discussions about how peace will be built and in the mechanisms where decisions are made.
